title: IT-2 (neu nach PR #490) Grade-Snapshot: Dirty-State erfassen statt messen, plus das Emissionsvolumen
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-4bbbd233 (angelegt 2026-07-28 ~11:00), KONSOLIDIERT trg-10aa91e3 + trg-d190cc37. Grund fuer die Neufassung: PR #490 ist um 13:13 gelandet und hat vier Sechstel des alten Ankers geliefert oder widerlegt - wer den alten Text liest, baut Erledigtes nach und die ZURUECKGEZOGENE Loesung obendrein. GELIEFERT DURCH #490, NICHT NOCHMAL BAUEN: (a) lineage - ein benannter Nicht-Default-Branch heisst jetzt 'branch'; Ancestry entscheidet nur noch bei detached HEAD, das keinen Namen hat, aus dem sich schliessen liesse (deckt trg-ca4fc0e7 und Symptom A von trg-aea8c97e). (b) event_amended --fields kann Attribution und Score nicht mehr ueberlagern; die Verweigerung sitzt jetzt in diesem Zweig, an das Shape-Modul gekoppelt, damit die zwei Routen nicht driften (deckt trg-c97faa35). (c) die 18/18-Probe ist zurueckgezogen, die Entscheidung steht auf ihren zwei tragfaehigen Argumenten (deckt trg-465a2caf). (d) trg-1603000f ist TEILWEISE WIDERLEGT: die Behauptung, auf dem Default-Branch regeneriere nichts die Compliance, ist falsch - jeder PHASE_REPORTS-Eintrag emittiert, und der Orchestrator regeneriert pro Phase auf dem Default-Branch. OFFEN, TEIL 1 - DIE URSACHE (aus trg-10aa91e3): grade und score werden aus dem WORKING tree berechnet, lineage und base koennen nur aus COMMITTED state abgeleitet werden, und nichts versoehnt die beiden. Auf dem main-lineage-Pfad ist merge-base(HEAD,default) gleich HEAD, ein Pre-Commit-Regen stempelt also den Commit, den er noch nicht gemacht hat. LANDMINE: ein Dirty-Flag wurde dafuer GEBAUT und nach zwei Review-Runden VOR DEM COMMIT ZURUECKGEZOGEN. Warum die naheliegende Implementierung scheitert, gemessen: jeder automatische Produzent schreibt GETRACKTE Dateien, bevor der Snapshot emittiert wird, also liest eine Dirty-Messung zum Emit-Zeitpunkt true auf einem makellosen Baum - vier Faelle belegt (update_compliance, Run-Orchestrator, finalize_iterate, sbom/test-evidence-Emitter), einer end-to-end reproduziert mit dirty=true bei null uncommittetem Quellcode. Eine Ausschlussliste wurde im Review verworfen: sie an DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS zu haengen ist strukturell falsch, weil test_derived_snapshots Event-Log und triage.jsonl bewusst DRAUSSEN haelt und die zwei Register verschiedene Fragen beantworten. RICHTIGER ANSATZ: Dirtiness ERFASSEN, bevor der Produzent zu schreiben beginnt, und durchreichen - nicht hinterher messen. Der Seam source_state.py modelliert das bereits mit einem run-id-primaeren Stempel, und source_state_git.resolve_git_state hat das Schwesterproblem der Pfad-Relativierung schon geloest; wiederverwenden statt nachbauen. OFFEN, TEIL 2 - DAS VOLUMEN (aus trg-5e945a39): shipwright_events.jsonl haelt 587 Zeilen, 172 davon grade_snapshot (29 Prozent), ueber 16 distinkte grade/score-Werte mit nur 29 Uebergaengen in 16 Tagen - rund 83 Prozent der Zeilen tragen keine neue Information. Am 2026-07-27 allein 35 Snapshots aus 15 verschiedenen Sessions, jeder identisch, einer mit leerem session-Feld. Der Emitter dokumentiert die Kein-Dedup-Entscheidung bewusst und delegiert Dedup an die WebUI, unter der Praemisse ein Regen sei ein expliziter Akt - 15 Sessions an einem Tag falsifizieren die Praemisse. Zweite Haelfte: ein Regen, dessen project root der Main-Tree ist, hat keinen Delivery-Pfad. KONSUMENTENSEITE, ersetzt trg-d190cc37 (dessen Rezeptur #490 WIDERLEGT hat): NICHT 'group by base, latest per base'. #490 stellt fest - nach base zu gruppieren plottet main@base plus einen ungemergten Diff auf der Koordinate von main@base, und N parallele Iterates teilen sich EINE base, sodass 'latest per base' den Rest verwirft. Der Kontrakt ist neu gefasst: ein Branch-Snapshot ist ueberhaupt kein Punkt auf dem Trend des Default-Branch. Die WebUI-Aenderung (shipwright-webui, server/src/core/run-data-join.ts projectGradeTrend) muss diesem Kontrakt folgen, nicht der alten Rezeptur. ANDERES REPO - eigener Lauf dort, kann kein Teil dieses Monorepo-Iterates sein. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: IT-10 Plugin-Scope-Split: Einstiegs-Plugins global, 11 Pipeline-Plugins projekt-scoped
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-57317128 - inhaltlich unveraendert, nur in das IT-Schema umbenannt, damit das Board einheitlich ist. Spec und ACs liegen fertig unter .shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-16-plugin-scope-split.md. Statt alle ~14 Plugins auf User-Ebene zu aktivieren (sie laden heute /shipwright-*-Kommandos und Hooks in JEDEM Verzeichnis, auch in Nicht-Shipwright-Repos) den Marketplace korrekt scopen. SPLIT: global bleiben nur die Plugins, die in einem noch-nicht-Shipwright-Verzeichnis aufgerufen werden - adopt, grade, run (codex bleibt global, unberuehrt). Die 11 Pipeline-Plugins (project, design, plan, build, test, deploy, changelog, compliance, security, iterate, preview) wandern auf PROJEKT-Ebene; adopt und der Greenfield-Run SCHREIBEN diesen Enablement-Block in die .claude/settings.json des Zielrepos. LINCHPIN: Installation (per-user cache) ist etwas anderes als Enablement (scope) - der phase-runner von run hat kein Skill-Tool und liest die Phasen-SKILL.md aus dem Cache-Pfad, Orchestrierung haengt also an der Installation, nicht am Enablement. Extern reviewed 2026-07-16 (GPT-5.4 + Gemini, 2/2). DREI BLOCKER: (B1) der Orchestrator muss Cache-Pfade explizit aufloesen, nicht ueber das per SessionStart injizierte SHIPWRIGHT_PLUGIN_ROOT (nur gesetzt wenn aktiviert) - per clean-env-Greenfield-Spike verifizieren; (B2) frische Nutzer haben die 11 Pipeline-Plugins nach C1 moeglicherweise nicht INSTALLIERT, also Install-Preflight in run, mit leerem Cache testen; (B3) bereits adoptierte Repos verlieren Kommandos, also Migrationskommando. ENTSCHIEDEN (Owner, 2026-07-16): (D1) Greenfield ist run-only, shipwright-project bleibt projekt-scoped, globales Set = adopt/grade/run; (D2) Solo-Nutzung, das Monorepo verwendet .claude/settings.local.json, die getrackte settings.json bleibt git-ignoriert (B4 damit gegenstandslos). Dazu JSONC-bewusster Merge, Secret-Leak-Guard, Marketplace-Source-Konflikt-Guard, Min-Version-UX und praeskriptive Aktivierungs-Lag-Meldungen.

title: IT-11 Adoptierte Repos erben derived-snapshots-off-branch ohne Refresh-Producer
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-2f89afcf - inhaltlich unveraendert, nur in das IT-Schema umbenannt. ZEITKRITISCH: die Entscheidung muss fallen, BEVOR der Refresh-Producer-Iterate ausgeliefert wird. shared/ synct in die Plugin-Cache-Wurzel, die jedes adoptierte Repo aufloest, und die Aenderung lebt im iterate-Skill - also hoert jedes gemanagte Repo auf, seine abgeleiteten Compliance-Ansichten zu committen, sobald das merged. Diese Repos haben keinen Post-Merge-Refresh, ihre Ansichten frieren also auf dem ein, was main zuletzt berechnet hat. Nicht schlechter als heute (eine branch-lokale Ableitung ist dort aus demselben strukturellen Grund falsch), aber ein Repo, das nie parallele Iterates faehrt, traegt den Nachteil ohne den Vorteil. Aufloesen entweder durch Scaffolding des Refresh-Producers via /shipwright-adopt, oder indem das Verhalten fuer Einzel-Iterate-Projekte opt-out wird. Betrifft FREMDE gemanagte Repos, nicht dieses - deshalb eigener Lauf und eigene Entscheidung.

title: PR-review tier assumes the internal review ran instead of checking the record
detail: The tier decision ends by exempting maintainer-authored PRs on the stated grounds that the internal review step already reviewed them. That is an assumption from authorship, not evidence. The run's review record ships in the same PR and states per review type whether each pass ran, so the gate could read it. Observed live in PR #493: the record carried two review types explicitly closed as not-run because a session policy blocked them, and the tier still exempted the PR on the grounds that they had run. Suggested direction: read the shipped review record and require review when the internal passes are not closed as completed, rather than inferring it from the author.

title: IT-0b Nachzieher zum Hygiene-Sweep: C3-Event-Anker stempeln, Maintainer-Name aus der Prosa
detail: KONSOLIDIERT trg-1346abbd + trg-1a215186. Beide wurden in IT-0 gefaltet, NACHDEM der Lauf schon begonnen hatte - er konnte sie nicht sehen, und sie sind in iterate-2026-07-28-hygiene-sweep entsprechend nicht enthalten. Klein, entscheidungsfrei, dateidisjunkt zu allen Wellen des Konsolidierungsplans. PUNKT 1 - DEN C3-EVENT-ANKER STEMPELN (aus trg-1346abbd). Canon C3 befragt seine Uhr nur dort, wo eine Completion einen Event-Anker traegt. shared/scripts/tools/append_iterate_entry.py stempelt bewusst keinen, also laeuft die Same-Phase-Clock-Pruefung fuer die iterate-Phase ueberhaupt nie. Die Schranke ist heute sicher (das Ledger ist eine Datei pro run id, ein veralteter Marker nennt also einen anderen Lauf und der run-id-Zweig faengt ihn) und ist an vier Stellen aufgeschrieben: in lib/phase_history.py oberhalb COMPLETION_PRODUCER, in den Known bounds von handoff_phase_canon.py, im Docstring des Tools selbst, und als Assertion in test_completion_writers.py. ZU TUN: event_at so stempeln, wie append_phase_history.py es tut; dann den KNOWN-BOUND-Absatz an allen drei Textstellen loeschen und die Schranken-Assertion in test_completion_writers.py umdrehen. BLOAT-LANDMINE, der Grund warum es liegen blieb: append_iterate_entry.py misst 425 Zeilen bei Baseline current:425 state:grandfathered - die 5 Zeilen ratchen einen BESTEHENDEN Eintrag, was der Pre-Commit-Hook blockt. Entweder den ohnehin vorgesehenen Split machen, oder den Baseline-Eintrag im selben Commit anheben und das begruenden. ZWEITE LANDMINE: test_completion_writers.py wurde von IT-0 bei 302 baselined und sitzt damit exakt auf seiner Decke - die umgedrehte Assertion darf die Datei nicht waschsen lassen, ohne den Eintrag mitzuziehen. PUNKT 2 - MAINTAINER-NAME AUS DER PROSA (aus trg-1a215186). Vier lebende Dateien nennen einen einzelnen Maintainer in PROSA statt in Authorship-Metadaten, sodass der Name in ausgelieferte Ausgabe gelangt: ein Reviewer-System-Prompt, der das LLM anweist den Maintainer zu nennen; ein Docstring in einem Security-Tool; eine Runtime-Skill-Referenz; und eine Test-Fixture. Die Authorship-Metadaten (LICENSE, plugin.json, pyproject.toml) sind KORREKT und bleiben unveraendert - es geht nur um den Namen als Autoritaetsmarker in Prosa. Aufgetaucht im externen Review von iterate-2026-07-28-docs-placement-rule, das dasselbe Muster aus dem Gate-Katalog und dessen Tests entfernt hat; die verbleibenden vier liegen in anderen Subsystemen und wurden herausgelassen, statt den Lauf zu einer Placement-Aufraeumung zu verbreitern. Der Fund-Lauf ist die Referenz fuer die genaue Liste. NICHT HIERHER: die Tier-Entscheidung im PR-Review (trg-51f69c7d) - das ist eine Workflow-Datei und gehoert IT-9. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: IT-9 (neu) Host-Checks: Gates die nichts gaten, das Verdict-Label, kein Windows-CI, und der Tier der sich auf Autorschaft verlaesst
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-e3f79524 (das trg-c7e5835b supersedete, das trg-2f9865fb supersedete), KONSOLIDIERT zusaetzlich trg-51f69c7d. OWNS weiterhin EXKLUSIV: alles unter dem workflows-Verzeichnis, die ausgelieferten Workflow-Templates und den must-pass-Ableitungshelfer. Keine andere Karte darf eine Workflow-Datei anfassen - deshalb ist die Zuordnung des neuen Punktes erzwungen, nicht gewaehlt. Teil 1 ist als PR #475 gelandet. NEU, PUNKT 6 (aus trg-51f69c7d): die Tier-Entscheidung endet damit, maintainer-authorte PRs auszunehmen - mit der Begruendung, der interne Review-Schritt habe sie bereits geprueft. Das ist eine Annahme aus AUTORSCHAFT, kein Nachweis. Das Review-Record des Laufs faehrt im selben PR mit und sagt pro Review-Typ, ob der Pass gelaufen ist - das Gate KOENNTE es lesen. Live beobachtet an PR #493: das Record trug zwei Review-Typen, die ausdruecklich als not-run geschlossen waren (eine Session-Policy hatte sie blockiert), und der Tier nahm den PR trotzdem aus, weil sie gelaufen SEIEN. Fundstelle gemessen: .github/workflows/pr-review-run.yml Zeile 146, die Bedingung author != 'svroch' && author != 'dependabot[bot]'. Richtung: das mitgelieferte Review-Record lesen und Review VERLANGEN, wenn die internen Passes nicht als completed geschlossen sind, statt es aus dem Autor zu folgern. SEQUENZ-KOPPLUNG, wichtig: dieser Punkt konsumiert den reviews.json-Kontrakt, den IT-3 repariert. Heute kann das Record gar nicht beweisen, dass Stage 1 lief - REVIEW_TYPES hat keinen 'spec'-Eintrag (IT-3, ehemals trg-64372769). Wer den Tier auf ein Record umstellt, das an genau der blockierenden Stufe strukturell blind ist, tauscht eine Annahme gegen eine halbe. ALSO NACH IT-3. RESTPUNKTE der Ursprungskarte, unveraendert: (1) der in jedes onboardete Projekt gescaffoldete Review-Workflow UEBERSPRINGT eine Aenderung ab einer Groessenschwelle, also passieren die groessten Aenderungen ungeprueft, waehrend der Reviewer des Frameworks in derselben Lage fail-closed geht - den ausgelieferten ebenso fail-closed machen. (2) eine Aenderung aus einer eigenen Kopie des Projekts bekommt gar kein Modell-Review, weil der Host solchen Laeufen Credentials vorenthaelt; der dokumentierte sichere Weg ist zweistufig ueber ein Artefakt. (3) die konfigurierte must-pass-Menge gegen die tatsaechlich vorhandenen Checks vergleichen und bei Abweichung einen Follow-up melden. (4) Verdict dort labeln, wo ein Mensch es zuerst sieht: das Security-Gate feuert nur auf der schwersten Klasse und meldet ein blankes 'pass', waehrend Dutzende high-Befunde offen sind; die Evidenzseite traegt die ehrliche Form bereits, der Workflow-Schritt nicht. (5) scripts/verify_contract_surface.py ist der einzige Check, der liest was ein Konsument TATSAECHLICH holt - und ist an nichts verdrahtet. Verdrahten, und in die must-pass-Ableitung von (3) aufnehmen. AUS trg-9862202d: zwei Checks laufen auf jedem PR, melden ein Ergebnis und halten nichts auf - 'Empirical calibration (real OSS repos)' und 'Prepare review request'. Ruleset-Aenderung bei GitHub, kein Code. LANDMINE: ein Check, der NICHT auf jedem PR laeuft, blockiert als Required JEDEN PR fuer immer; 'Prepare review request' laeuft verifiziert immer, 'Empirical calibration' NICHT verifiziert - grade-empirical.yml erst lesen. Danach dasselbe im WebUI-Repo. AUS trg-80e3b3cd: KEIN CI-Job laeuft auf Windows, jeder Workflow ist ubuntu-latest. Ein Windows-only-Defekt ist bereits gruen auf main gelandet (97392eea, shipwright-changelog: ein Kindprozess kodiert stderr mit dem Locale-Codec, jeder Leser dekodiert utf-8) und wurde nur gefunden, weil jemand lokal auf Windows testete; und Windows-Fixes werden von plattform-gegateten Tests 'verifiziert', die CI immer skippt. Brief: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-28-triage-consolidation.md

title: Two F11 gates contradict each other for any iterate touching .github/workflows
detail: check_ci_supplychain_ack reads the acknowledgement from the COMMITTED shipwright_test_results.json (its disk fallback fires only when git show fails, i.e. when the file is untracked at that commit - it is tracked on main, so the committed copy always wins and carries no ack). check_no_derived_snapshots_committed lists that same file in DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS and errors if the commit touches it. Both are ERROR severity, so a workflow-touching iterate cannot satisfy both: committing the file fails the second, omitting it fails the first. Observed on iterate-2026-07-28-main-self-heal, resolved by committing the file (the acknowledgement is the safety-relevant record; the other is a merge-collision cost). The derived-snapshot rule landed while its companion refresh mechanism is still parked, so the ack needs a home outside the derived file - or the ack check needs to accept the working-tree copy when the committed one predates the run.

title: restore_derived_to_head overwrites the F5 block — finalization ordering trap
detail: Reported independently by two sessions. restore_derived_to_head() resets every dirty DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS path to HEAD, and shipwright_test_results.json is one of them. A correctly written F5 block (test totals, test_completeness ledger, spec_impact) is therefore silently reverted when restore runs after F5. One session had the F5 block overwritten TWICE in a single run. title: Auto-merge cannot be armed without branch protection, so F11 never delivers on an unprotected repo
detail: MEASURED 2026-07-29 (throwaway PR #501 into an unprotected base; all PR-triggered workflows are scoped to branches:[main], so the base had zero checks). gh pr merge --auto --squash FAILS: 'GraphQL: Pull request Protected branch rules not configured for this branch (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)'. It does NOT merge immediately as feared — GitHub refuses to arm it at all. Consequence: F11 arms fail-soft (tolerated), then watch_pr_delivery.py only WATCHES (it never merges; exit 4 = pending-timeout after 1800s). So on any repo without branch protection every iterate ends not-delivered with an open, green, unmerged PR. This is 100% reproducible, not an edge case, and it hits the most pragmatic persona hardest: a private repo on GitHub Free CANNOT have rulesets, so it can never arm auto-merge. Fix shape: when arming is refused, watch for green and then merge directly, rather than waiting for a merger that cannot exist. Relates to trg-a678bd00 (Adopt Automerge-Readiness Pack) and trg-52f1fecb (B4.5 gh-pr-ci producer).

title: SecFix-3: accepted-risk gate - reconcile with no register, honour ignore-file expiry, add an inline-suppression target
detail:
Filed from shipwright-webui, where the accepted-risk gate was first wired into CI (webui PR #332). Group SecFix-1..3 belong together; SecFix-1 and -2 are the webui-local halves and live in that repo's triage. This is the UPSTREAM half - all three items are in shared modules and cannot be fixed downstream, because forking a shared leaf would make an adopter's CI gate disagree with its own compliance dashboard.

1. The drift check returns success when the register file is ABSENT, before discovering any suppressions. That is correct for a fresh or legacy repo, but for a repo that HAS a register it means deleting the file silences the gate while every suppression stays live. Suggested: reconcile even with no register, so a suppression with no register at all reports as unrecorded rather than passing. Found by external review of the webui change; currently backstopped downstream by a repo-level invariant, which is a workaround rather than a fix.

2. The ignore-file reader collects entries regardless of their own expiry date, so an entry whose scanner-side expiry has already passed still counts as an active suppression - and the gate then reports the register reconciled while the scanner has stopped suppressing. Renewing only the register's date produces exactly that state. Suggested: honour the entry expiry, treating a lapsed one as absent.

3. Inline per-site suppressions are source-controlled and in effect, but no entry type in the register vocabulary covers them, so they are structurally unreconcilable. The shared docstring notes this deliberately. Suggested: consider an inline-suppression entry type, which would let adopters record them with a rationale and a re-review date instead of relying on a local ratchet.

Cross-checked with Codex, which agreed items 1 and 2 are real and that 3 is a genuine vocabulary gap rather than a misuse.

title: ADR INDEX.md silently drifts: rebuild_adr_index runs only when there are decision-drops to fold
detail:
MECHANISM. aggregate_decisions.py calls rebuild_adr_index() only INSIDE aggregate()'s `if valid:` branch, i.e. exclusively as a side-effect of folding decision-drops. An ADR that an iterate writes straight into .shipwright/planning/adr/<NNN>-<slug>.md therefore never reaches INDEX.md until some LATER release pass happens to have drops to aggregate. Nothing else refreshes it.

EVIDENCE. webui's INDEX.md sat at ADR-133 while five files (134, 135, 136, 137, 138) were unlisted. Repaired target-side on 2026-07-30 (webui PR #334) by importing rebuild_adr_index() and calling it directly - deliberately NOT main(), which also folds drops into decision_log.md and unlinks them from disk. The regenerated output was byte-identical for all 15 pre-existing rows and a second run produced a zero diff, so the function itself is correct and idempotent; only its CALL SITE is wrong. The same gap will re-open in every adopted repo on the next ADR an iterate writes.

WHY IT IS NOT COVERED BY THE DERIVED-SNAPSHOTS WORK. INDEX.md is a pure derivation of the folder listing, yet it is NOT a member of DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS (DERIVED_MDS = COMPLIANCE_MDS | AGENT_DOC_MDS, plus CI_SECURITY_SUMMARY / TEST_TRACEABILITY / TEST_RESULTS). So it is a committed derived view with no refresh producer, no drift guard, and no conflict handling - the same CLASS of problem as iterate-2026-07-27-derived-snapshots-off-branch, but outside its scope. Adjacent but NOT a duplicate of trg-ad29a709: that one is derived_snapshots.py / integrate_main.py ordering, this one is the aggregate_decisions.py call site. Confirmed there is no existing item on this: folded 510 items across triage.jsonl and the outbox, searched every status for aggregate_decisions / adr index / index.md / rebuild_adr_index - six hits, all false positives.

EXPLICITLY NOT PROPOSED: registering INDEX.md in DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS. That list exists for views that are (1) conflict-generating AND (2) WRONG when derived on a branch - change-history.md reads the BRANCH's git history (pre-squash SHAs) and an event log missing every concurrently-merging branch. Reason (2) does not hold here: INDEX.md derives from the ADR FOLDER LISTING, which on a branch is correct and complete, because the iterate puts its ADR file there in the same commit - view and truth travel together. Only reason (1) partly applies (two parallel iterates each append a line). Registering it would therefore be the WRONG fix: it would strip the index row out of the very commit that adds the ADR, and then require a main-side producer to re-derive it. The right direction is the opposite - make the index move WITH the ADR file (candidate b).

CANDIDATES. (a) Call rebuild_adr_index() unconditionally in aggregate(), outside `if valid:` - smallest change, but still only fires when the aggregator runs at all. (b) Call it from whatever writes the ADR spec file, so the index moves with the file that caused the drift - closest to the real cause. (c) Add a drift guard (meta-test) asserting INDEX.md lists every <NNN>-<slug>.md in the folder, so a stale index fails loudly instead of accumulating five entries of debt.

CONSTRAINTS FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP. A drift guard must tolerate DUPLICATE numbers: two distinct files legitimately share the 102- prefix in webui (campaign-c c4 and c6), and rebuild_adr_index() already emits both rows by design. The sibling clone and the plugin cache held byte-identical copies of aggregate_decisions.py on 2026-07-30, so the fix needs the usual update-marketplace.sh re-sync to reach the runtime.

THE MONOREPO'S OWN INDEX IS STALE TOO - AND REGENERATING IT IS NOT SAFE AS-IS. Measured 2026-07-30: 39 ADR files, 29 listed, 10 missing (106 through 115). But a regeneration run against a scratch copy of the folder is NOT byte-stable there: it also OVERWRITES two rows that someone hand-polished despite the "do not edit by hand" header. `ADR-104 - TT6 shared backfill engine` becomes `tt6 ...`, and `ADR-105 - TT7 adopt establishes the traceability baseline` becomes `tt7 adopt traceability baseline`. Net effect of a naive run: 12 lines added, 2 lines lost.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THIS FIX. rebuild_adr_index() derives the label PURELY from the filename slug (`ADR-<num> - <slug with dashes replaced by spaces>`). It has no other label source, so it structurally CANNOT emit "TT6" - filenames are lowercase - and it cannot preserve wording a human added. The hand-edit was therefore not sloppiness; it papered over a generator limitation, which is also why the "do not edit by hand" instruction sits in tension with the actual file. Any fix that starts calling rebuild_adr_index() more often will silently downgrade those two labels on its very first run, someone will hand-fix them again, and the cycle repeats. A drift guard (candidate c) has the same problem in reverse: it would flag the hand-polished rows as drift and force them back to the machine form.

SO THE FIX NEEDS A LABEL DECISION, not just a call-site change. Candidates: (i) accept machine labels as the SSoT and re-polish nothing - cheapest, mildly less readable; (ii) give the ADR file a title source the generator can read (front-matter or the first `# ` heading) and fall back to the slug - keeps human wording without renaming anything, and makes the "do not edit by hand" header true again; (iii) rename the two files so the generated label happens to be right - breaks every existing link to them.

DECIDED 2026-07-30 (Sven): do NOT regenerate the monorepo INDEX ahead of this fix. The cause lives in this repo, so the fix should carry the regeneration as its own side-effect - one PR instead of two, and no immediate re-drift. The 10 unlisted ADRs stay unlisted until then; that is the accepted cost. webui was handled differently and on purpose: it is a consumer repo with no cause to fix, and its regeneration WAS byte-stable for all 15 existing rows, so PR #334 was pure gain there.

detail: NACHFOLGER von IT-3 (trg-e3ca4314, geschlossen). Beide Befunde entstanden NACH dessen Abschluss und treffen exakt dessen Thema - F11 sagt etwas Unwahres ueber den Lauf, den es prueft - diesmal auf der Zustellseite statt auf der Ledger-Seite. (1) trg-68e39bd5, high, GEMESSEN 2026-07-29 mit Wegwerf-PR #501 in eine ungeschuetzte Base (alle PR-Workflows sind auf branches:[main] gescoped, die Base hatte also null Checks): 'gh pr merge --auto --squash' SCHLAEGT FEHL mit 'GraphQL: Pull request Protected branch rules not configured for this branch (enablePullRequestAutoMerge)'. Es merged NICHT sofort wie befuerchtet - GitHub weigert sich, es ueberhaupt zu armen. Folge: F11 armt fail-soft (toleriert, die Warnung nennt sogar 'no branch protection'), dann schaut watch_pr_delivery.py nur ZU - es merged nie, Exit 4 = pending-timeout nach 1800s. Auf jedem Repo ohne Branch Protection endet damit JEDES Iterate als nicht-geliefert mit einem offenen, gruenen, ungemergten PR. Zu 100 Prozent reproduzierbar, kein Edge Case. Trifft die pragmatischste Persona am haertesten: ein privates Repo auf GitHub Free KANN keine Rulesets haben, kann also nie armen. WICHTIG: das heutige Verhalten ist bewusst gebaut ('PR left open for manual merge'), der Fix ist deshalb eine ENTSCHEIDUNG, kein Bugfix - darf ein Shipwright-Agent einen PR selbst mergen? title: IT-11 (neu nach dem Architektur-Review) Adoptierte Repos brauchen aktuelle Evidenz - aber wahrscheinlich OHNE Refresh-Producer
detail: SUPERSEDES trg-c5b05f31. Grund fuer die Neufassung: der alte Text sagt 'die Entscheidung muss fallen, BEVOR der Refresh-Producer-Iterate ausgeliefert wird' und setzt damit voraus, dass es diesen Producer geben wird. In einem Produkt, das mit Pruefbarkeit wirbt, ist das kein akzeptabler Dauerzustand. Das bleibt der Kern dieser Karte. title: Triage-Delivery: eine aus CI gefilte Karte landet im gitignorierten Outbox und erreicht niemanden (gehoert zu IT-1)
detail: GEHOERT ZU IT-1 (trg-4ebc928e, Triage-Store und Delivery haerten) - dort einhaengen, nicht separat abarbeiten.  MECHANISMUS, bewiesen und nicht theoretisch: triage.should_route_to_outbox liefert True, wenn 'has_origin AND current_branch == default_branch'. Auf einem GitHub-Runner sind beide Bedingungen erfuellt - actions/checkout konfiguriert ein origin und checkt bei einem push auf refs/heads/main einen benannten main-Branch aus. Jeder Producer, der aus CI heraus eine Triage-Karte filet, schreibt damit .shipwright/triage.outbox.jsonl. Diese Datei ist gitignoriert und wird ausschliesslich vom D2-Sweep beim Anlegen eines Iterate-Worktrees konsumiert - also auf einer Entwicklermaschine, die den Container nie sieht. Die Karte stirbt mit dem Job. triage_add exit 0, keine Fehlermeldung, keine Spur.  BEWEIS: genau das hat die AC-7-Zustellung des Derived-Snapshots-Refresh in der Produktion getoetet - der Failure-Card-Pfad war vollstaendig inert und funktionierte nur in den Tests, deren Fixture-Repos kein origin haben (und deren Integrations-Fixture ein detached worktree ist, also gar nicht auf einem Branch). Gefunden vom Stage-2-Code-Review, nicht von der Test-Suite. Behoben wurde es dort durch einen direkten Aufruf von append_triage_item_idempotent(to_outbox=False) statt der Delegation an triage_add.py.  STATUS: derzeit LATENT im Monorepo, weil nach dem Wegfall des Refresh-Producers voraussichtlich kein Producer mehr aus CI heraus filet. Es bleibt eine Falle fuer den naechsten, der es versucht - und die Routing-Entscheidung ist genau deshalb gefaehrlich, weil sie plausibel aussieht (idle main soll nicht dirty werden) und in der einen Umgebung kippt, in der niemand hinschaut.  FIXRICHTUNG: entweder should_route_to_outbox erkennt CI (GITHUB_ACTIONS/CI gesetzt) und routet dann in den getrackten Store, oder ein Producer, dessen Zustellung die Anforderung IST, waehlt sein Ziel explizit statt es einem Delegaten zu ueberlassen. Zweiteres ist die Lehre: wer die Zustellung zusagt, darf das Ziel nicht delegieren.

title: F11's derived-snapshot gate is blind whenever the branch was behind (it inspects the merge commit)
detail:
MEASURED 2026-07-30. `check_no_derived_snapshots_committed` reports "none
derived" while the eleven forbidden paths ride into main, whenever the branch was
BEHIND at F11.

WHY. F11 runs `ensure_current` (integrate-if-behind) BEFORE
`verify_iterate_finalization.py`, and the verifier is invoked with
`--commit "$(git rev-parse HEAD)"`. If the integrate created a merge commit, HEAD is
now that MERGE - and the gate inspects one commit. A merge commit's changed-path set
does not contain what the iterate's own commit carried.

PROOF (PR #493, whose iterate commit carried all eleven):
  f5f6cca2  the MERGE commit  -> _commit_changed_paths sees  5 paths, 0 forbidden
  48ee9665  the ITERATE commit -> _commit_changed_paths sees 46 paths, 11 forbidden
The gate ran, passed, and eleven derived snapshots landed on main.

HOW OFTEN. Of main's last 40 commits, 8 carry at least one forbidden derived path.
5 of those 8 are AFTER the gate went live (e21a7b71 / #480) - so they are not legacy,
they slipped past a live gate: 24a56158, bebdc9a3, d9bc7d90, 80647cc9, 23329f57.

WHAT IT HAS COST ALREADY - this is not cosmetic:
- main still TRACKS .shipwright/agent_docs/build_dashboard.md and session_handoff.md.
  main's copies name run iterate-2026-07-28-docs-placement-rule and a dead session id
  (7c6c7b07-...). Nobody reads them: every run writes its own copy in its own
  worktree, F6 does not stage them, and restore_derived_to_head resets them.
- shipwright_test_results.json still moves on main for the same reason (#497), which
  is what FALSIFIED the premise of the trg-ad29a709 carve-out ("nothing commits this
  file any more") and forced the carry mechanism in PR #502. The root cause was this
  gate all along.

WHY IT IS EASY TO MISS: a run whose `ensure_current` reports "already-current"
creates no merge commit, so the gate inspects the real commit and works perfectly.
The gate only goes blind when the branch was behind - which is the common case on a
busy main, and exactly when the derived churn matters most.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): inspect the RANGE the PR actually contributes
(merge-base..HEAD) rather than a single commit, or inspect the commit carrying the
Run-ID trailer rather than HEAD. Both are cheap. Note the gate's other skip is
honest and should stay: no --commit -> skipped.

RELATED: trg-012db453 (Weg B). B assumes the seven documents are written at RELEASE
only. While iterates keep smuggling them in, B's release-time regeneration fights
incoming churn on every merge - so this is effectively a prerequisite for B being
worth building.

title: SecFix-3 (monorepo, AUTONOMOUS-READY): accepted-risk gate - reconcile with no register, and honour the ignore-file expiry
detail:
Filed from shipwright-webui, where the accepted-risk gate was first wired into CI (webui PR #332). SecFix-1..5 are one family split so each is a SELF-CONTAINED autonomous unit; 1, 2 and 4 live in the webui triage. Order: run 1 and 3 in parallel, then 4, then 2.

SCOPE IS DELIBERATELY TWO ITEMS, NOT THREE. A third finding from the same review - that inline per-site suppressions have no entry type in the register vocabulary - is a schema decision with reach beyond this repo and is filed separately as SecFix-5, explicitly NOT autonomous. Do not fold it in here: this item is meant to run unattended, and it can only stay that way if every question in it is already answered.

AUTONOMY: both fixes below are well specified and behaviour-local. Note the repo has THREE pytest roots - running the shared suite alone is a false green.

1. The drift check returns success when the register file is ABSENT, before discovering any suppressions. Correct for a fresh or legacy repo, but for a repo that HAS a register it means deleting the file silences the gate while every suppression stays live. Suggested: reconcile even with no register, so a suppression with no register at all reports as unrecorded rather than passing. A reviewer sharpened this: a contributor who deletes the register AND the downstream backstop test in the same change still passes today. Downstream currently works around it with a repo-level invariant, which is a workaround, not a fix.

2. The ignore-file reader collects entries regardless of their own expiry date, so an entry whose scanner-side expiry has already passed still counts as an active suppression - and the gate then reports the register reconciled while the scanner has stopped suppressing. Renewing only the register's date produces exactly that state. Suggested: honour the entry expiry, treating a lapsed one as absent.

DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE - do not skip: webui vendors these modules with a hash manifest, and nothing verifies the upstream hash, so nothing there will notice this change. The re-vendor is tracked as SecFix-4 in the webui triage and must follow this item.

Both findings were cross-checked with Codex, which agreed they are real.

title: SecFix-5 (monorepo, NOT AUTONOMOUS - schema decision): should the accepted-risk register gain an entry type for inline per-site suppressions?
detail:
Filed from shipwright-webui. SecFix-1..5 are one family; this is the only member that must NOT run unattended, which is why it was split out of SecFix-3 rather than bundled with it.

WHY NOT AUTONOMOUS: this would extend the register's entry-type vocabulary, i.e. a schema that every adopter repo and the compliance dashboard consume. Adding a type changes what existing registers validate against and what the dashboard renders. That is a design decision with blast radius beyond this repo, and it should be taken deliberately - possibly with a schema-version bump - not decided inside an unattended run.

IT IS ALSO LEGITIMATE TO DECLINE. The shared tooling currently states, as a deliberate position, that an inline suppression is source-controlled and in effect but that no entry type covers it - and that treating it as though one did is a misreading. Downstream has accepted that position and is closing the gap locally with a ratchet instead (webui SecFix-2). So 'no change, the position stands' is a valid outcome; this card exists so the question is decided rather than merely inherited.

THE QUESTION. An inline suppression is a real, in-effect silencing of a finding on production code, carrying a justification comment but no owner, no expiry and no central visibility. A register entry would give it a re-review date and dashboard presence; a ratchet gives drift control but no expiry. Which of those an adopter should get is the decision.

IF YES, the design work is: a new target value, how it is DISCOVERED offline (a source scan, unlike the file-based targets), what the rule identifier is keyed to (rule id, or rule plus site), how it interacts with the both-directions drift check, and whether existing registers need a schema bump.

CONTEXT: downstream currently has 12 tracked inline suppressions across 4 rules, which is the sample that raised the question.

title: [f0] shared/tests failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
shared/tests: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It IS on the suite.xdist allowlist, so the fan-out inside the unit is a candidate cause: fix it, or drop it from suite.xdist.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock --with diff-cover==10.3.0 pytest shared/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider -m 'not slow and not cross_plugin'
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\derived-gate-sees-the-pr' --run-id iterate-2026-07-30-derived-gate-sees-the-pr

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.
launchPayload:
/shipwright-iterate --type bug

Context: F0 suite card f0-race:shared/tests. The test unit shared/tests failed while the units ran side by side and passed when re-run alone, so the gate stayed green and nothing else recorded it.
Reproduce alone (expect GREEN): uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock --with diff-cover==10.3.0 pytest shared/tests -q -p no:cacheprovider -m 'not slow and not cross_plugin'
Reproduce in parallel (expect intermittent RED): uv run shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\derived-gate-sees-the-pr' --run-id iterate-2026-07-30-derived-gate-sees-the-pr
Establish whether it is a race between units or an unreliable test, fix the cause, and close this card. Never weaken or delete the test to make it pass.

title: Derived compliance docs: build Weg B (release-time check-in + on-demand docs PR)
detail:
DECIDED 2026-07-30 by the operator: Weg B, with the open question answered
("does anyone read the evidence on main continuously between releases?" -> no; if
someone needs it fresh, they trigger a release or run the on-demand command).

Decision paper (full reasoning, plain German):
.shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-30-derived-snapshots-decision.md
on branch iterate/derived-snapshots-refresh (worktree kept for exactly this).

WHAT B IS, in one sentence: the seven derived documents are recomputed at RELEASE
and checked in through the release PR a human already opens and reviews - plus one
command that opens a plain docs-only PR for anyone who needs them fresher in
between. No robot with write access to main, no key, no exception to the branch
protection rule.

FOUR THINGS TO BUILD (all small):
1. The release step checks the seven files in. It already RECOMPUTES them today -
   it just does not ship them.
2. A command that opens a docs-only PR in between releases, with the same checks
   and the same visibility as any other change.
3. The stamp says "as of release X / commit Y" instead of pretending to be live.
   For audit evidence a fixed point is the better claim than a moving one.
4. Docs: what is current, what is not, and how to refresh it.

WHAT GETS THROWN AWAY: the Weg-A machinery on iterate/derived-snapshots-refresh
(post-merge workflow + deploy-key push + debounce + loop guard + the AC-7 failure
card). Weg A WORKS - the deploy key was measured pushing to protected main
("remote: Bypassed rule violations", commit 86a948ac). It was rejected on
judgement by three independent reviewers, not because it is impossible. Recording
that here so the decision stays revisitable rather than reading as a forced move.

NOT part of this: the ledger carve-out (trg-ad29a709) already shipped as PR #502
and is independent of which way this goes.

--- MEASURED 2026-07-30, so the scope is not guessed ---

DOES REGENERATION JUST WORK? YES for the tree-derived set - no backlog to catch up.
Probed by regenerating all seven in a throwaway worktree at main (a3e625fc) and
diffing against what is committed. It is a pure RECOMPUTATION, not incremental: one
run reproduces the correct current state from shipwright_events.jsonl + triage +
git history, all of which already ship. test-evidence.md moved 881 lines, which
looks alarming and is not: new rows are PREPENDED, so every index below shifts and
the whole table diffs. The 'ok' markers were 40 added / 40 removed - balanced, no
regression.

THREE THINGS THE BUILD MUST GET RIGHT ANYWAY (scope, not backlog):

1. ci-security.json is NOT tree-derived. The parked branch classified it
   DERIVES_FROM_CI_HISTORY: it reads the LATEST COMPLETED CI scan, not the
   repository. At release time that happens to be fine (a scan just ran on the
   release PR), but B must state the dependency instead of assuming all seven
   behave alike. This is the H4 finding from the parked iterate - do not lose it.

2. build_dashboard.md and session_handoff.md are SESSION_SCOPED and must stay OUT
   of the set. They are per-session and meaningless on main. B's 'seven files' is
   the compliance directory, which is already correct - pin it so a later hand does
   not widen it to 'all eleven derived snapshots'.

3. shipwright_test_results.json is RUN_WRITTEN and is nobody's to regenerate
   (trg-ad29a709, shipped as PR #502).

SEPARATE, UNOWNED, NOT PART OF B: the Consistency Audit has no schedule and no CI
trigger, so it never runs on its own - the dashboard discloses this honestly. Its
last run (2026-07-28) was 59 checks, 47 pass, 2 FAIL, 10 skip. Those 2 failures are
unrelated to B and currently belong to nobody. Worth its own item.

--- PAIRED WITH trg-d0e4592e (decided 2026-07-31) ---

Build both in ONE iterate. The reason is scheduling, not coupling, and the difference
is worth writing down so nobody later infers a dependency that does not exist:

CHECKED AND FALSE: that B would have to touch the derived-snapshot gate. The worry was
that B's release-time check-in (and its on-demand docs PR) would commit the seven
files and trip `check_no_derived_snapshots_committed`. It would not — that gate is
reachable ONLY from `iterate_checks.py`'s F11 check list, and the changelog/release
phase never invokes `verify_iterate_finalization`. A release commit and a docs-only PR
both pass it without noticing it exists.

SO WHY PAIR: a finalization cycle (F0 through F11, three review stages, external
review, PR, merge) costs hours regardless of diff size. B is four small build items;
the remedy fix is ~30 lines plus tests. Two cycles for that is the waste. The Tier-3
size gate is not a counter-argument here — the three PRs it closed on 2026-07-27 were
~5,000 lines; these two together are nowhere near it.

KEEP THEM SEPARABLE IN THE PR: different subjects (where documents live vs what a gate
tells an operator), different files. If the review cascade gets noisy because of the
mix, split at that point rather than up front.

title: The derived-snapshot gate's printed remedy is a no-op on a merge HEAD (HEAD~1 is the offending commit)
detail:
The derived-snapshot gate prints a remedy that does nothing on the very
shape it was just taught to catch, so the operator loops.

`derived_snapshot_gate.py` prints:
    git restore --source=HEAD~1 --staged [--worktree] -- <paths>   then amend

On a MERGE HEAD — the shape the gate now catches, offender in an earlier commit with
an `ensure_current` merge on top — `HEAD~1` is the FIRST PARENT, i.e. the branch's own
pre-merge tip. That is precisely the commit carrying the offending snapshot. So the
restore writes the offending content over itself, the amend changes nothing the gate
looks at, and the next run fails identically. Following the printed instruction is a
dead end, not a fix.

Secondary, lower-frequency: for a path the BRANCH never touched (mainline carried it
in through the merge), the same command reverts mainline's version into the index -
manufacturing the divergence the gate exists to prevent.

NOT introduced by the gate-range fix. `--source=HEAD~1` was already wrong on a merge
HEAD before it: the old single-commit gate could fire on a merge too (#493's merge
showed 5 paths; had one been derived, the same misaimed command would have printed).
The fix raises the FREQUENCY, not the existence - which is why it is filed rather than
folded in.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN THAT DIFF: the seam drawn there is what the gate SEES vs what
it SAYS, and a half-bounded remedy prints a WORSE command than today's. Bounding it
needs a decision - which commits count as "the branch's own" when HEAD is a merge -
and that decision belongs with someone who can also re-test the operator path.

FIX DIRECTION (not prescribed): resolve the restore source to the merge-base with the
default branch rather than HEAD~1, so it names the state before the branch touched
anything; and bound the offender list to paths the branch's own non-merge commits
touched, so mainline's files are never named. Both are cheap; neither is obvious
enough to smuggle in.

The gate BLOCKS correctly throughout - nothing bad ships. This is about the operator
being sent in a circle, and the detail still points at
`shared/scripts/lib/derived_snapshots.py` for the real explanation.

--- PAIRED WITH trg-012db453 (decided 2026-07-31) ---

Build alongside Weg B in one iterate. Scheduling only — there is NO technical
dependency: this gate is reachable solely from F11's check list, and the release phase
that B changes never invokes it (checked, not assumed). Kept as its own item because it
is its own defect with its own measurement; folded into B's iterate because a
finalization cycle costs hours and this is ~30 lines.

reason: FIXED and merged as PR #503 (dcf85f87). Every F11 gate that asks what the branch changed now reads git_helpers._iterate_changed_paths (merge-base..HEAD) instead of one commit, so an offender in an earlier commit is caught even when ensure_current left a merge on top. The base scores candidates and keeps the narrowest (a stale origin/master resolves fine), refuses a lone uncorroborated name, and an unavailable view returns None so it can never read as clean.

STALE, and the third id for one finding (dedupKey gh-ci:322548704; trg-a9b2b106 and trg-b9a2f7ff were already dismissed, this twin was missed). The 'Probe refresh-token bypass' workflow no longer exists on main - removed in 8f28d73b - and its failing run sits at an old sha that has aged out of the run list. main's head dcf85f87 is green. Diagnosed, not re-fixed.

Downloaded run 30609369118 (main@dcf85f87): 1 high, rule UNICODE_RIGHT_TO_LEFT_OVERRIDE at .shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-28-codescanning-alerts.md:63. title: Compliance refresh: the real update_compliance producer is never driven by a test
detail: Named as the one testable-but-untested behaviour in iterate-2026-07-31-derived-docs-at-release, so it is a work item rather than a spec note. Every refusal, rewind and content-floor test for the compliance-evidence refresh injects a fake regenerate() or monkeypatches converge(), so the real regenerate_tracked_snapshots -> _update_compliance chain runs in no test. That is not theoretical: the Stage-3 doubt review found a defect invisible for exactly this reason (the compliance config was never rewound because the append-only prefix guard could not apply to a rewritten file, and no test exercised the real producer's side effects). What is needed is a fixture project carrying a full .shipwright tree plus the compliance plugin importable, driving one real converge() pass and asserting (a) the seven documents actually change, (b) the producer inputs end where they started, and (c) the fixpoint is reached in the measured 2-3 passes. title: ADR INDEX.md has no merge-reconciliation entry for parallel iterates
detail: Since iterate-2026-07-31-adr-index-producer, .shipwright/planning/adr/INDEX.md is regenerated on a BRANCH at iterate F3 (previously only on main at release time). Two parallel iterates that each add an ADR both append a row at the same anchor, which is a 3-way merge conflict. INDEX.md is not in CHURN_ALLOWLIST (shared/scripts/lib/churn_merge.py) and has no merge=union .gitattributes entry, so resolve_churn_conflicts classifies it as blocking and ensure_current aborts rather than auto-resolving. Fails loudly and safely (no corruption), but needs a human. Suggested fix: add an ADR_INDEX constant to lib/churn_merge.py + CHURN_ALLOWLIST, update the documented SSoT that test_churn_merge_doc_sync pins, and re-derive it in resolve_churn_conflicts.regenerate_tracked_snapshots by calling lib.adr_index.rebuild_adr_index on the merged tree - it is a pure re-derive from the merged folder listing, the ideal shape for that machinery. Deferred from the originating iterate because touching churn/merge machinery trips the cross_component risk flag, which mandates its own integration-coverage test; the core producer fix was kept separable. NOT a DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS candidate - a folder listing is correct when derived on a branch.

reason: Fixed in iterate-2026-07-31-shared-tests-parallel-flake. Neither cause the card names: dev_server's one-shot lazy proxy derived a path with pathlib on first call, and pathlib picks its flavour from the process-global os.name a test fakes - so it raised only where nothing had burned the proxy. Serial order primed it; xdist made it a per-worker lottery. Splitting the retry's two variables: RED 3/3 alone WITH xdist, RED alone without. Fixed at import via os.path; allowlist unchanged.

title: F11 session_handoff freshness check compares a backtick-quoted run id against a bare one
detail: The check_session_handoff_fresh verifier reads the run id out of the handoff's 'Current Iterate Progress' section, where generate_session_handoff.py writes it as '- **Run ID**: `<run-id>`' - backtick-quoted. The comparison is against the bare --run-id, so the two never match and the message renders as: names `X`, not X - the same string, reported as a mismatch. Observed on iterate-2026-07-31-derived-docs-at-release with a handoff regenerated seconds earlier by the correct run. It is a WARN, so nothing blocks; the cost is that a freshness signal which should be meaningful is unconditionally noisy, which trains operators to ignore it - and a genuinely stale handoff would look identical. Fix direction: strip surrounding backticks (and whitespace) from the extracted value before comparing, in the verifier rather than in the generator, since the backticks are correct markdown for a code-ish identifier. Worth a test that a freshly generated handoff passes its own freshness check, which nothing currently asserts.

title: F0 race card records THAT a unit raced but not WHICH test failed, so it cannot be diagnosed after the session ends
detail: suite_report.entry_detail composes the card from named scalars only and states outright that the failing output stayed in that run's F0 console. The allowlist is correct and should stay - the card is git-tracked and published, so captured output must not reach it. But the card is then unactionable once the console is gone: consuming f0-race:shared/tests required reproducing the whole unit from scratch (two probe shapes, ~10 suite runs) purely to learn which test failed, and the card itself says one clean parallel run is not evidence. A failing pytest node id is repo-derived identity, the same class as unit_id which the card already carries. Candidate: extract node ids from the JUnit report the runner already writes (its existence is what proves pytest ran) and pass them through the same sanitiser as a scalar list. Check against the constitution's tracked-artifact rule before implementing.

title: dev_server derives its shared/scripts constant three ways and inserts it into sys.path twice
detail: After iterate-2026-07-31-shared-tests-parallel-flake, __init__.py derives shared/scripts with os.path at import (hardened so a faked os.name cannot break it), while state.py:20 still derives the same value with Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] and inserts it into sys.path FIRST - so the proxy's own guard can never fire in a normally imported process. profile_config.py:98 and spawn.py:47 carry two more pathlib derivations of nearby paths. All three are latent-safe today: two run at module scope where os.name is real, and spawn.py's is a fallback reachable only when the package attribute is absent, which nothing does. One derivation, one insert, one constant for the package is the right end state. Deliberately not done in that iterate - the code reviewer and the author both judged changing unrelated files inside a bug fix to be a refactor wearing a fix label.

title: F11 complexity gates turn two fail-closed coverage checks into green SKIPs below medium
detail: Belongs to the IT-3 anchor (F11 fail-open paths). Two verifiers gate on the AGENT-REPORTED complexity before doing the work they advertise. (1) check_integration_coverage documents itself as NON-dodgeable because it RECOMPUTES cross_component from the diff, but it returns SKIPPED when the recorded complexity is below medium - the recompute never runs, so the non-dodgeability is a property of the flag, not of the gate. (2) removal-coverage is documented as running at ALL complexities, yet its infra-failure branch is complexity-gated: below medium a missing --commit, an unresolvable base ref or a collector exception turns from a blocking ERROR into a green SKIP, and cross-layer coverage disappears outright. Both are PRE-EXISTING. They are filed now because iterate-2026-07-31-it5-classification-calibration capped the Stage-1 history fall-through at small, which raises how often runs sit below medium and therefore how often these skips are reached. That run mitigated the cause rather than the symptom - Quick Scout now runs the diff-driven detectors so a genuine cross-component change reaches medium from the diff - but that mitigation is agent-followed prose, not enforcement, which the external plan review flagged as high. The enforceable fix is to move each complexity gate BELOW the recompute so the diff decides, and to keep infra failures fail-closed at every complexity. Deliberately not changed in that run: these are shared F11 verifiers, and the consolidation brief forbids shifting gates alongside a calibration change.

title: touches_build JS message patterns match inside longer filenames (Python half now guarded, JS half not)
detail: RISK_TAXONOMY['touches_build'] matches its patterns against the MESSAGE with re.search and no filename boundary, so the JS entries fire on longer tokens that merely contain them - a message naming my-package.json or package.json.bak raises touches_build even though the diff-driven detector deliberately returns False for exactly those (pinned by test_touches_build_files_does_not_match_partial_basename). The Python entries added in iterate-2026-07-31-it5-classification-calibration were given token guards ((?<![\w.-]) / (?![\w.-])) after an external review found the same defect there, so the two halves of one taxonomy entry now use different matching semantics. Over-firing is the safe direction, which is why this is low: the cost is a spurious small floor plus a review trigger, never a missed one. title: F11 gate contradiction: 'session_handoff fresh' and 'no derived snapshots' cannot both be satisfied
detail:
Observed on PR #508, reproducible on any medium+ iterate.

verify_iterate_finalization runs both:
  - 'session_handoff.md fresh' WARNs unless the handoff names THIS run;
  - 'no derived snapshots in the iterate commit' FAILs if the commit carries one.

.shipwright/agent_docs/session_handoff.md is in DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS
(shared/scripts/lib/derived_snapshots.py). So satisfying the first REQUIRES committing
a file the second forbids. Restoring it to mainline (as the derived gate instructs)
guarantees the WARN; regenerating it for the run guarantees the FAIL.

Today this is survivable because one is a WARN and the other an ERROR, so the run
resolves it in the safe direction by accident rather than by design. But the WARN then
fires on every medium+ iterate, which is the habituation-to-red problem FR-01.06 was
hardened against - and it is indistinguishable from a handoff that is genuinely stale.

Fix directions (not prescribed, they are different decisions):
  (a) drop the freshness check - the handoff is derived, so 'whose run wrote it' is not
      a property the PR can carry;
  (b) move the per-run handoff onto a per-run path the restore cannot reach, the same
      move this run had to make for surface_verification (see the F5c entry);
  (c) exempt session_handoff.md from DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS, which trades the WARN for the
      N(N-1)/2 collision the derived rule exists to prevent - probably wrong.

NOT fixed in the originating iterate: it is a gate-design decision, the run that found
it was scoped to the PR reviewer, and (b) is the same shape as a fix that iterate
already had to make under time pressure - worth deciding deliberately rather than
copying.

title: The delivery ladder's self-merge rung has never run against a real unprotected repository
detail:
PR #510 shipped a code path that MERGES a pull request when the code host structurally cannot arm auto-merge (base branch unprotected). It is heavily unit-tested (69 behaviours, incl. every refusal path) and one integration test drives the real watcher and readiness against a faked host — but no test, and no run, has ever merged a real PR through it. This monorepo's main branch IS protected, so the delivery of PR #510 itself exercised rung 1 (arm + watch) only; rung 3 is unexercised by construction here and cannot be exercised here.

What the end-to-end claim currently rests on: three probed host facts (gh pr merge accepts --match-head-commit; repos/{o}/{r}.allow_auto_merge and repos/{o}/{r}/branches/{b}.protected are readable without admin) plus the argv asserted in tests. Every refusal path fails closed, so the expected failure mode is 'reports not delivered' rather than 'merges the wrong thing' — but that is a design property, not an observation.

Deferred deliberately, not overlooked: it needs a repository this repo cannot provide. Cheapest honest exercise: a throwaway repo (or an unprotected second branch used as a base) with one iterate-shaped PR, then run deliver_pr.py against it and check (a) it classifies unavailable from the facts, (b) it waits for whatever checks exist, (c) it merges pinned to the verified commit, (d) it confirms MERGED, and (e) with SHIPWRIGHT_ITERATE_SELF_MERGE=0 it returns exit 6 immediately instead of waiting. Worth pairing with trg-a678bd00 (Adopt Automerge-Readiness Pack), which already concerns repos without protection.

Not in scope of this card: the F11 handoff/derived-snapshot gate contradiction (already open as trg-758e62c0) and the missing @FR-tagged unit tests for adopted FRs (already the scope of trg-137f48b5, REQ3.05).

title: Promote the Stage-1 spec pass into reviews (webui reader is ready) - NOT a one-liner
detail:
The webui consumer half shipped 2026-07-31 (shipwright-webui PR #339, ce21323e): readReviewRecord now accepts review types outside its pinned five and any schema_version >= its own, so the release condition named in review_record_schema.py:74 is met. BUT the promotion is NOT the one line that comment implies, for three reasons found after that PR merged.

(1) THE PRODUCER IS STRICT IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE CONSUMER WAS. validate_record (shared/scripts/lib/review_record_schema.py:218-223) requires every REVIEW_TYPES key to be present in  AND rejects any key outside it. Every record ever written keeps  under , so the moment  joins REVIEW_TYPES they all report  - to this repo own F11 gate (check_review_record), which fails CLOSED and tells the operator to repair-or-delete an immutable, git-tracked history that is perfectly fine. There is NO gates->reviews fallback in review_record_core.py (grepped 2026-07-31). A transitional READ path is required, plus a test that a pre-promotion record still validates.

(2) DO NOT BUMP SCHEMA_VERSION. The webui reader is a FLOOR now, so a bump buys it nothing, while validate_record rejects a version newer than its own constant - creating old-plugin-cache casualties for zero gain. Promotion-only is the shape.

(3) GATE ON A DEPLOYED WEBUI, NOT ON THE MERGE. Merge-order is not install-order: this plugin auto-updates via the marketplace cache while shipwright-webui is hand-deployed. New-plugin + old-webui makes readReviewRecord invalid, and review-state.ts deliberately does not degrade - all five rows render "exists but could not be read. That is a data problem, not a clean result", which is FALSE under version skew and fires on every run until someone rebuilds.

Scope: move spec from GATE_TYPES into REVIEW_TYPES, keep GATE_TYPES as the (now empty) seam or retire it, add the backward-compatible read for records carrying spec under gates, and cover it. Reference: the webui-side reasoning is in shipwright-webui .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-07-31-review-record-tolerant-reader.md (AC10 + the Stage-3 doubt table).

title: Promote the Stage-1 spec pass into reviews (webui reader is ready) -- NOT a one-liner
detail:
The webui consumer half shipped 2026-07-31 (shipwright-webui PR #339, ce21323e): readReviewRecord now accepts review types outside its pinned five AND any schema_version >= its own, so the release condition named in review_record_schema.py:74 is met.

BUT the promotion is NOT the one line that comment implies. Three reasons, all found after that PR merged:

(1) THE PRODUCER IS STRICT IN EXACTLY THE WAY THE CONSUMER WAS. validate_record (shared/scripts/lib/review_record_schema.py:218-223) requires every REVIEW_TYPES key to be PRESENT in the reviews object, and rejects any key outside it. Every record ever written keeps spec under the gates sibling -- so the moment spec joins REVIEW_TYPES, all of them report 'reviews is missing: spec', to THIS repo's own F11 gate (check_review_record), which fails CLOSED and tells the operator to repair-or-delete an immutable, git-tracked review history that is perfectly fine. There is NO gates-to-reviews fallback in review_record_core.py (grepped 2026-07-31). So the change needs a transitional READ path plus a test that a pre-promotion record still validates -- not a constant edit.

(2) DO NOT BUMP SCHEMA_VERSION. The webui reader is a FLOOR now, so a bump buys it nothing, while validate_record rejects a version NEWER than its own constant -- creating old-plugin-cache casualties for zero gain. Promotion-only.

(3) GATE ON A DEPLOYED WEBUI, NOT ON THE MERGE. Merge-order is not install-order: this plugin auto-updates through the marketplace cache while shipwright-webui is hand-deployed. New-plugin + old-webui makes readReviewRecord return invalid, and review-state.ts deliberately does NOT degrade to the marker view -- all five rows render 'This run's review record exists but could not be read. That is a data problem, not a clean result.', which is FALSE under version skew and fires on every run until someone rebuilds and redeploys.

title: Backport webui#338: fork-PR resolution in the Tier-3 review is broken (belongs to IT-9)
detail:
BELONGS TO IT-9 (trg-bd66b9b0), which holds exclusive ownership of everything under the workflows directory. This card RECORDS the finding only - the change itself must be executed as part of IT-9, not as a competing card. Triage has no amend primitive (append/status only), which is why this is a separate append rather than an edit of IT-9.

FINDING. Stage 2 of the Tier-3 PR review resolves the pull request from the head SHA via the "commits/{sha}/pulls" endpoint. That endpoint returns an EMPTY list for a pull request raised from a fork, because the commit lives in the fork's object store, not the base repository's. Consequence: every fork PR fails to resolve, the step exits non-zero, and the required PR Review context is posted as a failure - permanently red, and never actually reviewed. That is the precise case the two-stage split was built for, inverted into an availability regression that no same-repo PR would ever reveal.

VERIFIED, NOT ARGUED. Probed against three real fork pull requests on cli/cli: all three return an empty list from "commits/{sha}/pulls" and all three resolve correctly by listing the base repository's open pull requests and matching on head.sha.

FIX ALREADY EXISTS DOWNSTREAM. shipwright-webui PR #338 ports this workflow and ships the corrected resolve step, paginated, plus a fork case in its executed test suite. Port that form back rather than re-deriving it. Origin: webui#338, doubt-reviewer finding 26, recorded in its iterate spec 2026-07-31-two-stage-pr-review.

reason: Annotation, NOT a state change - status deliberately re-asserted as triage so IT-9 keeps its current state. Cross-reference: trg-94e71021 (Backport webui#338: fork-PR resolution in the Tier-3 review is broken) BELONGS TO THIS CARD. It records a high-severity availability bug in .github/workflows/pr-review-run.yml and explicitly defers execution to IT-9, because IT-9 holds exclusive ownership of everything under the workflows directory. DO NOT CLOSE IT-9 WITHOUT RESOLVING trg-94e71021 - otherwise that card is orphaned and whoever picks it up next would touch a workflow file outside IT-9, which is what the exclusivity rule exists to prevent. Written this way because the triage model has no card-to-card relation field and no amend primitive: a status event with an unchanged status is the only way to attach a note to an existing card without misstating its state.

All four Weg-B items built: the release stages the seven documents and verifies the COMMIT carries the stamp; --refresh-pr opens a docs-only PR in between under the operator's own gh login; the Source-State banner names base= and release=; guide.md says what is current and how to refresh it. It is closed because it is FIXED and shipped in PR #512 (95f39078): the remedy resolves the branch merge-base instead of HEAD~1, and prints words rather than a wrong --source when no base resolves or the commit is already on the trunk. The test EXECUTES the printed command and re-runs the gate.

title: P1.01 [AUTO] Fleet sub-iterates run without the external plan review
detail: BLOCKS Phase 2. The sub-iterate-runner classifies exactly once, at Step 2, from the spec text, before any code exists. classify() takes (message, sync_config_path, project_root) - no file list, no diff - and its docstring notes Stage 2 (repo scout) may upgrade, which the runner never reaches. Every diff-driven risk flag is therefore structurally unable to fire in campaign mode: cross_component, touches_ci_supplychain, and the file-pattern halves of touches_io_boundary / touches_build. Combined with the #506 fall-through cap, fleet units land at small with no flags, and Step 3.5 (mandatory medium+) is a GUARANTEED skip - the highest-yield gate measured at 0.94 unique HIGH findings per run over 66 records. Step 3.7 has an escape hatch (medium+ OR risk flag OR diff > 100 LOC) that 3.5 lacks. NOT a flag: there is no --complexity CLI option and no env override (verified, 0 hits). Recommended fix (a): mirror Step 3.7's trigger onto Step 3.5 in agents/sub-iterate-runner.md - the plan review already runs after Build, so the diff is available. Option (b) diff-driven re-check needs a classify() parameter that does not exist; option (c) an env var lifts every gate. Option (d) seeding scope keywords into specs is FORBIDDEN by SKILL.md:96. NOTE: brief section 4 still carries a stale 'pin --complexity medium' label from an earlier draft - section 1 is authoritative. Operator decision required. Evidence: Spec/fleet-preconditions-brief.md sections 1-2.

title: P1.03 [SERIAL 1/3] F0 tests on Python 3.13 while CI tests on 3.11
detail: Largest single CI failure class: of 22 sampled CI failures over 3.4 days, 9 were 'Run plugin tests' and 4 'Run shared tests'. Root cause verified at 95f39078: run_test_suite.py:99 build_command() emits 'uv run --with pytest --with pytest-mock ...' with NO --python, and the repo carries no .python-version (git ls-files -> 0). Each plugin venv therefore resolves its own interpreter (14 plugins on 3.13.13, one on 3.12.13) while every workflow pins 3.11. Correction to prior lore: the ROOT resolves 3.11.15 - the drift has moved into the plugin venvs, so this is not the old 'local 3.12 vs CI 3.11' note. Change: add --python 3.11 in build_command plus a root .python-version. SEQUENCING: do NOT run concurrently with trg-348386e4 (suite_report.py + junit) - different files, same subsystem. LANDMINE: a fresh worktree needs 'uv sync --extra dev'; if pinning triggers a re-resolve it surfaces as an F0 infra fault, not a test failure - do not weaken the runner's junit-report-exists heuristic that separates those two cases. Do NOT parallelise CI to close the gap: test_f0_ci_parity.py::test_ci_stays_SERIAL forbids it by design. Evidence: Spec/fleet-preconditions-brief.md sections 2 and 6.

title: P2.01 [SERIAL 2/3 after P1.03] Diff-coverage gate has no local equivalent
detail: 5 of 22 sampled CI failures were 'Diff coverage (gate)'. The gate exists only in CI, so it can only fail after a push. NO ci.yml CHANGE NEEDED, therefore NO IT-9 COLLISION: the gate is already extracted to .github/actions/diff-coverage-gate/action.yml, whose own description puts coverage PRODUCTION on the caller in an earlier step. Change: the F0 suite runner emits cobertura per unit, combine, then 'uvx diff-cover==10.3.0 --fail-under 80' against the merge-base. Pin the version - CI pins it and an unpinned local run would disagree. Keep the CI step as backstop. READ THE LANDMINES BEFORE IMPLEMENTING (brief section 6): (1) subprocess tests measure 0 percent in diff-coverage because the code runs in another process, so adding this locally will red-flag well-tested hook code - add in-process tests of the decision function alongside, and when monkeypatching patch the MODULE OBJECT, never the dotted string, per ADR-045. (2) Test roots do not compose: the repo-root conftest.py hard-refuses a multi-root pytest invocation (exit 4, ADR-044), so one root per invocation, one --cov per root, merge afterwards - mirror what ci.yml already does across plugin / shared / integration steps rather than collapsing them. (3) 'pytest -m' on the command line OVERRIDES addopts rather than intersecting; compose the full expression. This is a PERMANENT addition to F0, not transitional: the trade is ~2 min local against the 1.18 extra CI cycles per branch observed at a 29 percent failure rate, which land after the iterate reports done. Evidence: Spec/fleet-preconditions-brief.md sections 2, 3 and 6.

title: P2.08 [AUTO] Three surface gates run only in CI (verify_local.py)
detail: 2 of 22 sampled CI failures were 'Sweep delivery surface (gate)'. Build one local entry point (verify_local.py) that drives scripts/verify_contract_surface.py, scripts/verify_sweep_delivery_surface.py and shared/scripts/tools/check_ci_gate_coverage.py before push. NEW FILE - file-disjunct from all ten existing Phase 2 units, so it parallelises cleanly. LANDMINE (brief section 6): import the three checkers carefully. An eager 'from lib.X import ...' outside lib/ resolves differently under the plugin-vs-shared root split (ADR-045) - green at F0, red in CI. A lazy import only defers WHICH lib binds; it does not make it safe. Note that scripts/verify_contract_surface.py is currently wired to nothing, which is also a loose end in the IT-9 anchor. Evidence: Spec/fleet-preconditions-brief.md sections 2 and 6.

title: P1.05 [AUTO] F11 spec-impact gate reads one commit, so it false-fails after integration
detail: Measured in iterate-2026-07-31-it1-s2-expected-status. check_spec_impact_recorded resolves the changed-path set from the SINGLE commit passed as --commit, while its siblings (integration coverage, derived-snapshot, cross-layer) read merge-base..HEAD via git_helpers._iterate_changed_paths. F11 runs ensure_current BEFORE verifying, by design, so HEAD is then the integration MERGE commit whose own path set holds only the conflict-resolved files - 4 paths here, vs 36 in the range. The gate reported 'touched no spec.md and recorded no spec_impact=none' for a run whose iterate commit did touch spec.md, and passed only when re-run against the pre-merge commit. Same class as the defect #493 fixed for the other gates; this one was not converted. Fix: route it through the same range resolver.

title: P1.06 [AUTO] Path-canon lint false-positives on any hyphenated dirname
detail: Measured in iterate-2026-07-31-it1-s2-expected-status. The Layer-1 canon patterns in shared/scripts/lib/artifact_migrations.py use the negative lookbehind (?<![\w/.\]) before each legacy dirname. That set covers word chars, forward slash, dot and backslash - but NOT the hyphen. So a path under a hyphenated directory whose name ENDS in a migrated dirname reads as a bare legacy reference: 'plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/x.py' matches the 'compliance/' pattern and is reported as a legacy path. Probed directly: the pattern returns True for 'plugins/shipwright-compliance/tests/x.py' and 'shipwright-compliance/tests', False for '.shipwright/compliance/dashboard.md'. It fired on this run's F5c entry, which is the first agent_docs/iterates JSON to cite a compliance-plugin test; a JSON artifact cannot carry the inline suppression marker, so the only outs are the allowlist or rewording. Worked around here by rewording. Also applies to agent_docs, designs and planning. Fix: add the hyphen to the lookbehind class, or anchor on a path separator.

reason: Delivered with PR #509. should_route_to_outbox in shared/scripts/triage.py now carries condition (3) 'NEVER under CI' and names this card in its docstring, with the rationale in lib.ci_env. A card filed from a GitHub runner no longer lands in the gitignored outbox.

Re-homed to trg-a678bd00 (Adopt Automerge-Readiness). Rung 3 is unreachable here: main is protected and self-merge only runs on an UNPROTECTED base. The exposure is on consumer repos without protection. Exercise it there with a throwaway repo.

title: P2.04 [AUTO] Capture dirtiness before the producer writes, not after
detail: Split out of anchor trg-ac4fc684 (which superseded trg-4bbbd233 after PR #490 delivered four of six parts). LANDMINE: a dirty flag was built for this and WITHDRAWN before commit after two review rounds - do not rebuild it. Why the obvious implementation fails, measured: every automatic producer writes TRACKED files before the snapshot is emitted, so a dirtiness measurement at emit time reads true on a pristine tree (four cases evidenced, one reproduced end-to-end with dirty=true and zero uncommitted source). An exclusion list was rejected in review: hanging it off DERIVED_SNAPSHOTS is structurally wrong because that register deliberately keeps the event log and triage.jsonl OUT, and the two registers answer different questions. Correct approach: capture dirtiness BEFORE the producer starts writing and pass it through. The seam source_state.py already models this with a run-id-primary stamp, and source_state_git.resolve_git_state has already solved the sibling path-relativisation problem - reuse, do not rebuild.

title: P2.05 [AUTO] grade_snapshot emission: 83 percent of lines carry nothing new
detail: Split out of anchor trg-ac4fc684. Measured: shipwright_events.jsonl held 587 lines, 172 of them grade_snapshot (29 percent), across 16 distinct grade/score values with only 29 transitions in 16 days. On 2026-07-27 alone, 35 snapshots from 15 different sessions, each identical, one with an empty session field. The emitter documents its no-dedup decision deliberately and delegates dedup to the WebUI on the premise that a regen is an explicit act - 15 sessions in one day falsifies that premise.

title: P2.16 [GUIDED] An unreadable run config reads as standalone
detail: Split out of anchor trg-040223fe. _read_standalone_flag treats an unparseable config like a missing one and answers standalone. title: P2.21 [AUTO after trg-e4156151] review_record: accept a well-formed unknown reviews key
detail: validate_record rejects any reviews key outside REVIEW_TYPES. That rule was justified by 'strictness protects the mirror', and the mirror stopped rejecting strangers when the webui shipped its tolerant reader - so the premise is repealed while the conclusion stands.
