title: check_ci_supplychain_ack still uses the binary git probe, so a git fault inside a repo green-SKIPs it
detail:
DEFERRED OUT OF iterate-2026-08-01-coverage-gate-recompute-order ON PURPOSE (scope), recorded so it has an owner.

FINDING. `shared/scripts/tools/verifiers/ci_supplychain.py` opens with `rc, _, _ = _run_git(project_root, 'rev-parse', '--git-dir'); if rc != 0: return SKIP`. Any non-zero rc is read as 'not a git repository'. But a broken git binary, a `safe.directory` / dubious-ownership refusal, a permission failure, corrupt repo metadata, or a timeout all return non-zero from INSIDE a real repository — so the CI supply-chain acknowledgement gate green-SKIPs on an infrastructure fault, at every complexity, in the one gate whose whole purpose is that a complexity floor must not be a dodge. This is the exact fail-open class that iterate-2026-08-01-coverage-gate-recompute-order removed from check_integration_coverage and check_removal_coverage.

THE FIX ALREADY EXISTS. That change extracted the tri-state classifier to `git_helpers.git_context()` (work_tree | not_git | git_error), which is locale-independent (it does NOT rely on English stderr — git ships gettext translations) and fail-closed on anything it cannot definitively call a non-repo. ci_supplychain is the third caller it was extracted for and the only one not migrated. Roughly 6 lines: swap the probe, SKIP on not_git, ERROR on anything that is not work_tree.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE IN THAT RUN. Migrating it changes the behaviour of a third gate that the card did not verify and the operator did not scope in — a run may claim only what it does. The docstring in ci_supplychain.py now carries an explicit NOTE describing this hole so a reader is not misled in the meantime.

TEST TO WRITE ALONGSIDE: mirror `test_a_localized_non_repo_answer_is_still_not_a_git_error` and `test_git_timeout_is_a_git_error_not_a_missing_repo` from shared/tests/test_check_integration_coverage_infra.py.

title: iterate_entry readers do not catch UnicodeDecodeError, so a non-UTF-8 entry file crashes F11
detail:
DEFERRED OUT OF iterate-2026-08-01-coverage-gate-recompute-order ON PURPOSE (scope), recorded so it has an owner.

FINDING. `shared/scripts/lib/iterate_entry.py` reads entry files and the legacy run config with `path.read_text(encoding='utf-8')` inside `except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError)`. UnicodeDecodeError is a ValueError subclass and is caught by NEITHER arm. So a non-UTF-8 `.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.json` (a write torn mid-multibyte-sequence, or a cp1252 editor save) propagates out of `find_entry_by_run_id`. `verify_iterate_finalization.main` has no try/except around `run_all_checks`, so F11 exits with a traceback and the operator loses the report for ALL checks, not just the one that raised.

PRE-EXISTING and FAIL-CLOSED (non-zero exit, never a false pass), which is why it was not fixed inline. The sibling reader in `verifiers/_iterate_latest.py:85` already catches UnicodeDecodeError for exactly this reason, so the intended posture is settled — the two readers simply disagree.

FIX: add UnicodeDecodeError to both except tuples in iterate_entry.py (the corrupt-file skip path already exists and logs a warning), with a test seeding a non-UTF-8 entry file and asserting the reader skips it rather than raising. Surfaced by the Stage-3 doubt review of iterate-2026-08-01-coverage-gate-recompute-order, which disproved a comment in integration_coverage.py asserting the reader 'never raises'; that comment now states the real invariant.

title: P1.09 [AUTO] llm_review reports a truncated external review as success
detail:
Found at the end of iterate-2026-08-01-coverage-gate-recompute-order (session 63420439), after all three Gemini calls in that run came back degraded - twice truncated, once empty. The diagnosis is MEASURED, not assumed, and the conclusion was explicitly NOT to swap the model.

TWO BUGS, ONE MECHANISM.

(1) THE SILENT FAIL-OPEN - this is the dangerous half. lib/llm_review.py never inspects finish_reason and returns a cut-off answer as status: "success". So half a review counts as a clean pass on the gate the fleet-preconditions brief measured as the HIGHEST yield of any pass: 0.94 unique HIGH findings per run over 66 records, ahead of doubt (0.53), external_code (0.20) and code (0.18). The classifier it needs ALREADY EXISTS in the sibling lib/external_review_degraded.py (_TRUNCATED_FINISH_REASONS, openai_finish_reason, gemini_finish_reason) and tools/external_review.py uses it correctly. The two paths simply disagree - the same producer-vs-checker shape as P1.08 and P2.22.

(2) THE BUDGET. max_tokens is hard-coded to 4096 at four call sites: external_review.py:157 and :189, llm_review.py:64 and :95 (the gpt-5.x arms use max_completion_tokens for the same value). Reasoning tokens count against that ceiling. Probed on a TRIVIAL prompt: Gemini burned 2234 of 2823 completion tokens - 79 percent - on internal reasoning, leaving about 589 for the visible answer. Against a real prompt (a 108k-char diff plus a demand for a long structured review) the reasoning burn eats the whole ceiling. That is exactly the observed progression: cut off after ~500 visible chars, then further, then EMPTY. One mechanism explains all three failures. GPT-5.6-terra never truncated at the same cap because it reasons less per call - not because it reviews better.

DO NOT SWAP THE MODEL. Gemini 3.6 Flash would fit the limit by thinking less, which is an argument against 4096, not an argument for Flash - it trades review quality to dodge a budget bug. GLM 5.2 would additionally reverse a settled decision (external review = GPT + Gemini, Codex by exception only); if that is ever revisited it must be a quality-driven decision on its own, not a truncation workaround.

FIX, all four sites plus the detector:
  * raise the budget at external_review.py:157,189 and llm_review.py:64,95 - fixing one path is not enough, llm_review.py is a separate path carrying the same limit (the it5 lesson: a gate with two surfaces must be widened on both);
  * bound reasoning EXPLICITLY rather than only raising the total - OpenRouter accepts extra_body={"reasoning": {"max_tokens": N}} - otherwise the thinking share simply scales with the new ceiling;
  * make llm_review.py call the existing degraded-classifier so a truncated reply can never be status success;
  * consider pinning the two paths together with a drift test, the way this repo pins detector tuples.

VERIFICATION (measurable, do not take on faith): repeat the real code-review call against this same diff and log finish_reason plus reasoning_tokens before and after.

PHASE NOTE. Filed as P1 because the failure is SILENT and it is live: P1.07 is cross_component and therefore medium, so it invokes this path, and P1.01 already hit it. Counter-argument for demoting to P2, stated so the choice is informed: most P2 units classify small, where the phase matrix skips external review entirely.

title: P1.10 [AUTO] Serialize the ensure_shared_cache SessionStart fan-out (12 concurrent copiers)
detail:
ensure_shared_cache is vendored into 12 plugins and Claude Code fires SessionStart from every hook-bearing plugin with no active-plugin filter, so all 12 run per session. Since iterate-2026-08-01-cache-heal-per-plugin each invocation walks both sides of both cache trees (~4400 entries, measured ~200ms), so the steady-state cost is 12x that. More importantly, when a repair IS needed all 12 reach the same verdict and copy onto the same destination concurrently (copyfile truncates, no temp+rename) while sibling hooks in other plugins' SessionStart arrays import from that same tree. The previous sentinel check was ~1 stat, so the fan-out was free and concurrent copying was nearly impossible; a completeness check makes it the normal path. The repo already has the pattern for this (lib.event_once.claim_once, used to close the same non-atomic-write window for a single JSON file); a stdlib-only O_EXCL claim keyed on the SessionStart payload's session_id would work without importing from shared/. Belongs with the hook fan-out / consolidation work rather than inside one of 12 vendored copies of one hook. Raised by the Stage-3 doubt review.

PHASE NOTE (placed 2026-08-01). Filed as P1.10 because P1.07 (iterate-2026-08-01-cache-heal-per-plugin) is what made this the NORMAL path: the previous sentinel check was ~1 stat, so the fan-out was free and concurrent copying nearly impossible. With a completeness check, every repair now has 12 processes reaching the same verdict and copying onto the same destination with copyfile (truncates, no temp+rename) while sibling hooks in other plugins' SessionStart arrays import from that same tree. The hazard is conditional on a repair being needed - i.e. exactly the reap scenario P1.07 exists to serve - and it is live while a parallel fleet is running. title: P2.24 [AUTO after P1.07+P1.08] Version ordering treats a SemVer prerelease as newer than its release
detail:
Both scripts/cache_tree_compare.version_key and its stdlib-only mirror in the ensure_shared_cache hook parse the leading MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH as ints and keep any suffix as a plain string tail. That makes 1.0.0-rc1 sort AFTER 1.0.0, because '-rc1' > '' as a string, so a prerelease would be picked as the newest installed version. SemVer says the opposite: a release outranks all prereleases of the same numeric version. Consequences differ per caller: latest_cache_version_dir would report the prerelease as the cache's current version, and since iterate-2026-08-01-cache-heal-per-plugin the self-heal hook would additionally treat the prerelease's contents as the AUTHORITY on whether the mirror is complete and overwrite a mirror built from the stable version. Not reachable today - every installed plugin in the live cache carries a plain MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH version and only one version each - so this is latent, not live. Deliberately NOT fixed inside the healer alone: the hook's key is pinned equal to the shared helper by test, and changing one side only would break that pin and split the convention. A fix belongs in cache_tree_compare.version_key with the hook's mirror and the pin updated together, plus a case covering 1.0.0-rc1 vs 1.0.0. Raised by the external code review (openai).

SEQUENCING (placed 2026-08-01). Needs BOTH P1.07 (trg-72457428, the vendored hook) and P1.08 (trg-70e5a385, the shared version resolver) merged first - the fix has to change cache_tree_compare.version_key, the hook's stdlib-only mirror and the test that pins the two equal, all in one diff, and both of those files are being edited right now. Latent, not live: every installed plugin in the current cache carries a plain MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH and only one version each.

title: P4.02 [GUIDED] grade_snapshot dirty: the orchestrator's sibling-process residual
detail: Left open deliberately by iterate-2026-08-01-grade-snapshot-dirty-capture, which shipped grade_snapshot.dirty captured before the producer writes. The capture travels through the environment, so it reaches DESCENDANTS of the capturer. In a pipeline run the phase's own record_event.py is a SIBLING subprocess of the later compliance regen, not an ancestor, so its single tracked append to the event log can still be counted as tree dirt and stamp dirty=true on an otherwise pristine tree. Not the reproduced case (that was the iterate finalize_iterate chain, now fixed and pinned end-to-end). Both obvious closures were considered and rejected in the shipping run: capturing at pipeline-run start is stale by the time a later phase legitimately edits source, and a durable run-scoped store was dropped on reducibility grounds after external review (it needed five defensive mechanisms to serve a consumer that was measured not to exist). A fix likely needs the orchestrator to capture at each phase boundary, after the phase's source work and before its bookkeeping writes - a seam that does not cleanly exist today. Consumer impact is bounded: dirty=true is the conservative direction, so a consumer that excludes dirty points loses a point rather than trusting a false one.

Needs its own basis/verdict semantics per ADR-120.

title: P2.27 [GUIDED after P2.08] Decide how verify_local.py gets run: pre-push hook, F0 step, or manual
detail:
verify_local.py mirrors ci.yml's three bespoke merge guards locally, but nothing invokes it: no hook, no SKILL.md step, no F-phase, no workflow. It runs only when a human types it. The failures it targets came from iterate runs, and agents execute steps rather than CLAUDE.md prose, so the round-trip tail it was built to remove is unchanged until someone remembers. Needs an operator decision because each option changes behaviour beyond this card's scope. Option A: scripts/hooks/pre-push (core.hooksPath already points at scripts/hooks/, pre-commit already lives there; repo-scoped by construction so it cannot leak into consumer projects) - but a blocking pre-push can stop a legitimate push, including a repair push, and the constitution forbids --no-verify. Option B: same hook, advisory only (print and exit 0) - never blocks, but the push has already happened by then. Option C: an F0 step guarded on the file existing, so it no-ops in consumer projects - F0 lives in plugins/shipwright-iterate and ships to end users, while this script is monorepo-only. Left unwired deliberately: installing a hook changes how every push in the repo behaves and is the operator's call, not an autonomous one.

SEQUENCING (placed 2026-08-01). Blocked on P2.08 (trg-bb554cb9, worktree verify-local-surface-gates) - verify_local.py has to exist before its wiring can be decided. GUIDED because each option changes behaviour beyond the card: a blocking pre-push can stop a legitimate repair push while the constitution forbids --no-verify (A), an advisory hook fires after the push already happened (B), and an F0 step lives in a plugin that ships to end users while this script is monorepo-only (C).

title: Two F11 readers tail-fall-back to the previous run when this run's entry is unreadable
detail:
FOUND BY the Stage-3 doubt review of iterate-2026-08-01-fail-closed-reader-migration; deferred out of it because closing the hole changes three checks the card did not scope.

FINDING. spec_checks._read_iterate_entry and iterate_compliance._latest_iterate_entry both end with 'return entries[-1]' when the requested run_id is not found. So when a run's own entry file is unreadable and the merged reader skips it, these two do NOT see 'absent' - they hand back the most recent OTHER run's entry. Downstream, check_s9_readme_freshness and check_s10_claude_md_sync branch on the inherited 'category', and check_w2_external_review_marker branches on the inherited 'complexity', so a medium feature run whose entry is corrupt can have three checks stand down on a previous small change run's data. Fail-open, and silent.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT INTRODUCED by that run: measured both ways - a malformed-JSON entry already produced the substitution before the change, because the reader has always skipped that class. The UnicodeDecodeError fix merely routes one more corruption class into the same pre-existing fallback (previously it crashed F11 outright, losing all 20 checks, which was strictly worse).

The behaviour is pinned as-is by test_a_corrupt_entry_substitutes_the_previous_run_in_tail_fallback_readers in shared/tests/test_iterate_entry_encoding.py, which asserts the fail-OPEN direction deliberately so that closing the hole FAILS that test and forces the prose to be updated with it.

FIX SHAPE: make the two tail fallbacks corruption-aware - either have the reader expose which run_ids it skipped, or have the callers distinguish 'no entry for this run' from 'no entries at all'. A sentinel-run_id guard for the same hazard already exists at verifiers/_iterate_run_id.py:30-36 and is the natural place to extend.

title: P2.26 [AUTO after P2.22] _git_available still uses the binary probe, so five callers keep the conflation
detail:
FOUND BY the Stage-3 doubt review of iterate-2026-08-01-fail-closed-reader-migration; the natural next card in the same family.

FINDING. git_helpers._git_available is still the binary 'rc == 0' probe and carries exactly the conflation the tri-state git_context was extracted to remove: a broken git binary, a safe.directory / dubious-ownership refusal, a permission failure or a wedged index.lock all return non-zero from INSIDE a real repository and are read as 'git unavailable'.

It is not dead code. Five live call sites: iterate_checks.py:950, spec_checks.py:336 (S4), :611 (S9), :704 (S10), and _layer_coverage_regen.py:275. The first guards check_spec_impact_recorded, an F11 ERROR gate, which returns a green SKIP ('skipped (git unavailable - cannot inspect the branch)') on an infrastructure fault - the same fail-open shape that was just removed from check_ci_supplychain_ack, check_integration_coverage and check_removal_coverage.

CONTEXT. iterate-2026-08-01-fail-closed-reader-migration migrated the THIRD and last git_context consumer, and its prose originally claimed the family no longer held contradictory decisions about what a git fault means. The doubt review disproved that: the claim is true only of the three git_context consumers, and the docstrings in ci_supplychain.py and integration_coverage.py were corrected to say so explicitly and to name this card's subject as still outstanding.

FIX SHAPE: migrate each of the five callers to git_context with the settled posture (SKIP on not_git, refuse on anything that is not work_tree), then delete _git_available. Each call site needs its own judgement about whether its current SKIP should become an ERROR or stay a SKIP, which is why this is a card and not a mechanical rename. Mirror the tests in shared/tests/test_check_ci_supplychain_infra.py.

SEQUENCING (placed 2026-08-01). Blocked on P2.22 (trg-eba97569, worktree fail-closed-reader-migration), which is migrating the third git_context consumer right now and touches the same helper family. NOTE THE FLEET RELEVANCE: a wedged .git/index.lock is one of the named triggers, and it is far more likely than usual while ~18 worktrees run concurrently - so the green SKIP on check_spec_impact_recorded is not a theoretical path this week.

title: P2.28 [AUTO after P2.05] record_event by-commit dedup is not type-scoped, unlike the grade branch
detail:
append_event_idempotent's deduplicate_by_commit branch is gated only on the presence of a commit field and consults has_commit(), which searches for work_completed events. A grade_snapshot recorded via the CLI with --commit and --deduplicate-by-commit is therefore skipped as a duplicate_commit whenever any work_completed shares that sha. title: P1.15 [CAMPAIGN][PARALLEL] Replace full iterate startup read of shipwright_events.jsonl with bounded relevant context
detail:
PROBLEM
Every iterate can load the complete shipwright_events.jsonl into LLM startup context. The canonical log grows without bound, while relevance is area- and change-dependent. This spends tokens before the agent knows what it is working on and has become an operator usage blocker. The raw log itself is not the defect; treating it as an undifferentiated prompt is.

SETTLED ARCHITECTURE
Keep shipwright_events.jsonl as the complete append-only source of truth. Deterministic consumers continue to read it directly. LLM consumers receive a bounded, relevance-ranked event bundle only after Repo Scout identifies changed files and likely areas. Event content is untrusted data, never instructions. The full log remains an explicit diagnostic fallback, not the normal prompt.

SEQUENCE — do not collapse the safety barriers
A. FOUNDATION + SHADOW
- Define one canonical area catalog and one producer contract. shipwright-adopt creates it for brownfield repos.
- Existing repos without a catalog must not hit a wall: use a documented fail-soft ladder based on changed files/path ownership, then bounded recent/global events, with visible provenance and warnings.
- Build a derived, disposable index from shipwright_events.jsonl; it must be fully rebuildable and must never become a second source of truth.
- Add a query surface supporting at least areas, changed files, event types, deterministic ordering, provenance, hard result/token limits, and explicit truncation.
- Preserve all current startup behaviour in this unit. In shadow mode, compute the bundle that would have been supplied and record its size without letting it affect agent behaviour.

B. COMPACT SWITCH
- After shadow evidence is valid, make the bounded query bundle the default LLM event context after Repo Scout.
- Remove the unconditional full raw-log startup read for LLM consumers only.
- Keep explicit full-log fallback and record every fallback/truncation. A missing/stale catalog or index must degrade visibly and usefully, never silently omit all context.
- Pin full/shadow/compact modes so rollback and comparison are possible.

C. TEMPORARY MEASUREMENT + REMOVAL
- During the experiment write machine data to .shipwright/compliance/context-cost/events-context-metrics.jsonl and a regenerated human report to .shipwright/compliance/context-cost/events-context-report.md.
- Record per iterate: mode, full event count/bytes/estimated tokens, selected count/bytes/tokens, query count, truncations, fallbacks, and reduction percentage. These artifacts must never be startup context.
- After 5-10 stable compact iterates, judge reduction, fallbacks, missing-context incidents, and review quality. Then delete both measurement artifacts and temporary collection/reporting machinery. Keep only product behaviour, tests, runtime warnings, and optionally an on-demand --stats diagnostic. Do not retain an experiment-history document.

ACCEPTANCE
- Raw event history and deterministic consumers are unchanged.
- Index rebuild produces deterministic equivalent query results.
- Area catalog exists after adopt; absent/stale catalog follows the tested fail-soft ladder.
- Query output is bounded, deterministic, provenance-bearing, truncation-visible, and prompt-injection-safe.
- Compact mode no longer places the full events log in normal LLM startup context.
- Full fallback is explicit and measurable.
- The Markdown report shows latest run and rolling comparison plainly to the operator.
- Temporary telemetry has an executable cleanup criterion and is removed after the observation window.

Primary design brief: Spec/context-cost-report.md. This card is independent of the Claude local read-tool batching experiment and may run in parallel with the current CI/iterate work, but its own A -> B -> C barriers are serial.

title: P1.17 [AUTO after P1.15/P1.16][MEASURE-FIRST] Attribute iterate review and remediation wall-clock before optimizing it
detail:
PROBLEM
The coarse Iterate-Rail review phase currently accounts for a median 55.2 minutes and 53.9% of comparable iterate wall-clock. That bucket combines pre-F0 browser/E2E validation, self-review, spec review, code review, doubt review, external review, reviewer waits, and remediation. The aggregate establishes review as the strongest measured candidate, but it does not identify which work is responsible. Optimizing before attribution risks weakening required review while leaving the actual bottleneck unchanged.

IMPLEMENTATION
- Add additive, best-effort timing spans for pre_f0_validation, self_review, spec_review, code_review, doubt_review, external_review, and remediation.
- Record reviewer spawn versus follow-up, active/wait duration, remediation round, outcome, and invalidation-driven restart where known.
- Preserve the mandatory spec -> code -> conditional doubt cascade and all external-review triggers unchanged.
- Do not add follow-up limits, caching, fingerprint reuse, or review invalidation behaviour in this item. This action-unit measures only.
- Do not record prompts, findings, source contents, or other unbounded or sensitive payloads.

STORAGE CONTRACT
- Write transient marks to the gitignored per-run sidecar .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.review_timings.jsonl.
- At F5b, validate and fold normalized spans into the existing durable work_completed event as work_completed.review_timings.
- The durable machine-readable source of truth remains the root shipwright_events.jsonl. Do not create another permanent metrics JSONL.
- Generate the human-readable derived report at .shipwright/compliance/performance/review-throughput.md.
- The report must be reproducible entirely from completed events, must never become agent startup context, and must clearly identify incomplete or pre-instrumentation runs.

REPORT
For the latest run and rolling comparable runs, show total iterate duration; duration and percentage per review subphase; reviewer spawns and follow-ups per stage; reviewer wait versus remediation time; remediation-round count; invalidation-driven restarts; and median/P90 where enough samples exist.

ACCEPTANCE
- A completed iterate can persist normalized review_timings without changing its verdict.
- Missing timing marks never block or alter an iterate.
- Malformed timing data is rejected at the event-write boundary rather than persisted.
- The generated report reproduces its values from shipwright_events.jsonl.
- Existing runs without review_timings remain valid.
- Tests cover span recording, normalization, F5b folding, partial runs, malformed input, and deterministic report generation.
- docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md documents the producer, sidecar, durable event field, report consumer, and lifecycle.
- After at least three normal instrumented runs, the operator decides whether to create a separate optimization item. Do not pre-create that item or claim a time saving from this measurement card.

SEQUENCING
Start after P1.15 and P1.16 are delivered: P1.15 changes iterate context startup and P1.16 changes F0 timing and fleet behaviour, so measuring before both land would establish a moving baseline.

title: P1.17 [AUTO][MEASURE-FIRST] Attribute full iterate wall-clock before optimizing it
detail:
ONE ACTION-UNIT
Instrument the complete Iterate wall-clock in one measurement-only change. Do not split instrumentation by phase and do not optimize any phase in this item.

PROBLEM
The prior coarse analysis identified review as the strongest candidate: median 55.2 minutes and 53.9 percent of comparable Iterate wall-clock. P1.16 then exposed why review-only instrumentation is insufficient. Its canonical scope clock ran 7h55m to work_completed and 9h39m to merge: roughly 4h34m elapsed before external plan review completed, 2h08m in the internal review/remediation region, and 1h12m in post-CI repair. Its final canonical F0 was active for only 5.4 minutes but queued for 18.0 minutes behind a pre-P1.16 weight-22 sibling. Without complete attribution, the largest interval would still be labelled only scope and active execution would remain confused with queueing and external waits.

IMPLEMENTATION
- Add additive, best-effort hierarchical timing spans across the full Iterate lifecycle. Top-level spans must cover discovery_diagnosis, planning, implementation, verification, review, finalization, and delivery.
- Add nested spans where the distinction changes an optimization decision: focused_tests, canonical_f0_active, f0_queue, pre_f0_validation, self_review, spec_review, code_review, doubt_review, external_review, reviewer_wait, remediation, ci_wait, post_ci_remediation, and delivery_wait.
- Give every span a stable name, parent, source, UTC start/end, monotonic duration where the producer is one process, attempt/round where applicable, and outcome of completed, incomplete, cancelled, or unavailable. Never add parent and child durations together; reports show inclusive and exclusive time explicitly.
- Record reviewer spawn versus follow-up, active versus wait time, remediation round, invalidation-driven restart, F0 queue blocker/run weight when already available, CI attempt and conclusion, and whether a retry repeated or changed shape.
- Instrument existing producers at their real boundaries rather than asking the agent to estimate durations after the fact. Preserve current verdicts, gate ordering, retry authority, review cascade, CI requirements, and delivery behavior unchanged.
- Do not add follow-up limits, caching, fingerprint reuse, review skipping, new CI jobs, or timing-based policy decisions. This action-unit measures only.
- Do not record prompts, findings, source contents, console logs, test output, credentials, or other unbounded or sensitive payloads.

STORAGE CONTRACT
- Write transient marks to the gitignored per-run sidecar .shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.iterate_timings.jsonl. The sidecar is resumable and append-only for the live run, but is not a second durable history.
- At F5b, validate and fold normalized spans into the existing durable work_completed event as work_completed.iterate_timings. Reject malformed names, invalid parent relationships, negative durations, impossible ordering, and unbounded fields before persistence.
- The durable machine-readable source of truth remains the root shipwright_events.jsonl. Do not create another permanent metrics JSONL.
- Generate the human-readable derived report at .shipwright/compliance/performance/iterate-throughput.md. It must be reproducible entirely from completed events, must never become agent startup context, and must identify partial and pre-instrumentation runs plainly.

REPORT
For the latest run and rolling comparable runs, show total time to work_completed and delivery; inclusive and exclusive duration and percentage per top-level phase; nested review-stage duration; active test time versus F0 queue time; reviewer active/wait time; remediation rounds; CI active/wait/post-CI remediation time; invalidation-driven restarts; unattributed time; and median/P90 where enough samples exist. Display the timing source and confidence/coverage so missing marks cannot look like zero duration.

ACCEPTANCE
- A completed Iterate persists normalized iterate_timings without changing any verdict, gate, retry, or delivery outcome.
- Top-level exclusive durations plus explicitly reported unattributed time reconcile to the measured wall-clock within a documented tolerance. Nested spans cannot be double-counted.
- F0 queue and active execution are distinguishable, including a synthetic weight-22 blocker case matching the P1.16 rollout shape.
- Review active work, reviewer wait, remediation, CI wait, post-CI remediation, and delivery wait are distinguishable.
- Missing or interrupted marks never block or alter an Iterate and appear as incomplete/unattributed, never zero.
- Malformed timing data is rejected at the event-write boundary rather than persisted. Existing work_completed events without iterate_timings remain valid.
- The generated report reproduces its values deterministically from shipwright_events.jsonl.
- Tests cover span recording, resume, hierarchy normalization, overlap/exclusive-time calculation, F5b folding, partial/cancelled runs, malformed input, F0 queue attribution, CI retry attribution, and deterministic report generation.
- docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md documents every producer boundary, the sidecar, durable event field, report consumer, retention, and failure behavior.
- After at least three normal instrumented runs, the operator decides whether to create separate optimization items. Do not pre-create an optimization item or claim a time saving from this measurement card.

SEQUENCING
P1.15 and P1.16 are delivered. Start from current main so bounded event context and fleet-budget behavior are part of the measured baseline. Do not mix Headroom or another semantic context transformer into the observation runs.

=== MEASURED BASELINE, ADDED 2026-08-04 — READ BEFORE PLANNING ===

DO NOT ASSUME THE EXISTING MARKS ARE A USABLE BASELINE. They are not. Measured against origin/main's shipwright_events.jsonl:

  start          total   scope  build   test review  final
  08-02T19:01     1.65    0.00   0.00   1.65   0.00   0.00
  08-02T21:14     9.24    0.33   0.02   5.26   3.63   0.00
  08-03T06:20     4.56    0.12   0.31   0.00   4.12   0.00
  08-03T16:15     3.36    3.36   0.00   0.00   0.00   0.00
  08-03T19:46    12.08   12.08   0.00   0.00   0.00   0.00
  08-04T05:15     1.80    1.80   0.00   0.00   0.00   0.00
  08-04T06:56     7.92    7.92   0.00   0.00   0.00   0.00
  08-04T10:43     6.60    4.79   0.07   1.30   0.43   0.01

Four of the last five runs recorded exactly ONE span. A test duration of 0.00 on a run that merged a PR means NOT RECORDED, not zero. So 73-100 percent of recent wall-clock is unattributed, and the earlier "review is 53 percent" figure holds only for the 01.08 runs that recorded 4-5 marks. Nobody currently knows where recent iterate time goes.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE GAP — THIS IS THE DESIGN CONSTRAINT, NOT A BUG TO FIX FIRST. plugins/shipwright-iterate/skills/iterate/references/phase-timing.md states it plainly: the iterate flow's phases are LLM-executed SKILL steps, so instead of paired producer events the AGENT emits each boundary mark itself, via `iterate_phase_timing.py mark <group> ... || true`, documented as additive and best-effort with an explicit "a skipped mark just omits that node's bar; never block on it". Nothing is broken. The marks are simply not being emitted, and the completeness varies by run and by agent - one 04.08 run recorded all five while its neighbours recorded one.

WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THIS CARD. The implementation section already says "Instrument existing producers at their real boundaries rather than asking the agent to estimate durations after the fact" - that instinct is correct and is now the load-bearing requirement, not a preference. But the acceptance criterion "Missing or interrupted marks never block or alter an Iterate and appear as incomplete/unattributed, never zero" preserves best-effort semantics, which is exactly the property that produced the table above. Both must hold, so hold them apart deliberately:

  * WHERE A REAL PROCESS BOUNDARY EXISTS, THE PRODUCER STAMPS IT - not the agent. The F0 suite runner already knows its own start/end, lease grant and queue wait; external_review.py and llm_review.py know their own call boundaries; the CI wait and the delivery ladder know theirs; finalize_iterate knows F1. Those spans must not depend on an agent remembering a shell command.
  * ONLY WHERE NO PROCESS OWNS THE BOUNDARY (e.g. entering Build, entering Self-Review) may an agent-emitted mark remain, and there its absence must be reported as UNATTRIBUTED with the reason, never silently omitted.
  * Report coverage per run as a first-class number - how many expected spans were captured - so a degraded run is visibly degraded rather than looking fast.

FIRST FINDING OF THE RUN. Before designing anything, verify the two claims above against the code and the event log, and record which spans can be producer-owned versus which must stay agent-emitted. If that split turns out to be smaller than assumed, say so - a card that only re-implements best-effort marks would reproduce this exact table in a month.

TWO THINGS THE OPERATOR ALREADY RULED OUT AS CAUSES OF THE SLOWDOWN:
  * The F0 host lease is NOT the bottleneck. Weight 22 of capacity 22 is honest, not miscalibrated: 18 discovered units demand roughly 32 (two xdist units at 8, about sixteen at 1) against a budget of 22, so one F0 genuinely saturates the host and serialising siblings is correct. P1.18 was filed on the opposite premise and withdrawn the same day. Do not re-open it.
  * The 34-hour runs of 01.08 were NOT queueing. Eleven runs launched within 45 minutes split bimodally - six at 1.33 to 1.87 hours, six at 33.96 to 48.96 hours, with a 32-hour gap and nothing in between. A FIFO queue produces a gradient, not a gap. Those runs were blocked on something that released for all of them at once. Identifying what that was is squarely in scope here: it is the single largest unexplained interval in the history.

title: P1.18 [AUTO][MEASURE-FIRST] F0 claims the whole host, so sibling worktrees never run tests concurrently
detail:
ONE ACTION-UNIT. Calibrate the F0 host-lease weight so sibling worktrees can run F0 concurrently. Measure first, then set. Do not change the lease mechanism, the xdist allowlist, unit discovery, retry authority, or CI behaviour.

MEASURED 2026-08-04 (this repo, 24-core host):
- suite_host_resources.hardware_cpu_budget() returns cpu_count - 2 = 22.
- normalize_cpu_weight(requested) returns min(requested or capacity, capacity). With requested None it returns the FULL capacity.
- shipwright_test_config.json sets suite.xdist but does NOT set suite.max_workers, so SuiteConfig.max_workers is None.
- Therefore lease_cpu_weight(config) = 22, and f0_cpu_lease takes weight 22 against capacity 22.

CONSEQUENCE. The f0-cpu lease is strict FIFO and repository-keyed across sibling worktrees. A weight of 22 out of 22 means exactly one F0 can hold the lease at a time, so with N parallel worktrees every F0 after the first QUEUES for the full duration of the one ahead of it. The lease is behaving as designed; it is the weight that is uncalibrated. Corroborating measurement already on record in P1.17 (trg-7c94e1ab): a canonical F0 was ACTIVE for 5.4 minutes but QUEUED for 18.0 minutes behind a weight-22 sibling - 77 percent of that F0's wall-clock was queueing, not testing.

WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY "SET IT LOWER". max_workers is the runner's own cross-unit worker budget, so lowering it also lowers INTRA-run parallelism. The trade is single-run latency against fleet throughput, and the crossover depends on how many cores one F0 actually saturates and for how long. That is measurable and must not be guessed.

MEASURE (record the numbers in the run's spec before changing anything):
- Peak and mean concurrent worker processes of ONE F0 run on an otherwise idle host, and its wall-clock.
- The same at two or three candidate max_workers values (e.g. 6, 8, 11), single run.
- Fleet wall-clock for a representative set of sibling worktrees at the current setting versus the best candidate: total time until the LAST sibling finishes, plus per-run active and queued time.
- Whether any unit's own duration degrades disproportionately, especially the two xdist units.

THEN SET. Choose the max_workers that minimises fleet completion time without materially degrading a single run, add it to shipwright_test_config.json's suite block, and state the measured basis in the _comment (that block already documents max_workers as optional and already carries its measured rationale for xdist - follow that form).

LANDMINES:
- shipwright-compliance is DELIBERATELY ABSENT from the xdist allowlist and MUST stay absent: 5 shared-state races under -n 8 that pass 37/37 serially. Never widen the allowlist and never substitute a global -n auto.
- xdist is per-unit fan-out INSIDE a unit; max_workers is the budget ACROSS units. They compose, so a low max_workers with xdist 8 can still oversubscribe. Measure the product, not either alone.
- The two-CPU reserve in hardware_cpu_budget is deliberate host headroom - do not reclaim it.
- Do not weaken the strict-FIFO or crash-safe release behaviour of the lease to buy concurrency.

RELATION TO P1.17. Independent and complementary. P1.17 instruments the FULL iterate wall-clock and must not be mixed into these observation runs. This card touches only the F0 weight. Running this one FIRST is deliberate: it removes a known serialisation so P1.17 measures a fleet that is not artificially single-file. Note the ordering claim is a judgement, not a measurement - if the calibration turns out to be a wash, say so and close it rather than shipping a change that buys nothing.

SCOPE NOTE. This is the smallest available throughput lever, but it is NOT the biggest cost. Phase medians over 10 fully instrumented runs: review 0.96h (53 percent), test 0.35h (19 percent), scope 0.26h, build 0.16h, finalize 0.08h. Test is not the dominant phase; this card buys back queueing, not review time. Do not present it as an iterate-duration fix.

reason: Correct outcome, sharper reason. #549 did NOT set max_workers - it calibrated per-unit weights INSIDE a run. The card premise was still false: weight 22/22 is HONEST. 18 units demand ~32 (2 xdist at 8, ~16 at 1) against budget 22, so one F0 saturates the host and serializing siblings is correct. Do not look for max_workers.

Operator decision: closed on the re-fire contract. Fired 06:28 on 2026-08-04, BEFORE #549 merged at 18:35; no f0-race has fired since. The producer re-files on the next parallel red, so a still-live race returns with fresh evidence. Unit IS xdist-allowlisted.

title: P1.19 [AUTO] Every producer timing span is an orphan, so no run has recorded iterate_timings
detail:
P1.17 (#551, merged 2026-08-05 05:29) delivered correctly and its producer instrumentation WORKS. But eight runs later, ZERO work_completed events carry iterate_timings. Measured 2026-08-05 against main and the live worktrees.

WHAT WORKS. The producer-owned spans write real data to the per-run sidecar. From .worktrees/*/.shipwright/agent_docs/iterates/<run_id>.iterate_timings.jsonl:
  bloat-baseline-vendored-hook: delivery 8.8min, delivery_wait 8.8min, ci_wait 8.7min, canonical_f0_active 4.2min, external_review 3.7min over 4 calls, f0_queue 0.0s, pre_f0_validation 0.0s
  semver-prerelease-sort:       canonical_f0_active 4.9min, external_review 3.3min over 2 calls, f0_queue 53.5s, pre_f0_validation 0.1s

WHAT FAILS. Every one of those spans names a PARENT that is never emitted. Observed parent demand versus presence:
  bloat-baseline-vendored-hook: needs delivery, delivery_wait, planning, review, verification -> only delivery present
  semver-prerelease-sort:       needs planning, review, verification                          -> none present
  risk-recheck-recording-integrity: needs verification                                        -> none present
The seven top-level spans (discovery_diagnosis, planning, implementation, verification, review, finalization, delivery) are AGENT-EMITTED. Only `delivery` ever appears, because deliver_pr.py self-records it as a producer span. So every producer child is an orphan, normalization rejects the tree, and _fold_iterate_timings at finalize_iterate.py:292 folds nothing.

NOT A CACHE OR WIRING PROBLEM - both were checked and are fine. The plugin cache was re-synced at 05:31, two minutes after the merge and hours before the runs finalized (08:13 to 09:16); the cache copy of finalize_iterate.py is byte-identical to the repo; and the fold is wired at line 292 alongside the phase_timings and tests_block folds.

THIS IS THE EXACT FAILURE THE CARD WAS AMENDED TO PREVENT, ONE LEVEL UP. P1.17's own reference file states the principle: it distinguishes producer-owned spans from agent-emitted marks, and says of the old phase_timings that asking the agent to remember mark calls is what broke it. The producers were correctly made self-instrumenting - but they were hung off scaffolding that only an agent can emit, so the same dependency remained, just moved to the parents. Evidence that this is not hypothetical: phase_timings degraded identically, four of five runs recording a single span.

FIX DIRECTION - do not solve it by asking agents to emit the parents. Synthesize a missing ancestor from its children: when a child span names a parent that has no explicit record, materialize that parent from the children's envelope (earliest start, latest end) and mark it derived/incomplete so it is never mistaken for a measured boundary. Report explicitly which top-level spans were measured, which were derived, and which are absent, so coverage stays visible. An agent-emitted parent, when present, must still win over the derived one.

WHY THIS IS P1. Until it is fixed the whole of P1.17 produces nothing: no iterate_timings on any event, and .shipwright/compliance/performance/iterate-throughput.md is never generated. The instrumentation is already paid for; this is the last step that makes it observable.

WHAT THE PARTIAL DATA ALREADY SAYS - carry this into the fix, it is the first real attribution the repo has had:
  * F0 queueing has essentially collapsed: 0.0s and 53.5s, against the 18.0 minutes P1.16 observed. P1.18 was withdrawn on the argument that weight 22 of 22 is honest; this supports that.
  * canonical_f0_active is 4.2 and 4.9 minutes, matching P1.16's 5.4.
  * external_review totals 3.3 to 3.7 minutes across 2 to 4 calls.
  * ci_wait at 8.7 minutes is the single largest measured span, and delivery is almost entirely CI wait.

title: [f0] integration-tests failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
integration-tests: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It is NOT xdist-allowlisted, so this is inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  uv run --python 3.11 --with pytest --with pytest-mock --with pytest-cov pytest integration-tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --cov=shared '--cov-config=C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\iterate-entry-tail-fallback-fail-closed\pyproject.toml' --cov-report=
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run --python 3.11 shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\iterate-entry-tail-fallback-fail-closed' --run-id iterate-2026-08-05-iterate-entry-tail-fallback-fail-closed

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.

title: P2.37 [AUTO] triage_add.py cannot set a launch payload, so 22 of 24 open cards render a producer-bug warning
detail:
Reported by the operator 2026-08-05 from the triage surface: cards render '[!] no launch payload - producer bug; please report'. The surface is right, and the producer is the CLI.

MEASURED 2026-08-05 across the tracked store plus the outbox: of 24 open items, only 2 carry a launchPayload. The 22 without it break down by source as board-split 11, req3-campaign 3, req3-phase2-walk 2, board-normalization 2, and one each from triage-consolidation-2026-07-28, two iterate runs, and github.

ROOT CAUSE, verified at code. The library supports it on both write paths: triage.py:350 and :418 (append_triage_item) and :448 and :534 (append_triage_item_idempotent) accept launch_payload and persist it as the launchPayload field. The renderer expects it: triage_render.py:143 emits the exact warning string. But shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py exposes NO such flag - its argparse surface is only --project-root, --title, --detail, --severity, --kind, --source, --fr-id, --evidence-path, --run-id and --commit. So every card filed through the documented manual CLI is structurally incapable of carrying one, and the surface then correctly reports a producer bug that the operator cannot fix from the command line.

WHY IT MATTERS. The triage board is meant to be a LAUNCH surface, not a findings mirror - an item should be startable from the card. Without the payload the operator has to reconstruct the command by hand for 22 of 24 items, which is exactly the friction the launch surface exists to remove. The two cards that DO carry one (both from automated producers) show the intended shape: '/shipwright-security' and '/shipwright-compliance'.

FIX. Add --launch-payload to triage_add.py and pass it through to the library call. Keep it OPTIONAL - a card with no sensible launch command must stay legal, and the renderer's warning should continue to fire for those rather than being suppressed. Consider whether the default for a manual card should be '/shipwright-iterate <id>', since that is what an operator types for nearly every board item; if so, make it an explicit default rather than a silent one, and let --launch-payload override it.

DO NOT retro-fill the existing 22. They are append events in a git-tracked append-only log; rewriting them is a history edit, and the warning is honest about what those records actually contain. New cards get the field; old ones keep their warning.

SCOPE. shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py plus its tests. File-disjoint from every other open unit. Note the store's own sensitivity rule still applies to whatever goes in the payload: triage is git-tracked and sweeps into a public PR, so the payload must stay neutral - no paths that leak a private tree layout, no secrets.

detail:
Design agreed for issue #547 (carlosgil-ai): add a 4th route 'gateway' alongside openrouter/direct/none in shared/scripts/lib/llm_review.py, config under SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_* (base_url, per-role headers, per-role keys). Default openrouter/direct paths, the model-identity lock, and the DeepSeek ZDR allowlist stay fully unchanged -- Shipwright's own review policy is untouched. The gateway route is additive and operator-owned: no identity lock, no ZDR check on that path, the operator's gateway/virtual key decides which model answers. reviews{} keys for that route use a new generic role pair (model-1/model-2) registered alongside the existing deepseek/openai and historical gemini/openai pairs in review_verdict.SUPPORTED_REVIEWER_SETS, so the verdict/contradiction/marker machinery needs no changes. The actually-answering model (from the API response, where available) is captured as a separate evidence field so the record never implies a specific model that the operator's gateway didn't actually use. First-time contributor (0 merged PRs) on a high-sensitivity shared/ path per CONTRIBUTING.md's graduated trust model -- plan is Shipwright side scaffolds the route + mocked-HTTP tests, carlosgil-ai validates against his real Portkey/WAF setup AFTER merge (see correction below).

=== CORRECTED 2026-08-05 — MERGE-FIRST, AND THE PUBLIC COMMITMENTS ARE BINDING ===

SEQUENCING CHANGED BY THE OPERATOR. The text above says the contributor validates 'before merge'. That is NO LONGER the plan: build it, review it, MERGE it, and the operator informs carlosgil-ai afterwards so he can validate against his real Portkey/WAF setup on main. Do NOT hold the PR open waiting for external validation, and do not disable self-merge on that account.

THE ISSUE COMMENT IS PUBLIC AND SPECIFIC — IT IS NOW A CONTRACT. The maintainer's reply on issue #547 (2026-08-05) names the config surface verbatim. Implement these EXACT names; a different spelling makes a published promise false:

  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL

The rationale given to the contributor: when an egress policy requires all traffic through the gateway, a silent fallback to a direct API call is a policy VIOLATION, not a convenience. title: P2.27 [GUIDED] Decide once how local-only checkers get run: verify_local.py AND check_required_checks.py
detail:
MERGES P2.27 (trg-486cb11c) and P3.03 (trg-304c764b, itself the reduced successor of trg-a089c9f7). One decision, two scripts - answering them separately would leave the repo with two conventions for the same problem.

THE SHARED PROBLEM. Both scripts are built, tested, and invoked by NOTHING - no hook, no SKILL step, no F-phase, no workflow. They run only when a human types them, so the failure class each was built to catch is unchanged until someone remembers.

  * scripts/verify_local.py - mirrors ci.yml's three bespoke merge guards locally. The failures it targets came from iterate runs, and agents execute STEPS rather than CLAUDE.md prose.
  * shared/scripts/tools/check_required_checks.py (+ lib/required_checks_drift.py + 3 test files) - answers 'does the host's must-pass check set match the checks that exist?', and treats an empty must-pass set as a finding rather than an error. Verified 2026-08-05: no caller outside its own module and tests.

THE OPTIONS - each changes behaviour beyond either card, which is why this is guided:
  (A) scripts/hooks/pre-push, BLOCKING. core.hooksPath already points at scripts/hooks/ and pre-commit already lives there, so it is repo-scoped by construction and cannot leak into consumer projects. Cost: a blocking pre-push can stop a legitimate push, including a REPAIR push, and the constitution forbids --no-verify.
  (B) Same hook, ADVISORY - print and exit 0. Never blocks, but by then the push has already happened, which is precisely the round-trip these scripts exist to remove.
  (C) An F0 step guarded on the file existing, so it no-ops in consumer projects. Cost: F0 lives in plugins/shipwright-iterate and SHIPS TO END USERS, while both scripts are monorepo-only.
  (D) Different answers per script - allowed, but then say WHY in the spec, because the default reading will be that one of them was an oversight.

Left unwired deliberately in both delivering runs: installing a hook changes how every push in the repo behaves, and that is the operator's call, not an autonomous one.

LANDMINE, carried from the original P3.03: a check that does NOT run on every PR blocks every PR forever once it is made Required. Verify grade-empirical.yml before promoting anything to must-pass. This only applies if the chosen answer routes check_required_checks into a Required check, which is NOT one of the four options above - it would be a further decision.

SCOPE NOTE. Neither script touches a .github/workflows/ file today, so this does not collide with the remaining IT-9 units (P3.05, P3.06). It WOULD collide if the chosen wiring is a workflow step - if you pick that, sequence it after those two.

title: P2.36 [AUTO] F0 console report dies on a Windows codepage when captured test output is non-cp1252
detail:
SUPERSEDES trg-96a0ac9f - same content, placed in the phase scheme. Raised by iterate-2026-08-05-iterate-timings-derived-parent (P1.19).

FINDING. F0's canonical suite runner prints its final per-unit summary and diagnostics via print(line) to stdout. On a Windows terminal using the cp1252 codepage, a captured test-output tail containing U+FFFD (or any other non-cp1252 character) raises an unhandled UnicodeEncodeError AFTER the suite has already decided pass/fail. The printed report is truncated and the operator sees a raw traceback instead of the summary table. Observed twice while finalizing that run (shared/tests unit, encoding cp1252, position ~52083 and ~10309).

title: P2.37 [AUTO] triage_add.py cannot set a launch payload, so 22 of 24 open cards render a producer-bug warning
detail:
Reported by the operator 2026-08-05 from the triage surface: cards render '[!] no launch payload - producer bug; please report'. The surface is right, and the producer is the CLI.

MEASURED 2026-08-05 across the tracked store plus the outbox: of 24 open items, only 2 carry a launchPayload. The 22 without it break down by source as board-split 11, req3-campaign 3, req3-phase2-walk 2, board-normalization 2, and one each from triage-consolidation-2026-07-28, two iterate runs, and github.

ROOT CAUSE, verified at code. The library supports it on both write paths: triage.py:350 and :418 (append_triage_item) and :448 and :534 (append_triage_item_idempotent) accept launch_payload and persist it as the launchPayload field. The renderer expects it: triage_render.py:143 emits the exact warning string. But shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py exposes NO such flag - its argparse surface is only --project-root, --title, --detail, --severity, --kind, --source, --fr-id, --evidence-path, --run-id and --commit. So every card filed through the documented manual CLI is structurally incapable of carrying one, and the surface then correctly reports a producer bug that the operator cannot fix from the command line.

WHY IT MATTERS. The triage board is meant to be a LAUNCH surface, not a findings mirror - an item should be startable from the card. Without the payload the operator has to reconstruct the command by hand for 22 of 24 items, which is exactly the friction the launch surface exists to remove. The two cards that DO carry one (both from automated producers) show the intended shape: '/shipwright-security' and '/shipwright-compliance'.

FIX. Add --launch-payload to triage_add.py and pass it through to the library call. Keep it OPTIONAL - a card with no sensible launch command must stay legal, and the renderer's warning should continue to fire for those rather than being suppressed. Consider whether the default for a manual card should be '/shipwright-iterate <id>', since that is what an operator types for nearly every board item; if so, make it an explicit default rather than a silent one, and let --launch-payload override it.

HISTORY WAS NOT REWRITTEN, AND MUST NOT BE. On 2026-08-05 the operator chose to re-file the payload-less open cards instead: each original was DISMISSED pointing at a successor that carries a launch payload, using triage.append_triage_item directly since the CLI cannot set the field. No append event was edited. That clears the board without touching the log - but it is a one-off, and it is not a substitute for this fix: without --launch-payload the next manually filed card reproduces the defect immediately.

SCOPE. shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py plus its tests. File-disjoint from every other open unit. Note the store's own sensitivity rule still applies to whatever goes in the payload: triage is git-tracked and sweeps into a public PR, so the payload must stay neutral - no paths that leak a private tree layout, no secrets.

title: P4.02 [GUIDED] grade_snapshot dirty: the orchestrator's sibling-process residual
detail:
Left open deliberately by iterate-2026-08-01-grade-snapshot-dirty-capture, which shipped grade_snapshot.dirty captured before the producer writes. The capture travels through the environment, so it reaches DESCENDANTS of the capturer. In a pipeline run the phase's own record_event.py is a SIBLING subprocess of the later compliance regen, not an ancestor, so its single tracked append to the event log can still be counted as tree dirt and stamp dirty=true on an otherwise pristine tree. Not the reproduced case (that was the iterate finalize_iterate chain, now fixed and pinned end-to-end). Both obvious closures were considered and rejected in the shipping run: capturing at pipeline-run start is stale by the time a later phase legitimately edits source, and a durable run-scoped store was dropped on reducibility grounds after external review (it needed five defensive mechanisms to serve a consumer that was measured not to exist). A fix likely needs the orchestrator to capture at each phase boundary, after the phase's source work and before its bookkeeping writes - a seam that does not cleanly exist today. Consumer impact is bounded: dirty=true is the conservative direction, so a consumer that excludes dirty points loses a point rather than trusting a false one.

title: REQ3.06 [CAMPAIGN AUTONOM] Enforcement-Liste abarbeiten: Checks bauen fuer prompt-only (mechanisable) - Monorepo
detail:
AUTONOME Kampagne. Der Anker, der die Enforcement-Liste des AC-Nachweis-Registers abarbeitet - das Register IST die Arbeitsliste, eine Zeile pro Kriterium, bounded pro Kriterium. GENAU ZWEI Sorten Arbeit gehoeren hierher. (1) 44 Zeilen 'prompt-only (mechanisable)': die Zusage existiert heute NUR als Anweisung in einem Prompt, ein deterministischer Check waere aber moeglich. Erst den CHECK bauen, DANN den Test - es gibt heute nichts zu testen. 39 davon tragen keine Zuordnung. (2) 15 Zeilen 'prompt-only (judgement)': hier ist KEIN Gate erlaubt (Kampagnen-Entscheidung D7 - naiv 98% Flag-Rate, zweckgebaut 0.52-0.66 Praezision, innerhalb von Wochen ignoriert). Die ehrliche Obergrenze ist ein Drift-Test, der prueft, dass die Anweisung noch dasteht. Wer hier ein LLM urteilen laesst, baut genau das, was die Kampagne abgelehnt hat. NICHT hierher: die 10 Zeilen 'enforced, untested' - Mechanismus existiert, nur der Test fehlt, das ist REQ3.05 (trg-137f48b5). Ebenso NICHT die AC-Identitaet, das Manifest, die Bindung und das Keystone-Gate - das ist REQ3.04 (trg-7085d783). Und NICHT die 25 Zeilen 'unimplemented': die bauen die Bereichskarten; sobald eine ausgeliefert ist, wird ihre Zeile 'enforced, untested' und erst dann schuldet REQ3.05 einen Test. ERSTE SUB-ITERATE, Buchhaltung: sieben 'unimplemented'-Zeilen nennen auf der Zeile selbst keine Karte (FR-01.02 #3 und #7, FR-01.03 #3b, FR-01.04 #1 und #4, FR-01.08 #6b, FR-01.15 #6). Einige sind nur in der Prosa zugeordnet - fuer einen Lauf, der Zeilen liest, unsichtbar. Zuordnung pro Zeile explizit machen, bevor irgendetwas gebaut wird, sonst faellt genau das durch, was niemand liest. REIHENFOLGE: laeuft nach den Bereichskarten (deren 'unimplemented' wird sonst waehrend des Laufs zu neuer Arbeit) und ist sauberer nach REQ3.04s AC-Identitaet, weil ein neuer Check dann benennen kann, welches Kriterium er durchsetzt. ABBRUCHBEDINGUNG pro Kriterium: wenn sich beim Bauen zeigt, dass kein deterministisches Orakel existiert, wird die Zeile auf 'judgement' umgestuft und bekommt einen Drift-Test - NICHT ein schwaecheres Gate, das so tut als ob.

title: External review: pluggable LLM gateway route (issue #547) [AUTO][MERGE-FIRST][public config contract]
detail:
Design agreed for issue #547 (carlosgil-ai): add a 4th route 'gateway' alongside openrouter/direct/none in shared/scripts/lib/llm_review.py, config under SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_* (base_url, per-role headers, per-role keys). The gateway route is additive and operator-owned: no identity lock, no ZDR check on that path, the operator's gateway/virtual key decides which model answers. reviews{} keys for that route use a new generic role pair (model-1/model-2) registered alongside the existing deepseek/openai and historical gemini/openai pairs in review_verdict.SUPPORTED_REVIEWER_SETS, so the verdict/contradiction/marker machinery needs no changes. The actually-answering model (from the API response, where available) is captured as a separate evidence field so the record never implies a specific model that the operator's gateway didn't actually use. === CORRECTED 2026-08-05 — MERGE-FIRST, AND THE PUBLIC COMMITMENTS ARE BINDING ===

SEQUENCING CHANGED BY THE OPERATOR. The text above says the contributor validates 'before merge'. That is NO LONGER the plan: build it, review it, MERGE it, and the operator informs carlosgil-ai afterwards so he can validate against his real Portkey/WAF setup on main. Do NOT hold the PR open waiting for external validation, and do not disable self-merge on that account.

THE ISSUE COMMENT IS PUBLIC AND SPECIFIC — IT IS NOW A CONTRACT. The maintainer's reply on issue #547 (2026-08-05) names the config surface verbatim. Implement these EXACT names; a different spelling makes a published promise false:

  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_BASE_URL
  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_HEADER_<NAME>      # arbitrarily many, e.g. WAF auth
  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_MODEL_1            # model / virtual-key alias, slot 1
  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_KEY_MODEL_1
  SHIPWRIGHT_REVIEW_GATEWAY_MODEL_2

The rationale given to the contributor: when an egress policy requires all traffic through the gateway, a silent fallback to a direct API call is a policy VIOLATION, not a convenience. ALSO PROMISED, already in the card but restated because it is publicly committed:
  * The generic surface must fit ANY OpenAI-compatible gateway (Portkey, Helicone, LiteLLM proxy, Azure AI Foundry) - no Portkey-specific naming.

A missing payload on any other source is LEGAL and silent. The earlier version of this card claimed 22 of 24 open items rendered the warning; that counted items lacking a payload, not items that trigger the warning. Exactly ONE did: the LLM-gateway card, which additionally carried the wrong source ('github' is the security importer's source in this repo, so it also routed into the security channel). That card has been re-filed under 'github-issue'.

THE PRODUCER GAP IS STILL REAL, AND IT IS THE POINT. triage.py:350/:418 (append_triage_item) and :448/:534 (append_triage_item_idempotent) both accept launch_payload and persist it as launchPayload. shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py exposes NO such flag - its argparse surface is only --project-root, --title, --detail, --severity, --kind, --source, --fr-id, --evidence-path, --run-id, --commit. So the documented manual CLI cannot produce a launchable card at all, and any future github-sourced card filed through it reproduces the warning immediately.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WARNING. The board is meant to be a LAUNCH surface, not a findings mirror. On 2026-08-05 all open cards were re-filed WITH payloads by calling the library directly, precisely because the CLI could not - that one-off proves the field is wanted, and that the CLI is the only thing standing in the way.

FIX. Add --launch-payload to triage_add.py and pass it through. Keep it OPTIONAL: a card with no sensible launch command must stay legal, and the github-only warning must keep firing for automated producers that genuinely forgot one. Consider a default of '/shipwright-iterate' for manual cards, made explicit rather than silent.

DO NOT REWRITE HISTORY. The store is an append-only log; re-filing (dismiss + successor) is the supported way to change a card, and is what was done above.

SCOPE. shared/scripts/tools/triage_add.py plus tests. File-disjoint from every other open unit. The payload is git-tracked and sweeps into a public PR, so it must stay neutral - no private tree paths, no secrets.

title: P2.19a Automatische Aufraeum- und Wiederherstellungspfade loeschen oder verklemmen (IT-1 Audit 9/16/23/25)
detail: Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; ein Iterate zieht die Karte durch. Alle vier liegen im Schreibpfad auf den getrackten Store: triage_gc.apply_gc, sweep_drift, reconcile_triage, churn_merge. (16) apply_gc schreibt den getrackten Log neu, committet aber NICHT -> plan_main_tracked_drift meldet danach main_tracked_diverged und der Sweep liefert bei JEDEM weiteren Iterate nichts mehr aus; reconcile_main_triage hat dieselbe Form ohne Rollback. Kein Werkzeug warnt, dass es gerade den Lieferkanal abgeschaltet hat. (9) apply_gc baut tmp+fsync+os.replace von Hand statt durable_atomic_write: keine Windows-Sharing-Violation-Retries, kein Parent-Dir-fsync, und das .bak nutzt write_text (nicht durable, uebersetzt Zeilenenden). (23) Die Re-Verifikation vor dem checkout-- verengt das Fenster, schliesst es aber nicht; ein Append eines nicht-kooperierenden Schreibers dazwischen ist weg und wird als unvermeidbar dargestellt statt als Datenverlust. ACHTUNG: beruehrt churn_merge -> loest cross_component aus (Integrations-Coverage pflicht). Reihenfolge: seriell zu P2.19e (beide fassen reconcile_triage.py an). title: P2.19b Endzustaende ohne Ausweg in Triage-Validierung und Quarantaene (IT-1 Audit 15/17/18)
detail: Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; ein Iterate zieht die Karte durch. Zwei Dateien, triage_validate und sweep_quarantine, drei Wege in einen Zustand, aus dem die Auslieferung nicht zurueckkommt. (15) classify_triage_text macht json.loads je physischer Zeile OHNE Grenz-Recovery, waehrend der Leser sie hat und der Ereignislog-Zwilling laengst auf split_records umgestellt wurde. Der Operator-Text nennt triage_repair nie. (17) protected_status_unplaceable blockiert dauerhaft, und der genannte Ausweg (main ausliefern per push/merge) ist in diesem Workflow nicht erreichbar, weil main nicht direkt gepusht wird - absorbierender Zustand, und der Puffer ist ein git clean -xfd vom Leersein entfernt. (18) Eine Status-Zeile mit fehlender oder nicht-str id wird als Fehler vermerkt, aber NICHT in orphan_status_ids aufgenommen: decide sagt block, quarantaenen geht nicht (id fehlt) und reparieren geht nicht (das JSON ist gueltig). title: P2.19c Beschaedigung liest sich als Abwesenheit; das Board unterscheidet geliefert nicht von gepuffert (IT-1 Audit 5/12/21/22/28)
detail: Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; ein Iterate zieht die Karte durch. Leserseite: jsonl_records, triage, triage_contract, triage_cli. (28) pendingDelivery wird aus zwei Mengen berechnet, die BEIDE nur append-Ereignisse enthalten - ein gepufferter Status-Flip ist strukturell unsichtbar. Am 2026-08-05 gemessen: 33 Flips im Outbox, davon 26 mit bereits getracktem Append, also alle 26 mit pendingDelivery=false. In diesem Fall waren sie korrekt auf den Branch gesweept (KEIN beobachteter Verlust) - der Defekt ist, dass das Board in beiden Faellen identisch aussieht: es gibt keine Oberflaeche, die sagt, eine Entscheidung habe origin noch nicht erreicht. Damit ist 28 das Messgeraet fuer P2.19a und P2.19b und sollte NACH mindestens einer der beiden gebaut werden. (21) Die Grenz-Recovery in split_records ist einseitig: schlaegt der Zeilen-ANFANG fehl, wandert der ganze Rest in den Remainder, samt aller gueltigen Datensaetze dahinter - und die dokumentierte Hauptursache (abgeschnittener Vorgaenger) hat exakt diese Form. Die zwei deckenden Tests pruefen die anderen beiden Formen. (5) read_jsonl_records nutzt bare open statt durable_read_text, obwohl die Datei per durable_atomic_write publiziert wird; ungesperrte Leser rennen gegen den Sweep-Rewrite (Windows-Fenster gemessen 1 von 36). title: P2.19d Schreib- und Sperr-Primitiven: Dateirechte, fehlender Windows-Fehlercode, Sperre ohne Zeitlimit (IT-1 Audit 10/20/24)
detail: Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; ein Iterate zieht die Karte durch. Zwei Dateien, atomic_write und file_lock, winziger Diff, aber breiter Radius - jede Aenderung hier trifft rund 30 Aufrufer, also gehoert sie in einen eigenen Lauf und nicht als Anhaengsel an einen Fix. (20) durable_atomic_write legt die Temp-Datei per mkstemp an (Modus 0600) und publiziert sie per os.replace, ohne den urspruenglichen Modus wiederherzustellen: auf POSIX verliert JEDE so geschriebene Datei still ihre Gruppen- und Andere-Leserechte, und git sieht davon nichts (nur das x-Bit ist getrackt). Auf dem heutigen Windows-Entwicklungshost und im Ein-Nutzer-Repo folgenlos, deshalb medium und nicht high. (10) Die Sharing-Violation-Retry-Liste fuehrt die Windows-Codes 5 und 32, aber nicht 33 (ERROR_LOCK_VIOLATION), den CPython ebenfalls auf PermissionError abbildet - ein Byte-Range-Lock auf dem Ziel faellt damit aus dem Retry heraus und schlaegt sofort durch. (24) Die blockierende FileLock-Variante hat WEDER Zeitlimit NOCH Reentranz: auf POSIX blockiert flock(LOCK_EX) unbegrenzt, auf Windows dreht eine 1-ms-Schleife ewig, und eine verschachtelte Anforderung verklemmt sich selbst ohne jede Diagnose. Der Schwester-Kontextmanager im selben Modul hat ein hartes 5-s-Limit und begruendet es. Am 2026-08-05 nachverfolgt: die Sperre liegt auf Hook-Pfaden (Ereignislog, Iterate-Timings) UND auf dem Worktree-Setup-Schritt 5 - also genau dort, wo ein stiller Haenger von einem Session-Tod nicht zu unterscheiden ist. Die Audits haben allerdings belegt, dass es HEUTE keine Doppel-Anforderung im Code gibt: das ist eine Leitplanke, kein aktiver Defekt. 10 war nie einer Nachfolgekarte zugeordnet.

title: P2.19e Duplikat der Git-Zustands-Praedikate zusammenfuehren (IT-1 Audit 29)
detail: Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; bewusst ein eigener kleiner Iterate, damit der Review der Datenverlust-Fixes nicht mit reinen Verschiebungen vermischt wird (Operator-Entscheidung 2026-08-05). sweep_outbox und reconcile_triage halten zwei Kopien derselben Git-Zustands-Praedikate, die beide destruktive Commits freigeben: _op_in_progress (31 bzw. 34 Zeilen, inhaltlich gleich bis auf Kommentare) und _has_staged_changes (7 bzw. 10). Zusammen rund 38 LOC. KORREKTUR zur Evidenzdatei: deren dritter Punkt, _CI_TRUTHY bzw. _ci_active liege in DREI Kopien vor, ist ueberholt - alle vier Vorkommen delegieren heute an den gemeinsamen Leaf lib.ci_env und dokumentieren das auch im Docstring; dieser Teil ist bereits erledigt und braucht keine Arbeit. Bemerkenswert bleibt die Asymmetrie: reconcile_triage hat zusaetzlich _is_detached, sweep_outbox nicht. Das ist im heutigen Ablauf vertretbar (der Sweep committet in einen Worktree, der auf iterate/<slug> steht), aber es ist genau die Art Drift, die zwei Kopien erzeugen - beim Zusammenfuehren bewusst entscheiden statt beilaeufig angleichen. Beide Praedikate nehmen bereits einen root-Parameter, die Extraktion ist also mechanisch: der Sweep prueft den Worktree, reconcile den Haupt-Baum, und das muss so bleiben. Reihenfolge: seriell zu P2.19a (beide fassen reconcile_triage.py an). Stand 2026-08-05 nachgemessen.

title: [f0] shipwright-run failed in parallel and passed alone - race or flaky test
detail:
shipwright-run: red in parallel (rc 1), GREEN alone (rc 0). It is NOT xdist-allowlisted, so this is inter-unit pollution or an unreliable test.

The F0 suite runner ran this unit twice. With every unit running side by side it reported a pytest test failure (exit 1). Re-run ALONE - after the pool drained, without xdist, in a clean temp dir - it PASSED (exit 0). That alone-run verdict is authoritative, so the gate was NOT stopped.

The runner cannot tell which of these it is:
  - a race between concurrently running units (shared state, ports, temp files, the shared working tree), or
  - a test that fails intermittently on its own.
Both are real defects; only measurement separates them.

Reproduce the unit exactly as the runner re-ran it (expect GREEN):
  cd plugins/shipwright-run && uv run --python 3.11 --with pytest --with pytest-mock --with pytest-cov pytest tests -q -p no:cacheprovider --cov=scripts '--cov-config=C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\llm-review-gateway-route\pyproject.toml' --cov-report=
Reproduce the whole suite in parallel (expect the intermittent red):
  uv run --python 3.11 shared/scripts/tools/run_test_suite.py --project-root 'C:\01_Development\shipwright\.worktrees\llm-review-gateway-route' --run-id iterate-2026-08-05-llm-review-gateway-route

The failing output stayed in that run's F0 console and is deliberately not copied here.

This entry is never closed automatically: one clean parallel run is not evidence the race is gone. Close it when the unit is fixed, or dismiss it deliberately.

title: verify_local.py runs at F0, but the commit CI judges is not the tree it read
detail:
Raised by the Stage-3 doubt review of iterate-2026-08-05-wire-local-guard-scripts, which wired scripts/verify_local.py into F0 (closing P2.27 / trg-486cb11c). That spec originally claimed F0 was 'the only home where the script's documented weakness disappears'. It is not, and the claim has been corrected in the spec, the script docstring and docs/hooks-and-pipeline.md.

THE GAP. verify_local.py reads the WORKING TREE; CI reads the commit you PUSH. F0 runs before F6, so between the verdict and the push there are (a) eight phases that write tracked artifacts - F0.5, F3, F3a, F4, F5, F5a, F5b, F5c, per SKILL.md's own ordering note - and (b) F11's ensure_current.py, which fetches and MERGES origin/<default> before the push. The commit CI judges is therefore F0's tree plus eight phases plus a merge of main.

WHY IT LANDS ON THE INPUT THAT MATTERS. check_ci_gate_coverage.py reads .github/workflows and the gate allowlist. Both can arrive in that F11 merge. A concurrent PR landing a new gate step is precisely the failure class the guard exists for, and F0 structurally cannot see it - so the one gate whose subject changes underneath it is the one this placement covers least.

PROPOSED REMEDY. A second invocation inside F11, after ensure_current.py has integrated and regenerated, and before the push. That is the only local moment the merged result exists. Cost: one more ~8s run on the F11 path, and a STOP condition arriving late (the work is already committed), which is why it was not folded into the delivering run.

NOT URGENT, NOT THEORETICAL. The F0 step delivers the common case today; this is the tail. Sequence it after any change to F11's delivery ladder rather than alongside one.

The position is now ENFORCED: shipwright_inline_suppressions.json ratchets the per-rule count (5 rules / 20 sites). See docs/security-ci-setup.md.

title: run_test_suite.py returns exit 2 (not the documented 130) on cancellation, on Windows
detail: Surfaced by IT-9 Unit 5 (windows-tests.yml, the repo's first-ever Windows CI job). shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_run_test_suite_faults.py::test_main_cancellation_releases_real_locks_and_next_run_resets_state asserts mod.main() == 130 on a KeyboardInterrupt-driven cancellation with real locks held -- this passes on Linux (ci.yml already runs this test) but returns 2 on windows-latest. F0.md documents that Windows releases the launcher via a kill-on-close Job Object while POSIX uses a process group, so the two platforms' cancellation paths are genuinely different code -- this looks like the Windows path not normalizing to the same 128+signal convention the POSIX path uses, rather than a test bug. Needs someone who knows run_test_suite.py's Windows Job-Object cancellation handling to root-cause whether the fix belongs in main() (normalize the return code) or in the test (accept the Windows-native convention). Deselected from windows-tests.yml for now with a comment pointing at this card; still runs (and passes) on ci.yml's Linux job, so it is not silently unverified.
