title: P2.40 [AUTO][MEASURE-FIRST] The recurring F0 parallel failures are tests that read live global state, not flaky tests
detail:
DIAGNOSED 2026-08-06 from the on-disk F0 diagnostics, after 11 sightings over 10 days produced 9 dismissals and no fix. Filed as ONE card because the sightings share one cause; supersedes the two open sighting cards trg-81bef251 (integration-tests) and trg-f4728d1b (shipwright-run).

SIGHTING HISTORY, per dedup key: shipwright-run 4 (2026-07-27, 07-28 twice, 08-05), integration-tests 3 (08-04 twice, 08-05), shared/scripts/tools/tests 3 (08-04), shared/tests 1 (07-30). Every one closed on the re-fire contract; every one came back. That loop is the reason this card exists.

THE NAMED FAILURES, extracted from .shipwright/runs/*/f0-diagnostics/*/*.json (11 files with rc != 0). The tail was always there - the cards simply never carried it:
  shipwright-run                . tests/test_runconfig_concurrency.py::test_three_process_writers_no_truncation_no_lost_update
  shared/scripts/tools/tests    . test_host_resource_lease_process.py::test_wait_output_names_queue_owner_run_id_and_heartbeats
  integration-tests             . test_ensure_shared_cache_fanout.py::test_healthy_cache_fanout_elects_one_scanner_and_copies_nothing
  integration-tests             . test_requirements_corpus_matrix.py::test_golden_file_is_byte_current
  integration-tests             . test_requirements_corpus_matrix.py::test_target_behaviour_matches_the_frozen_baseline[disc.review_runner.run_review]
  shared/tests                  . test_adr_index_producers.py::test_committed_index_is_not_stale
  shared/tests                  . test_adr_index_producers.py::test_every_adr_file_in_this_repo_is_listed
  shared/tests                  . test_inline_suppressions_repo_guard.py::test_no_inline_suppression_has_outgrown_its_baseline

THE PATTERN, and why 'flaky' is the wrong word. Every one of these reads or contends on REAL GLOBAL STATE that sibling worktrees legitimately move while the test runs:
  * the host resource lease is repository-keyed and shared ACROSS worktrees by design - a test asserting on queue owner and heartbeat output is asserting about a resource siblings are holding;
  * the plugin cache is ONE global directory, and every hook-bearing plugin fires SessionStart against it - a fan-out election test races real elections;
  * three-process-writer concurrency assertions are timing-sensitive and the host CPU budget is fully claimed by one F0 at a time (weight 22 of 22), so a sibling's suite starves them;
  * committed ADR INDEX.md, the golden corpus file and the inline-suppression baseline all live in the shared tree, and a concurrent run regenerating any of them changes the subject mid-assertion.
They are not unreliable tests. They are correct tests pointed at a moving target.

ONE HYPOTHESIS IS ALREADY ELIMINATED - record it so nobody re-tries it. integration-tests was on suite.xdist with 8 workers; it was REMOVED (shipwright_test_config.json now lists only shared/tests) on the theory that intra-unit fan-out caused it. It raced again AFTER the removal, on 2026-08-05. Intra-unit xdist is not the cause.

MEASURE FIRST, then fix. Run the full suite in parallel N times (N >= 5) and record, per named test, how often it fails and against which sibling activity. That separates 'contends on a global' from 'genuinely order-dependent', which the two need different fixes for. Do NOT skip this: the eight tests above are a hypothesis grouped by inspection, not a measurement.

FIX DIRECTIONS, to be chosen per test after measuring - all three are legitimate, none is a suppression:
  (a) POINT THE TEST AT A FIXTURE, not the live global. A cache-fanout test should elect against a temp cache root; a lease test should use a temp lease file. This is the preferred answer wherever the test's subject is behaviour rather than the live artifact.
  (b) PIN A SNAPSHOT AT TEST START where the subject genuinely is the repo artifact (INDEX.md staleness, baseline growth) - read once, assert against that read, so a concurrent regeneration cannot change the answer mid-test.
  (c) DECLARE EXCLUSIVITY for the few that must observe the real global. The suite already has a marker vocabulary and a per-unit budget; a test that needs the host to itself should say so and be scheduled accordingly.

WHAT IS NOT ACCEPTABLE, per the Iron Law: marking any of these as expected-flaky, adding a retry that hides it, or widening a tolerance until it passes. The verdict path is already correct - the alone-run is authoritative, so the gate never wrongly blocked - and that is exactly why this was survivable for 10 days without being fixed. The cost is not a broken gate; it is that a real failure in these units is now indistinguishable from the known noise.

SCOPE NOTE. This touches test files across four units, so it is NOT file-disjoint from much. Sequence it away from P2.19a-e (which rewrite the triage store the shared/tests ADR and baseline guards read) and from any run touching the plugin cache.

title: gate_policy.read_run_config_mode does not honour its own inert-on-corrupt promise
detail: Found by the Stage-2 code review of iterate-2026-08-05-standalone-flag-corrupt-config; deliberately OUT OF SCOPE there (shared/, and the agreed scope was the v1 orchestrator step-advance path). read_run_config_mode's docstring promises that a missing / mode-less / corrupt config reads as INERT_MODE, but its guard is except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError). Two shapes escape it, and they are exactly the two that iterate closed on the orchestrator side: (1) a config whose top-level JSON is not an object (null / [] / a number) parses cleanly and then raises AttributeError on .get('mode'); (2) a non-UTF-8 config raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is a ValueError and not a JSONDecodeError. Either crashes the caller (shared/scripts/tools/resolve_gate_policy.py) instead of reading inert. This is an availability gap in a READ-ONLY reporter, not a safety one - no gate is weakened, the process just dies with a traceback instead of a readable answer. Suggested fix is two lines: widen to except (ValueError, OSError) and add an isinstance(parsed, dict) check, mirroring orchestrator_pkg.config_io._read_parse_shape. The parity claim in config_io.py's Mode section was amended in that iterate to stop overstating the agreement rather than silently leaving it false.

title: host_resource_lease ownership check rejects GitHub-hosted windows-latest's runneradmin profile dir
detail: Surfaced by IT-9 Unit 5 (windows-tests.yml). shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_f0_cli_diff_coverage_e2e.py::test_the_f0_cli_stops_on_an_under_covered_diff_then_passes_once_covered spawns run_test_suite.py as a real subprocess -- on windows-latest it fails immediately with 'host lease runtime root is not private: C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local: directory is not owned by the current user' (shared/scripts/lib/_windows_acl.py's ownership check, invoked from _host_resource_locking.py). This is a security hardening check (guards lock files against tampering by another user) that is deliberately not something to weaken. It looks like GH-hosted windows-latest provisions the runneradmin profile directory with an owner/ACL shape this check does not recognize as self-owned -- needs someone to inspect the actual owner SID on that runner (or a local repro with a similarly-provisioned account) to determine whether _windows_acl.py's detection needs to accept an additional legitimate ownership shape, or whether this CI environment genuinely cannot satisfy the security property host_resource_lease requires. Passes on ci.yml's Linux job today (no equivalent check fires there). Deselected from windows-tests.yml for now with a comment pointing at this card.

title: Phase-quality Stop audit never receives the iterate run_id, so S2/S3/S9/S10/W2 always SKIP
detail: resolve_run_id (shared/scripts/lib/phase_quality/_resolution.py) resolves in priority order: shipwright_run_config.json top-level 'run_id' -> latest events.jsonl 'run_started' event -> SHIPWRIGHT_LOOP_ID -> the raw session id. In this repo NONE of the first three is ever populated for an iterate: run_config carries no top-level run_id (the canonical id lives in iterate_history entries and in shipwright_test_results.json iterate_latest.run_id), and no producer emits a 'run_started' event (all 15 matching files are readers). The audit therefore runs with run_id='unknown'. Evidence: .shipwright/compliance/skill-compliance/iterate-unknown-unknown.json is the only iterate audit snapshot on disk and carries run_id='unknown'. Consequence: every spec check gated by the unresolvable_run_id_skip guard -- S2, S3, W2, and now S9/S10 -- SKIPs on every real invocation, so this family of checks is effectively inert in production. The guard is correct and must stay (without it S9/S10 inherited an unrelated run's category, which is what iterate-2026-08-06-s9-s10-sentinel-guard fixed); the defect is upstream, in the seam that should hand the audit the iterate's own run_id. Fixing it would make all five checks live again. Pinned by shared/tests/test_spec_checks_run_id_guard.py::test_the_stop_audit_seam_hands_these_checks_an_unresolvable_run_id, which asserts the CURRENT (sentinel) behaviour and will fail loudly when the seam is repaired.

title: Retry-Praedikat der Schreib-/Lese-Primitive greift nicht, wenn Windows gar keinen Fehlercode liefert
detail: Waehrend iterate-2026-08-06-write-lock-primitives (Karte trg-dc013d82, Befund 10) empirisch gemessen, nicht aus dem Code geschlossen. Zwei Messungen auf Windows 11 / lokalem NTFS: (1) Der in Befund 10 behauptete Fall - ein Byte-Range-Lock auf dem Ziel liefere Windows-Code 33 - tritt NICHT ein; er liefert 5, weil ein Byte-Range-Lock die Datei ohnehin offen haelt und schon das offene Handle 5 ergibt. Derselbe Befund war bereits in iterate-2026-07-27-run-unit-parallel-race aus demselben Grund abgelehnt worden. 33 wurde trotzdem aufgenommen, ausdruecklich als Absicherung und nicht als gemessene Reparatur etikettiert. (2) Dabei kam der eigentliche Defekt zum Vorschein: Liest man einen Bereich, der per Byte-Range gesperrt ist, scheitert nicht das Oeffnen, sondern der Lesevorgang selbst - CPython erzeugt dann einen PermissionError OHNE jeden Windows-Fehlercode (winerror ist None). Verifiziert ueber Path.read_text, also genau den Aufruf, den durable_read_text benutzt. Das Retry-Praedikat vergleicht ausschliesslich Fehlernummern gegen eine Menge, und None steht in keiner Menge - die Lesewiederholung greift in diesem Fall also gar nicht, sondern reicht den Fehler sofort durch. Bewusst NICHT im selben Lauf behoben: es ist die Leseseite, und die Entscheidung, einen PermissionError ohne Code als voruebergehend zu behandeln, tauscht ein sofortiges Scheitern gegen ein Warten ueber das volle Lesebudget - das gehoert in einen eigenen Lauf mit eigener Abwaegung, nicht als Anhaengsel an einen Fix mit drei benannten Befunden. Reproduktion liegt als Sondierskript im Lauf-Scratchpad.

title: P2.19f Outbox-GC: Server-Stand und Puffer werden mit verschiedener Fehlerbehandlung dekodiert
detail: Gefunden vom Stage-3-doubt-reviewer waehrend iterate-2026-08-05-it1-audit-remainder, dort bewusst NICHT mitgefixt (Operator-Entscheidung 2026-08-05). Die GC-Zugehoerigkeit vergleicht seit diesem Lauf die kanonische Form beider Seiten. Die beiden Seiten werden aber unterschiedlich dekodiert: der Server-Stand kommt ueber lib.git_base.run_git, das fest auf errors=replace steht (ein kaputtes Byte wird U+FFFD), der Puffer ueber lib.sweep_text.read_text_verbatim mit errors=surrogateescape (dasselbe Byte wird U+DCxx). Traegt eine Zeile ein nicht-UTF-8-Byte, ergeben beide Seiten verschiedene Zeichenketten, die kanonischen Formen koennen nie uebereinstimmen, und die Zeile bleibt dauerhaft im gitignorierten Puffer liegen - dieselbe Klasse wie Audit-Befund 27. Die alte Id-Regel war dagegen immun, weil sie nur die reine ASCII-Id verglich. RICHTUNG: nur Liegenbleiben, KEIN Datenverlust - die Zeile ueberlebt, sie wird nur nie aufgeraeumt. Voraussetzung ist ein kaputtes Byte im bereits COMMITTETEN Log; sweep_outbox re-kodiert an zwei Stellen mit surrogateescape und jsonl_records nennt abgebrochene Mehrbyte-Schreibvorgaenge ausdruecklich als erwarteten Fall, also ist es erreichbar, aber selten. WARUM AUFGESCHOBEN: beide Behebungswege sind unverhaeltnismaessig. run_git umzustellen trifft 133 Aufrufstellen in shared/scripts. Lokal daran vorbeizugehen verliert die TimeoutExpired-Behandlung, die die Audit-Befunde 1 und 7 genau fuer diesen Pfad eingebaut haben (setup_iterate_worktree Schritt 5) - das waere eine Regression an einem bereits ausgelieferten Fix. FIXRICHTUNG: den Blob als Rohbytes lesen und mit derselben Fehlerbehandlung dekodieren wie den Puffer, plus ein Test, der eine getrackte Zeile mit einem rohen 0xFF-Byte seedet und prueft, dass die Puffer-Kopie nach Auslieferung verschwindet. Der doubt-reviewer hat ausserdem die naheliegende Sorge FALSIFIZIERT, ein einzelnes Surrogat koenne aus json.dumps eine UnicodeEncodeError werfen - tut es nicht, dumps liefert str und kodiert nicht; die Totalitaets-Zusicherung von canonical_form haelt.

title: P2.19g Outbox-Puffer: ueberholte Appends sammeln sich an, und eine tief verschachtelte Zeile kann den Sweep im Lock abbrechen
detail: Zwei Reste aus iterate-2026-08-05-it1-audit-remainder, beide bewusst dort NICHT behoben. Ein Iterate kann beide ziehen - selbe Nachbarschaft (sweep_gc / churn_merge / triage_validate). TEIL 1 - ANSAMMLUNG. dedup_triage_lines behaelt beim Materialisieren nur den LETZTEN Append je id, ein frueherer erreicht also nie einen Branch und nie origin. Seit die GC-Zugehoerigkeit ueber die kanonische Form geht, ist auch seine kanonische Form nie bei origin - er bleibt dauerhaft im gitignorierten Puffer. Die alte Id-Regel hat ihn abgeraeumt. WICHTIG FUER DEN NAECHSTEN ANLAUF: eine Abflussklappe dafuer WURDE gebaut, dreimal reviewt und wieder GELOESCHT. Gruende, alle gemessen: sie war der einzige Pfad im Modul, der die LETZTE Kopie eines Datensatzes loeschen konnte (dedup hatte die Zeile per Definition vom Branch ferngehalten); ihre Korrektheit war eine Uebereinkunft zwischen sweep_gc und churn_merge ueber zwei verschiedene Append-Erkenner auf zwei verschiedenen Zeichenketten, die kein Test halten konnte; zwei von drei Anlaeufen leckten in LOESCH-Richtung (einmal ueber doppelten Text, einmal ueber eine Leerzeichen-Variante, weil dedup Stufe 1 auf der ROHEN Zeile schluesselt und .strip() Unicode-bewusst ist, JSON-Whitespace aber nicht); ein Treffer war von einem harmlosen Aufraeumen nicht unterscheidbar (gleicher Zaehler, kein Hinweis, kein Protokoll); und der Nutzen ist gemessen NULL - im echten 1457-Zeilen-Log existiert keine einzige ueberholte Fassung. title: P3.05a [AUTO after PR #571] Two Windows-only F0 defects the first Windows CI job exposed
detail:
BUNDLES trg-e82d8771 and trg-d0f585b2. Both were surfaced by IT-9 Unit 5 (iterate-2026-08-05-windows-ci-tests, PR #571), both are Windows-only, and both keep the repo's FIRST-EVER Windows job from going green. One run, because a second Windows CI round-trip to fix them separately costs more than the diff does.

BLOCKED ON PR #571: the job these fail in does not exist on main yet.

--- (1) exit code, was trg-e82d8771 ---
Surfaced by IT-9 Unit 5 (windows-tests.yml, the repo's first-ever Windows CI job). shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_run_test_suite_faults.py::test_main_cancellation_releases_real_locks_and_next_run_resets_state asserts mod.main() == 130 on a KeyboardInterrupt-driven cancellation with real locks held -- this passes on Linux (ci.yml already runs this test) but returns 2 on windows-latest. F0.md documents that Windows releases the launcher via a kill-on-close Job Object while POSIX uses a process group, so the two platforms' cancellation paths are genuinely different code -- this looks like the Windows path not normalizing to the same 128+signal convention the POSIX path uses, rather than a test bug. Needs someone who knows run_test_suite.py's Windows Job-Object cancellation handling to root-cause whether the fix belongs in main() (normalize the return code) or in the test (accept the Windows-native convention). Deselected from windows-tests.yml for now with a comment pointing at this card; still runs (and passes) on ci.yml's Linux job, so it is not silently unverified.

--- (2) lease ownership on runneradmin, was trg-d0f585b2 ---
Surfaced by IT-9 Unit 5 (windows-tests.yml). shared/scripts/tools/tests/test_f0_cli_diff_coverage_e2e.py::test_the_f0_cli_stops_on_an_under_covered_diff_then_passes_once_covered spawns run_test_suite.py as a real subprocess -- on windows-latest it fails immediately with 'host lease runtime root is not private: C:\Users\runneradmin\AppData\Local: directory is not owned by the current user' (shared/scripts/lib/_windows_acl.py's ownership check, invoked from _host_resource_locking.py). This is a security hardening check (guards lock files against tampering by another user) that is deliberately not something to weaken. It looks like GH-hosted windows-latest provisions the runneradmin profile directory with an owner/ACL shape this check does not recognize as self-owned -- needs someone to inspect the actual owner SID on that runner (or a local repro with a similarly-provisioned account) to determine whether _windows_acl.py's detection needs to accept an additional legitimate ownership shape, or whether this CI environment genuinely cannot satisfy the security property host_resource_lease requires. Passes on ci.yml's Linux job today (no equivalent check fires there). Deselected from windows-tests.yml for now with a comment pointing at this card.

WHY TOGETHER: both are the same class - a POSIX assumption meeting a real Windows host - and both are only observable in that job. Fixing one leaves the job red on the other, so the next Windows CI signal is still unusable.

title: P2.41 [AUTO after PR #577] gate_policy.read_run_config_mode does not honour its inert-on-corrupt promise
detail:
Found by the Stage-2 code review of iterate-2026-08-05-standalone-flag-corrupt-config; deliberately OUT OF SCOPE there (shared/, and the agreed scope was the v1 orchestrator step-advance path). read_run_config_mode's docstring promises that a missing / mode-less / corrupt config reads as INERT_MODE, but its guard is except (json.JSONDecodeError, OSError). Two shapes escape it, and they are exactly the two that iterate closed on the orchestrator side: (1) a config whose top-level JSON is not an object (null / [] / a number) parses cleanly and then raises AttributeError on .get('mode'); (2) a non-UTF-8 config raises UnicodeDecodeError, which is a ValueError and not a JSONDecodeError. Either crashes the caller (shared/scripts/tools/resolve_gate_policy.py) instead of reading inert. This is an availability gap in a READ-ONLY reporter, not a safety one - no gate is weakened, the process just dies with a traceback instead of a readable answer. Suggested fix is two lines: widen to except (ValueError, OSError) and add an isinstance(parsed, dict) check, mirroring orchestrator_pkg.config_io._read_parse_shape. The parity claim in config_io.py's Mode section was amended in that iterate to stop overstating the agreement rather than silently leaving it false.

title: P2.42 [AUTO] The Stop audit never receives an iterate run_id, so S2/S3/S9/S10/W2 always SKIP
detail:
resolve_run_id (shared/scripts/lib/phase_quality/_resolution.py) resolves in priority order: shipwright_run_config.json top-level 'run_id' -> latest events.jsonl 'run_started' event -> SHIPWRIGHT_LOOP_ID -> the raw session id. In this repo NONE of the first three is ever populated for an iterate: run_config carries no top-level run_id (the canonical id lives in iterate_history entries and in shipwright_test_results.json iterate_latest.run_id), and no producer emits a 'run_started' event (all 15 matching files are readers). The audit therefore runs with run_id='unknown'. Evidence: .shipwright/compliance/skill-compliance/iterate-unknown-unknown.json is the only iterate audit snapshot on disk and carries run_id='unknown'. Consequence: every spec check gated by the unresolvable_run_id_skip guard -- S2, S3, W2, and now S9/S10 -- SKIPs on every real invocation, so this family of checks is effectively inert in production. The guard is correct and must stay (without it S9/S10 inherited an unrelated run's category, which is what iterate-2026-08-06-s9-s10-sentinel-guard fixed); the defect is upstream, in the seam that should hand the audit the iterate's own run_id. Fixing it would make all five checks live again. Pinned by shared/tests/test_spec_checks_run_id_guard.py::test_the_stop_audit_seam_hands_these_checks_an_unresolvable_run_id, which asserts the CURRENT (sentinel) behaviour and will fail loudly when the seam is repaired.

Zwei Messungen auf Windows 11 / lokalem NTFS: (1) Der in Befund 10 behauptete Fall - ein Byte-Range-Lock auf dem Ziel liefere Windows-Code 33 - tritt NICHT ein; er liefert 5, weil ein Byte-Range-Lock die Datei ohnehin offen haelt und schon das offene Handle 5 ergibt. (2) Dabei kam der eigentliche Defekt zum Vorschein: Liest man einen Bereich, der per Byte-Range gesperrt ist, scheitert nicht das Oeffnen, sondern der Lesevorgang selbst - CPython erzeugt dann einen PermissionError OHNE jeden Windows-Fehlercode (winerror ist None). Verifiziert ueber Path.read_text, also genau den Aufruf, den durable_read_text benutzt. Das Retry-Praedikat vergleicht ausschliesslich Fehlernummern gegen eine Menge, und None steht in keiner Menge - die Lesewiederholung greift in diesem Fall also gar nicht, sondern reicht den Fehler sofort durch. Bewusst NICHT im selben Lauf behoben: es ist die Leseseite, und die Entscheidung, einen PermissionError ohne Code als voruebergehend zu behandeln, tauscht ein sofortiges Scheitern gegen ein Warten ueber das volle Lesebudget - das gehoert in einen eigenen Lauf mit eigener Abwaegung, nicht als Anhaengsel an einen Fix mit drei benannten Befunden. Reproduktion liegt als Sondierskript im Lauf-Scratchpad.

--- (2) third copy of the lock mechanics, was trg-2e961fee ---
Beim Beheben von trg-dc013d82 Befund 24 aufgefallen. Die blockierende Sperre in shared/scripts/lib/file_lock.py hat jetzt ein Zeitlimit und Reentranz; nachgewiesen wurde das gegen die unveraenderte Vorgaengerfassung, die im Test woertlich blockiert (kein Zeitlimit) beziehungsweise sich selbst verklemmt (keine Reentranz). In plugins/shipwright-run/scripts/lib/phase_task_lifecycle.py steht jedoch eine dritte, woertliche Kopie derselben Mechanik - ihr eigener Kommentar sagt ausdruecklich, sie spiegele das Muster aus record_event, also genau die Kopie, die 2026 in die gemeinsame Klasse ausgelagert und jetzt repariert wurde. Sie hat unveraendert kein Zeitlimit (POSIX blockiert unbegrenzt, Windows dreht eine 1-ms-Schleife) und keine Reentranz. Der Reparaturweg ist derselbe wie bei den beiden anderen Kopien: an die gemeinsame Klasse delegieren statt eine vierte Variante zu pflegen. Bewusst nicht im selben Lauf erledigt - anderes Plugin, und die Karte war ausdruecklich auf zwei Dateien zugeschnitten. Radius ist klein: die Sperre schuetzt Aenderungen an der Phasenaufgaben-Liste eines Projekts, nicht die Hook-Pfade, auf denen der stille Haenger von Befund 24 gemessen wurde.

title: Adopted repos render Source-State: run=(unknown) - the adopted event is not a work event
detail:
MEASURED 2026-08-06 while building iterate-2026-08-05-adopt-derived-evidence-rollout. An adopted repository's compliance evidence renders 'Source-State: run=(unknown)'. Cause: the provenance header takes its run id from collectors.change_history.latest_work_event, which matches ONLY type=='work_completed'. Adopt seeds type=='adopted' (event_seeder.seed_adopted_event), and its optional backfill work_completed events carry no adr_id. So the run id never resolves. Probed directly by driving latest_work_event -> banner_line with an adopt-shaped event log.

PARTIALLY MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, by the iterate above: adopt Step H now stamps base=<commit_at_adoption>, so the banner names the state it was built from and reads 'run=(unknown) base=abc123def456'. The commit is now stated; the RUN still is not.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED THERE (deliberate, not an oversight): latest_work_event is the SINGLE resolver behind BOTH provenance lines - 'Generated:' (its timestamp) and 'Source-State:' (its adr_id) - for every project, not just adopted ones. Widening it to recognise the adopted event would change the Generated: timestamp of every document in every repo and risks re-opening the permanently-dirty-tracked-documents problem that iterate-2026-05-22-deterministic-render-timestamps closed. That is a separate decision with its own blast radius.

TWO CANDIDATE SHAPES, both need thinking about before either is built: (a) have adopt seed a work_completed event carrying the adopt run id as adr_id, alongside the adopted event - cheap, but adds a synthetic 'work' event describing work nobody did; (b) teach the resolver to fall back to the adopted event for the run id ONLY, leaving the timestamp resolution alone - narrower, but splits one resolver into two answers, which is exactly what its docstring warns against ('one event object, read once, on purpose').

Worth doing: FR-01.10 requires evidence to name the change it was built from, and '(unknown)' satisfies that only via the where-it-cannot-be-established escape clause - which is true today but need not be.

title: Drift-adoption gate strands the whole outbox on one glued line in main's tracked log
detail: Residual of iterate-2026-08-06-triage-validate-deadends, found by its Stage-3 doubt review and deliberately left out of scope there. That run converted the PROTECTION parser (sweep_drift_events.append_ids_of) to record-boundary recovery, because failing there DESTROYS an operator dismiss. The ADOPTION gate in the same module, _is_producer_event, still parses one json.loads per physical line. So an UNCOMMITTED line in main's tracked drift window that holds two records glued together (an unterminated predecessor write, the documented cause) is judged 'not a triage producer event' -> plan_main_tracked_drift returns refused with main_tracked_unparseable -> the sweep skips and delivers NOTHING that run. It mutates nothing and loses nothing, and it retries every sweep, so this is a stall rather than data loss - but it is the same 'one bad line strands the whole buffer' class the run set out to remove, and the refusal reason does not name triage_repair.py, which is exactly the tool that fixes it. Two candidate fixes: recover boundaries in _is_producer_event as well (note adoption is line-granular and MOVES lines, so a glued line must still not be adopted - the safe form is 'recognise it, refuse to move it, and say why'), or at minimum name triage_repair.py in the main_tracked_unparseable reason so the refusal is escapable without reading the source.

title: P4.03 [GUIDED] IT-10 Plugin-Scope-Split: entry plugins global, 11 pipeline plugins project-scoped
detail:
SUPERSEDES trg-57317128 - inhaltlich unveraendert, nur in das IT-Schema umbenannt, damit das Board einheitlich ist. Spec und ACs liegen fertig unter .shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-2026-07-16-plugin-scope-split.md. Statt alle ~14 Plugins auf User-Ebene zu aktivieren (sie laden heute /shipwright-*-Kommandos und Hooks in JEDEM Verzeichnis, auch in Nicht-Shipwright-Repos) den Marketplace korrekt scopen. SPLIT: global bleiben nur die Plugins, die in einem noch-nicht-Shipwright-Verzeichnis aufgerufen werden - adopt, grade, run (codex bleibt global, unberuehrt). Die 11 Pipeline-Plugins (project, design, plan, build, test, deploy, changelog, compliance, security, iterate, preview) wandern auf PROJEKT-Ebene; adopt und der Greenfield-Run SCHREIBEN diesen Enablement-Block in die .claude/settings.json des Zielrepos. LINCHPIN: Installation (per-user cache) ist etwas anderes als Enablement (scope) - der phase-runner von run hat kein Skill-Tool und liest die Phasen-SKILL.md aus dem Cache-Pfad, Orchestrierung haengt also an der Installation, nicht am Enablement. Extern reviewed 2026-07-16 (GPT-5.4 + Gemini, 2/2). DREI BLOCKER: (B1) der Orchestrator muss Cache-Pfade explizit aufloesen, nicht ueber das per SessionStart injizierte SHIPWRIGHT_PLUGIN_ROOT (nur gesetzt wenn aktiviert) - per clean-env-Greenfield-Spike verifizieren; (B2) frische Nutzer haben die 11 Pipeline-Plugins nach C1 moeglicherweise nicht INSTALLIERT, also Install-Preflight in run, mit leerem Cache testen; (B3) bereits adoptierte Repos verlieren Kommandos, also Migrationskommando. ENTSCHIEDEN (Owner, 2026-07-16): (D1) Greenfield ist run-only, shipwright-project bleibt projekt-scoped, globales Set = adopt/grade/run; (D2) Solo-Nutzung, das Monorepo verwendet .claude/settings.local.json, die getrackte settings.json bleibt git-ignoriert (B4 damit gegenstandslos). Dazu JSONC-bewusster Merge, Secret-Leak-Guard, Marketplace-Source-Konflikt-Guard, Min-Version-UX und praeskriptive Aktivierungs-Lag-Meldungen.

title: P2.19e [AUTO after P2.19a] Merge the duplicated git-state predicates (IT-1 audit 29)
detail:
Aus trg-79102ee3 aufgeteilt; bewusst ein eigener kleiner Iterate, damit der Review der Datenverlust-Fixes nicht mit reinen Verschiebungen vermischt wird (Operator-Entscheidung 2026-08-05). sweep_outbox und reconcile_triage halten zwei Kopien derselben Git-Zustands-Praedikate, die beide destruktive Commits freigeben: _op_in_progress (31 bzw. 34 Zeilen, inhaltlich gleich bis auf Kommentare) und _has_staged_changes (7 bzw. 10). Zusammen rund 38 LOC. KORREKTUR zur Evidenzdatei: deren dritter Punkt, _CI_TRUTHY bzw. _ci_active liege in DREI Kopien vor, ist ueberholt - alle vier Vorkommen delegieren heute an den gemeinsamen Leaf lib.ci_env und dokumentieren das auch im Docstring; dieser Teil ist bereits erledigt und braucht keine Arbeit. Bemerkenswert bleibt die Asymmetrie: reconcile_triage hat zusaetzlich _is_detached, sweep_outbox nicht. Das ist im heutigen Ablauf vertretbar (der Sweep committet in einen Worktree, der auf iterate/<slug> steht), aber es ist genau die Art Drift, die zwei Kopien erzeugen - beim Zusammenfuehren bewusst entscheiden statt beilaeufig angleichen. title: P2.19g [AUTO] Outbox buffer: superseded appends accumulate, and a deeply nested value is mis-read
detail:
Zwei Reste aus iterate-2026-08-05-it1-audit-remainder, beide bewusst dort NICHT behoben. Ein Iterate kann beide ziehen - selbe Nachbarschaft (sweep_gc / churn_merge / triage_validate). TEIL 1 - ANSAMMLUNG. dedup_triage_lines behaelt beim Materialisieren nur den LETZTEN Append je id, ein frueherer erreicht also nie einen Branch und nie origin. Seit die GC-Zugehoerigkeit ueber die kanonische Form geht, ist auch seine kanonische Form nie bei origin - er bleibt dauerhaft im gitignorierten Puffer. Die alte Id-Regel hat ihn abgeraeumt. WICHTIG FUER DEN NAECHSTEN ANLAUF: eine Abflussklappe dafuer WURDE gebaut, dreimal reviewt und wieder GELOESCHT. Gruende, alle gemessen: sie war der einzige Pfad im Modul, der die LETZTE Kopie eines Datensatzes loeschen konnte (dedup hatte die Zeile per Definition vom Branch ferngehalten); ihre Korrektheit war eine Uebereinkunft zwischen sweep_gc und churn_merge ueber zwei verschiedene Append-Erkenner auf zwei verschiedenen Zeichenketten, die kein Test halten konnte; zwei von drei Anlaeufen leckten in LOESCH-Richtung (einmal ueber doppelten Text, einmal ueber eine Leerzeichen-Variante, weil dedup Stufe 1 auf der ROHEN Zeile schluesselt und .strip() Unicode-bewusst ist, JSON-Whitespace aber nicht); ein Treffer war von einem harmlosen Aufraeumen nicht unterscheidbar (gleicher Zaehler, kein Hinweis, kein Protokoll); und der Nutzen ist gemessen NULL - im echten 1457-Zeilen-Log existiert keine einzige ueberholte Fassung. Wer das wieder aufgreift, braucht zuerst einen Eigenschafts-Test ueber BEIDE Funktionen (Schnittmenge mit dem, was dedup behaelt, ist leer) und einen eigenen Zaehler plus Hinweis - sonst entsteht dasselbe Leck ein viertes Mal. Liegenbleiben ist die fail-safe Richtung; ohne Klappe ist der heutige Stand strikt sicherer als vorher. TEIL 2 - ABBRUCH IM LOCK. churn_merge._append_id faengt nur (JSONDecodeError, ValueError); eine ausreichend tief verschachtelte Zeile wirft RecursionError aus dedup_triage_lines heraus, durch sweep_quarantine bis in sweep_outbox_to_branch - INNERHALB des kanonischen Locks und auf dem setup_iterate_worktree-Schritt-5-Pfad, also genau der Abbruch nach erfolgreichem git worktree add, den drei Docstrings als nicht ueberlebbar bezeichnen. classify_triage_text hat dieselbe blanke json.loads-Stelle und kann es daher nicht abfangen. Vorbestehend, nicht neu. Der Fix ist ein Token je Stelle (RecursionError in die except-Tupel), aber churn_merge loest cross_component aus und damit Integrations-Coverage-Pflicht - deshalb eigener Lauf. jsonl_records.split_records faengt RecursionError bereits ausdruecklich und nennt abgebrochene/verschraenkte Schreibvorgaenge als plausible Ursache, die Eingabeklasse gilt im Repo also bereits als real.

title: Retained post-merge worktree keeps an iterate run pointer looking live
detail: phase_quality._run_id.pointer_run_id honours a per-session run pointer only when its worktree_path is still a directory, which rejects the orphaned-pointer case (F11 cleanup removed the worktree). It does NOT cover the case this repo actually produces: worktrees are RETAINED after their PR merges (measured: 64 pointer files under .shipwright/iterate_active vs ~36 live worktrees), so a finished run's pointer still looks live. A session that completes iterate A and keeps working therefore resolves run_id=A on every later Stop; once A's ledger entry has merged into main, has_exact_iterate_entry turns True and S9/S10 evaluate A's category against the current tree, filing a Tier-2 WARN under a merged run's id. Bounded: S9/S10 are Tier-2 (WARN, never FAIL) and heuristic-only in the rollup; S2/S3/W2 find A's real artifacts in main and behave correctly. Fix shape: give the pointer an explicit end-of-run retirement (F11/F12 unlink, or a finalized flag the resolver checks) rather than inferring liveness from the worktree directory. Rejected during iterate-2026-08-06-resolve-run-id-seam: requiring project_root to equal the pointer's worktree_path would also reject the main-root audit, which is the shape production actually uses.
launchPayload: /shipwright-iterate <id>

title: already_audited can freeze an iterate's phase-quality verdict at its first Stop
detail: audit_phase_quality_on_stop skips a phase when already_audited(project_root, phase, run_id, session_id) finds a valid finding JSON for that triple. Since iterate-2026-08-06-resolve-run-id-seam the run_id is stable across a whole iterate (the run pointer resolves the same canonical id from B1a onward), so the triple is now constant for the run where it previously varied only by session. The first Stop after B1a writes the finding while the run's ledger entry does not exist yet -- so S2/S3/W2/S9/S10 record SKIP -- and every later Stop, including those after F5c writes the entry, short-circuits on that file and never revisits the verdict. Net effect: a run's spec-check verdicts can be permanently fixed at their least-informed moment. Evidence of the same shape pre-dating this change: .shipwright/compliance/skill-compliance/iterate-unknown-unknown.json, audited 2026-06-15, has kept the (iterate, unknown, unknown) triple claimed ever since. Fix shape: make the idempotency key sensitive to the inputs the verdict depends on (e.g. include whether the run's ledger entry was present, or re-audit when a SKIP was recorded for a run whose entry has since appeared), rather than treating any prior finding for the triple as final.

title: Provenance stamp writes an LF line into a CRLF document, leaving mixed endings
detail:
FOUND 2026-08-06 by the Stage-2 code reviewer during iterate-2026-08-05-adopt-derived-evidence-rollout. NOT introduced by that change - pre-existing in shared stamping already used by the release and documents-only-PR paths.

WHAT: compliance_provenance.stamp_fixed_point rewrites the Source-State line with a regex whose replacement ends in a bare LF. The pattern consumes the original line's carriage return as part of its wildcard, so a document checked out or written with CRLF endings ends up with exactly one LF-only line among CRLF lines.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW: the same function is reached by a new third caller that runs on customer repositories, where a CRLF checkout is the normal case rather than the exception. Previously it ran mainly in this monorepo.

MEASURED SCOPE, so it is not over-stated: the reviewer looked for a CI-vs-local divergence in the delivered tests and found none - the banner parser splits on whitespace, the Group E staleness normaliser strips the banner before comparing, git normalises on commit, and the tests read through universal newlines. So nothing is currently red because of it.

WHAT REMAINS: a committed artifact with mixed line endings, which editors and diff tools flag; and with core.safecrlf=true set (not the default) a git add of that file fails outright.

FIX SHAPE: preserve the matched line's own terminator instead of hardcoding one - capture it in the pattern, or re-append the two-character ending when the match had one. Needs a test with a CRLF fixture, and it touches a function two shipping paths already depend on, which is why it was filed rather than folded into the iterate that found it.

title: Gate-mode reader and orchestrator reader still diverge on the read leg under a concurrent config rewrite
detail: gate_policy.read_run_config_mode reads the run config with a plain Path.read_text, while orchestrator_pkg.config_io._read_parse_shape reads via durable_read_text, which retries for READ_RETRY_BUDGET_SECONDS past the delete-pending PermissionError a concurrent os.replace causes on Windows. The reporter therefore answers INERT_MODE on the first such error while the orchestrator reads the config successfully, so the two can disagree about whether a run is driven while the config is being rewritten underneath them. Content-class parity (decode / parse / shape / BOM) was closed by iterate-2026-08-06-shared-read-run-config-mode-guard; this read-leg case was left open deliberately: routing through durable_read_text adds a sibling import inside shared/scripts/lib that is invisible to the usual pytest roots, and gate_policy.py sits exactly at its bloat-baseline cap (301). Fail-safe in direction (inert, never a weakened gate) and requires a concurrent writer to observe.

title: Three subprocess reads decode captured output strictly and can raise on a non-UTF-8 byte
detail: Same class as the triage-log seam fixed in iterate-2026-08-06-gc-decode-parity, but in call sites that iterate did not touch. Each captures a child process's output with text mode and an explicit utf-8 encoding but no errors= handler, so the decode is STRICT and a single byte that is not valid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError out of the reader thread rather than degrading. Observed live: the full shared/tests run for that iterate emitted a PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning for byte 0x81, from subprocess._readerthread. The suite still passed (the exception lands in a reader thread, not the assertion path), which is exactly why it has gone unnoticed - it is latent, not loud. Affects lib/pr_blockers.py, tools/watch_pr_delivery.py and one test helper; all three read tool output that can legitimately carry a cp1252 byte on Windows. Direction is a spurious failure or a swallowed read, never data loss. Fix is a one-word change per site (errors='replace' for human-facing text, or surrogateescape where the bytes must round-trip) plus a regression test seeding a non-UTF-8 byte into captured output.

title: Campaign sub-iterates do not run the architecture review pass
detail:
PR #582 added external_review.py --mode architecture as a second call in the external review step, wired into /shipwright-iterate Step 3.5 step 2a and /shipwright-plan Step 5a. The campaign sub-iterate-runner was deliberately NOT wired, and it is named in that iterate's Out of Scope rather than left as a silent divergence (found by the Stage-2 code review, which caught the spec, the guide and the skill all claiming 'every medium+ Branch A').

Two real obstacles, both of which need a decision rather than just an edit:

(1) agents/sub-iterate-runner.md sits at EXACTLY its ADR-119 bloat cap (497 lines). The runner carries its own inlined copy of Step 3.5 Branch A, so wiring the second call in costs lines that have to be paid for by extraction elsewhere in that file, or by a new ADR-gated exception.

(2) The pass's contract on a reject verdict is 'STOP and ask the operator'. The runner is autonomous and cannot ask. A campaign-mode answer has to be designed: most likely halt the unit, put both verdicts plus the recommended alternative into result.json, and let the orchestrator surface it at campaign end -- which is the shape Branch B already uses for missing keys.

Worth doing because campaign sub-iterates are exactly where new standing mechanisms tend to get built. Reference: .shipwright/planning/iterate/2026-08-06-architecture-review-pass.md (Out of Scope).

title: The rolling compliance backlog card blocks ensure_current on every long iterate
detail:
Measured twice during iterate-2026-08-06-architecture-review-pass, in the same run.

The compliance backlog producer keeps ONE rolling action-unit and rewrites it on every Stop: it dismisses the previous card and appends a fresh one with the current open-finding count (6 -> 5 across the two observations). Both lines land in the TRACKED .shipwright/triage.jsonl.

Consequence: any iterate whose finalization spans more than one Stop finds triage.jsonl dirty, and ensure_current aborts with exit 6 ('Your local changes would be overwritten by merge'). On a fast-moving main that means the integrate-verify-push cycle is interrupted by unrelated producer churn every time -- PR #582 hit it on two consecutive integration attempts and had to carry the appends onto the branch as chore commits to proceed.

Discarding the lines is wrong (they are real operator-facing state), and carrying them puts unrelated triage churn in a feature PR. Options worth weighing: route the rolling card to the gitignored outbox like other background producers (the outbox exists precisely so idle main does not accrue tracked-log drift), or have ensure_current stash-and-reapply a dirty triage.jsonl under the canonical triage lock, or make the rolling refresh idempotent so an unchanged finding set writes nothing.

title: P2.41a [AUTO after P2.41] Gate-mode reader and orchestrator reader still diverge on the read leg
detail:
gate_policy.read_run_config_mode reads the run config with a plain Path.read_text, while orchestrator_pkg.config_io._read_parse_shape reads via durable_read_text, which retries for READ_RETRY_BUDGET_SECONDS past the delete-pending PermissionError a concurrent os.replace causes on Windows. The reporter therefore answers INERT_MODE on the first such error while the orchestrator reads the config successfully, so the two can disagree about whether a run is driven while the config is being rewritten underneath them. Content-class parity (decode / parse / shape / BOM) was closed by iterate-2026-08-06-shared-read-run-config-mode-guard; this read-leg case was left open deliberately: routing through durable_read_text adds a sibling import inside shared/scripts/lib that is invisible to the usual pytest roots, and gate_policy.py sits exactly at its bloat-baseline cap (301). Fail-safe in direction (inert, never a weakened gate) and requires a concurrent writer to observe.

[NUMBERED 2026-08-06 as P2.41a. Tail of P2.41 (PR #585), which made the gate-mode reader answer instead of crashing its caller. Low: the crash path is closed, this is the remaining asymmetry between the two readers.]

title: P2.44 [AUTO] Three subprocess reads decode captured output strictly and can raise on non-UTF-8
detail:
Same class as the triage-log seam fixed in iterate-2026-08-06-gc-decode-parity, but in call sites that iterate did not touch. Each captures a child process's output with text mode and an explicit utf-8 encoding but no errors= handler, so the decode is STRICT and a single byte that is not valid UTF-8 raises UnicodeDecodeError out of the reader thread rather than degrading. Observed live: the full shared/tests run for that iterate emitted a PytestUnhandledThreadExceptionWarning for byte 0x81, from subprocess._readerthread. The suite still passed (the exception lands in a reader thread, not the assertion path), which is exactly why it has gone unnoticed - it is latent, not loud. Affects lib/pr_blockers.py, tools/watch_pr_delivery.py and one test helper; all three read tool output that can legitimately carry a cp1252 byte on Windows. Direction is a spurious failure or a swallowed read, never data loss. Fix is a one-word change per site (errors='replace' for human-facing text, or surrogateescape where the bytes must round-trip) plus a regression test seeding a non-UTF-8 byte into captured output.

[NUMBERED 2026-08-06 as P2.44. Same class as P2.36 (F0 console, PR #564) and P2.19f (the triage-log decode seam, PR #587), both delivered: a reader that assumes UTF-8 meets real captured bytes. Those two fixed their own surfaces; this names three more. Follow the pattern they set rather than inventing a third convention.]

title: P2.45 [AUTO][COST] ModelConfig: per-run model-tier flags for review, finalization and execution
detail:
PROBLEM. Agent definitions carry model: inherit, so every subagent runs on whatever the main session runs on. When the operator switches the session down a tier for cost, the review cascade follows silently, as do the two agents that drive F0-F11 unattended. The run still reports three passed reviews with no record of the tier they ran on. The defect is the silence, not the tier.

SETTLED DESIGN. Per-run flags on the invocation, over a project-level default. Precedence: flag > project config > unset. Unset omits the Agent tool model parameter entirely, which falls through to the frontmatter inherit, i.e. bit-identical to current behavior. Note the Agent tool model parameter has no inherit value; omitting the parameter is how deferral is expressed. Accept the literal value inherit as an explicit way to say the same.

ROLES. review = spec-reviewer, code-reviewer, doubt-reviewer, opus-plan-reviewer. finalization = section-builder, sub-iterate-runner (the justification is that nobody is watching them, so autonomous may be the better role name). execution = test-runner, security-fixer, section-writer, browser-fixer, phase-runner (phase-runner sits on the boundary).

SCOPE. Parse the flags in iterate and build; show them in the Planned Run Summary so the choice is visible; pass them at every spawn site; record the resolved tier per pass in reviews.json; propagate to campaign sub-iterates. Drift-test that the spawn instruction is present in both SKILL.md files, per the Step 6 rules pattern.

REJECTED. Hardcoding model: opus or model: sonnet in agent frontmatter. It ships to plugin consumers and removes their choice in BOTH directions: a cheaper pin forces a downgrade including the security-remediation agent, a stronger pin forces higher cost and is unavailable on some plans. inherit was the only consumer-respecting value. A first attempt at this was built and abandoned before delivery for exactly this reason.

OPEN DECISION, decide first. Home for the default: a new shipwright_model_config.json, or a block inside shipwright_run_config.json. The second needs a v2 schema bump but the Command Center already has a reader for that file, so this choice determines the size of the companion webui card.

CONTEXT. Brief with the full findings, established facts and a reusable test design: .shipwright/planning/iterate/iterate-agent-model-tiers-BRIEF.md

[NUMBERED 2026-08-06 as P2.45 and tagged COST. This is the operator's own card and the one direct lever on iterate model spend currently on the board: today every subagent carries model: inherit, so lowering the session tier silently lowers the review cascade and both unattended F0-F11 drivers with it, and the run still reports three passed reviews without recording which tier produced them. AUTO because the card states the design as SETTLED (per-run flags over a project default; precedence flag > project config > unset; unset omits the field). LANDMINE from prior design rounds: frontmatter pins and a role registry were both designed and DROPPED - do not rebuild either.]

title: Context-cost meter: measure tokens, calls and cost per phase before optimising anything
detail:
WHY (measured, 2026-08-07, 187 sessions / 54,516 API calls):
cost = calls x context. Every API call costs $0.56 regardless of what it does;
78.1% of calls add <2k tokens yet are 80.6% of the bill. A median session is
276 calls ~= $200. But 85.3% of that cost is NOT attributable to a phase,
because only 13% of calls carry a recognisable phase signature. Two
investigations into token cost have now drawn a wrong conclusion for lack of a
meter - including the first draft of Spec/context-cost-measured.md, which was
2x off. Measuring must come before optimising.

SCOPE:
1. A hook reads `transcript_path` (Claude Code passes it; no hook in this repo
   uses it yet), dedups records by `requestId` (MANDATORY - one API response is
   written as N transcript records, each repeating the identical `usage` dict:
   1.977x inflation), and computes per call: context = input_tokens +
   cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation, plus model and timestamp.
2. Appends to .shipwright/compliance/context-cost/session-cost.jsonl:
   calls, context integral, modelled cost, model mix.
3. A PHASE MARKER, or this rebuilds the 85% blind spot. Every phase stamps its
   own label; the meter aggregates calls / integral / wall-clock / cost per
   phase. This is the single acceptance criterion that matters.
4. Surface it: at phase boundaries and in the statusline.
5. Readiness check (the productisable part - a plugin CANNOT set user
   settings): report when `autoCompactWindow` is unset or above the window, and
   report the effort level in force. Same shape as verify_local.py.

REUSE, do not duplicate: `.shipwright/toolcall_count` +
estimate_context_pressure.py already gate on a tool-call PROXY (builder 120,
orchestrator 300). Replace the proxy with the measured quantity behind the same
thresholds - and note the orchestrator threshold of 300 barely ever fires, since
the median session is 276 calls.

DO NOT rebuild: raw-event or decision-log trimming. Both were measured at ~0% of
cost and the claim that they drive it is FALSIFIED (decision_log.md: ~25,000
chars total across ALL 194 sessions, zero at startup).

Evidence and method: Spec/context-cost-measured.md (Stage 1);
Spec/measurements/m10_authoritative.py is the authoritative script.
Reference numbers to beat for this iterate itself: a 100-300 call iterate cost
median $102 at 201 calls = $0.55/call, under xhigh + no autocompact + Opus.
launchPayload: /shipwright-iterate <id>

title: Test phase latency: verify the new wall-clock attribution emits, and separate suite runtime from re-runs
detail:
WHY: the `test` phase is 23.0% of instrumented iterate wall clock, and its
distribution is the problem, not its median: median 16.9 min, p90 5.3 h, max
34 h (83 runs with recorded phase_timings). A single coarse `test` bucket cannot
tell "the suite is slow" apart from "the suite ran four times because tests
failed three times" - so the tail is currently un-diagnosable.

CHECKED FIRST - two things already exist and must NOT be rebuilt:
1. The F0 suite is ALREADY parallel and calibrated by measurement:
   shipwright_test_config.json sets max_workers 11 (clamped to cpu_count-2, so
   two sibling F0 runs fit a 22-capacity host) and a per-unit xdist ALLOWLIST
   (shared/tests: 8). The config records why integration-tests and
   shipwright-compliance are deliberately excluded - nesting xdist under outer
   fleet load produced 17 failures although the root passed alone - and states
   NEVER replace this allowlist with a global `-n auto`. Treat that as binding.
2. Hierarchical wall-clock attribution landed 2026-08-05 (#551,
   shared/scripts/lib/iterate_timings.py record_producer_span), with two
   producer spans for this phase: `f0_queue` (host-lease wait) and
   `canonical_f0_active` (the suite's own execution). NEITHER appears in any of
   the 83 timed runs - the code is two days old, so this is unverified in
   production, not broken.

SCOPE:
1. Verify #551 actually emits: run F0 inside an iterate and confirm `f0_queue`
   and `canonical_f0_active` land in the work_completed phase_timings. If they
   do not, that is the bug.
2. Make a RE-RUN visible as a re-run: record each suite invocation separately
   (attempt number, unit, exit status, duration), so `test` = 5 h decomposes
   into runtime vs repetition vs lease queueing.
3. Only then, and only where the data points at it, cut latency. Lease wait and
   repeated full-suite runs after a single unit fails are the candidates the
   data can support. Per-unit worker counts are NOT - they are already measured.

EXPLICIT NON-GOAL: raising max_workers or widening the xdist allowlist without
new measurement. The 17-failure regression is documented in the config.

Context: Spec/context-cost-measured.md 5.1; phase shares scope 25.9% /
review 25.8% / test 23.0% / build 17.6% / finalize 7.7%. Pairs with the
context-cost meter card: that one measures tokens, this one measures wall clock,
and the two budgets are OPPOSED (fan-out buys latency with money).

title: Subagent model guidance: reviewers get Opus explicitly, a phase-runner handoff inherits the session model
detail:
AUTONOM: ja.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 (iterate-2026-08-07-test-phase-attribution): the session ran
509 main-thread calls on Sonnet, then handed finalization to
`shipwright-run:phase-runner` with `model='opus'` passed explicitly. That one
subagent cost $69.12 over 186 calls (158 Bash, 23 Read, 14 writes) — MORE THAN
EVERY OTHER SUBAGENT IN BOTH ITERATES COMBINED (6 review agents, $21.26 total,
$2-5.50 each).

NOT A PLUMBING BUG — checked: inheritance already works. Of seven Agent spawns in
that session, the two with `model=None` came out Sonnet; the five with
`model='opus'` came out Opus. And no instruction anywhere (`SKILL.md`,
`references/iteration-reviews.md`, `shared/prompts/`) tells the agent to pass a
model at all. It applied "subagent -> Opus" by analogy from the reviewers.

SCOPE — a written rule, not code:
1. Reviewers (`spec-reviewer`, `code-reviewer`, `doubt-reviewer`,
   `opus-plan-reviewer`) pass `model='opus'` explicitly. Measured $2-5.50 each;
   this is good value and stays.
2. A `phase-runner` / finalization handoff passes NO model, so it inherits the
   session model. F0-F12 is the most contract-checked phase (F11 RECOMPUTES
   rather than trusting), and a fresh-context handoff must reload the whole run
   state from disk — paying 5x for that is inverted.
3. State the general rule once: no phase gets its own model without also
   becoming a subagent, and the fresh-context reload cost counts.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE RUN: without the sentence, every future Sonnet
session that hands off finalization pays 5x again and it reads as an unexplained
cost spike. Belongs alongside trg-88621183 (ModelConfig / model tiers), which now
has an empirical basis.

title: Plan review has no internal arm: wire opus-plan-reviewer at medium+, before the external pass
detail:
AUTONOM: ja — die Policy-Entscheidung (Default-on bei medium+) ist getroffen.

VERIFIED 2026-08-07 by full grep over plugins/ (.md + .py): `opus-plan-reviewer`
is referenced by NO file except itself. Its own frontmatter advertises "fallback
when external LLM review is unavailable", but `/shipwright-plan` Step 5's three
branches are: external available -> `external_review.py --mode plan`; no API key
-> interactive retry-or-skip -> Self-Review; user disabled -> Self-Review. The
Self-Review Fallback is a 5-item checklist worked through by THE SAME AGENT THAT
WROTE THE PLAN. So when external review is down, the plan gate degrades to
self-assessment while an independent reviewer sits unused on disk.

THE ASYMMETRY IS ACCIDENTAL: code review has internal (spec -> code -> doubt)
PLUS mandatory external at medium+. Plan review has external only.

THE ARGUMENT IS A CAPABILITY DIFFERENCE, NOT A SECOND OPINION: the internal
reviewer can read the repo; the external providers only see the text they are
sent. Evidence from iterate-2026-08-07-test-phase-attribution, where the Opus
plan review ran ONLY because the operator ordered it, ran FIRST, and found two
BUILD-BLOCKING findings the external pass did not:
  - an attempt-counter collision across the CPU-lease window (the multi-hour
    queueing the iterate exists to measure)
  - `run_test_suite.py` at 518 lines against a cap of 300 — zero headroom, which
    forced a different design
Both are claims AGAINST THE CODE; an external reviewer structurally cannot check
them. The external pass then found two further highs on the revised spec.
Neither pass was redundant. Consistent with the earlier measured finding that the
internal cascade caught 21 items the external review missed (#438).

SCOPE:
1. `opus-plan-reviewer` becomes a default step at medium+, BEFORE the external
   review, spawned with `model='opus'`.
2. It carries the pass when external review is unavailable — replacing the
   self-assessment fallback on that branch.
3. GUARD AGAINST SCOPE RATCHET (observed, not hypothetical): three review rounds
   on that spec produced 12 acceptance criteria, one of them for a configuration
   the spec itself calls unsupported. Every finding must be triaged
   fix / disclose / decline-with-reason, and declining must be legitimate and
   written down.
4. Cost: negligible. Measured internal reviewers ran $2-5.50; a plan is a
   smaller input than a diff.

Unchanged: trivial/small keep the Self-Review Checklist only; the `spec` and
`doubt` roles are still never cascaded to external providers.

title: Decision-drop aggregation is coupled to the release, so the ADR record is ten weeks stale on one untracked disk
detail:
AUTONOM: ja, aber die Kadenz-Wahl (pro Iterate vs. Zeitplan) beim Approval vorlegen.

MEASURED on main 2026-08-07: 202 drops sit in
`.shipwright/agent_docs/decision-drops/`, and `decision_log.md` was last written
2026-07-20 (#415). `aggregate_decisions.py` — the ONE
serialized point that assigns the sequential ADR-NNN — is invoked only from
`/shipwright-changelog` Step 4, so it needs a RELEASE to run. No release since.

CONSEQUENCES:
1. Ten weeks of ADRs in an untracked, unreplicated inbox on a single machine
   (the gitignore is CORRECT and deliberate — drops are Staging, classified so
   in the launch-prep plan — so do NOT revert it; the CADENCE is the bug).
2. The tracked record every agent reads is ten weeks stale, while
   `architecture.md`/`conventions.md` were written the same day.
3. The next release will jump `decision_log.md` from ~333 to ~535 entries /
   ~900 KB in one commit.

SCOPE: decouple aggregation from the release — per iterate, or on a schedule.
Keep the numbering serialized and lock-held exactly as today (that part is
correct and is why numbering lives in one place).

resolvable-on-merge 79 days ago and is still open — likely stale, GC candidate.

title: A truncated mandated context load is never reported, so the governance guarantee voids itself silently as a project grows
detail:
AUTONOM: ja. Klein — ein Check, keine Architektur.

MEASURED 2026-08-07 across four projects: the Layer-1 mandate in
`references/context-loading.md` says to read `decision_log.md` COMPLETELY. It is
obeyed while the file is small and silently abandoned once it is big, because
`Read` caps at 2,000 lines:
  leadwright        23 KB /   450 lines -> read in full   (1 of 1 sessions)
  shipwright       570 KB / 4,379 lines -> fragments      (15 of 194)
  shipwright-webui 641 KB                -> fragments      (6 of 85)
NOTHING REPORTS THE TRANSITION. This is not a cost bug — the two logs are ~0% of
measured cost — it is a correctness bug in the product promise: the governance
guarantee evaporates precisely when a project is mature enough to need it.

SCOPE: detect and report when a mandated load was truncated. Any projection must
declare its coverage, so "I could not fit it all" becomes a reported fact.
`event_context.py query` already does this correctly and is the template.

The dangerous band is ~100-260 KB: still under the line cap, so still fully
read, already 6-13% of a session's context.

title: Persist the conversation-only iterate state so a compaction stops being able to lose work
detail:
AUTONOM: ja.

OBSERVED 2026-08-07, two of two runs: both iterates compacted, one of them DURING
its external review. Compaction is now routine, not hypothetical —
`autoCompactWindow` is set to 400k (raised from 300k precisely because of this),
and a median iterate runs 73k -> 508k.

THE EXPOSURE: interview answers are never persisted, and at complexity `small`
the mini-plan exists only in the conversation. Architecture-review reconciliation
is conversational too. `PreCompact` can only block or observe — IT CANNOT SHAPE
THE SUMMARY — so there is no way to protect that state at compaction time. It has
to be on disk before.

SCOPE:
1. Persist interview answers and the `small`-path mini-plan to disk as they are
   produced.
2. Write review findings to disk (`record_review_pass.py`) as soon as each
   reviewer returns, before continuing — this is what makes a compaction during
   review harmless.
3. Then run the resume-from-disk drill: kill a run mid-phase and prove it
   resumes from artifacts alone.

PREREQUISITE FOR TWO OTHER THINGS: the phase-scoped-contexts work (each phase
must be resumable from disk), and any autonomous/unattended iterate. Also the
reason a finalization handoff is currently expensive — a fresh context has to
reload everything.

title: Windows Tests job takes 25-28 min on double-billed runners with no xdist, while its own config proves 8 workers safe
detail:
AUTONOM: ja.

WHAT IT IS (it is new — landed 2026-08-05 via #571 / IT-9 Unit 5, hence
unfamiliar): `.github/workflows/windows-tests.yml` runs the three `shared/` test
directories on `windows-latest`, because tests gated
`skipif(sys.platform != "win32")` were executed NOWHERE in CI — a Windows-only
defect reached main green and was found only by chance locally. It also removes
the WSL `bash.exe` stub from System32, because the suite itself calls
`subprocess.run(["bash", ...])` and Windows searches System32 before PATH.

MEASURED: 24m39s and 27m45s on 2026-08-07, on Windows runners (2x billing
multiplier), twice per PR. It is NOT a required check — the six are Analyze
(python), Python (lint + test), Shipwright Security Scan, Analyze
(javascript-typescript), Anti-ratchet + allowlist diff, PR Review — so it blocks
no merges. This is Actions minutes and signal latency, not a gate.

SCOPE (both cheap):
1. The job runs plain pytest with NO xdist, while `shipwright_test_config.json`
   records `shared/tests: 8` workers as proven safe. Mirror THE ALLOWLIST — never
   a global `-n auto`, which that config forbids in writing after a 17-failure
   regression from nesting xdist under outer fleet load. `windows-latest` has 4
   cores, so size the worker count to the runner.
2. It provisions the environment three times via `uv run --with ...`, once per
   directory. Provision once.

DO NOT narrow it to the 11 platform-gated lines in 8 files: it runs 7,834 test
functions and has already found two genuine Windows bugs no gate marked
(`trg-e82d8771`, `trg-d0f585b2`). The breadth is earning its keep; only the
duration needs work.

title: Reviewer/agent model config: add a plan-reviewer role, any model, chosen by the consuming project
detail:
AUTONOMOUS: yes.

Extends trg-88621183 (ModelConfig / per-run model-tier flags) rather than
standing alone — the two describe one rule set and should be built together.

WHY A PLAN-REVIEWER ROLE IS MISSING AT ALL. Verified 2026-08-07 by a full grep
over plugins/ (.md + .py): `opus-plan-reviewer` is referenced by NO file except
itself. Its own frontmatter advertises "fallback when external LLM review is
unavailable", but `/shipwright-plan` Step 5's three branches are: external
available -> `external_review.py --mode plan`; no API key -> interactive
retry-or-skip -> Self-Review; user disabled -> Self-Review. The Self-Review
Fallback is a 5-item checklist worked through by THE SAME AGENT THAT WROTE THE
PLAN. So when external review is unavailable, the plan gate degrades to
self-assessment while an independent reviewer sits unused on disk. Code review
has both an internal cascade and a mandatory external pass at medium+; plan
review has external only. Nothing designed that asymmetry.

WHY THE INTERNAL ARM IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF THE EXTERNAL ONE — it is a capability
difference, not a second opinion: the internal reviewer can read the repo, the
external providers only see the text they are sent. Measured in
iterate-2026-08-07-test-phase-attribution, where the internal plan review ran
only because the operator ordered it, ran FIRST, and found two BUILD-BLOCKING
findings the external pass did not:
  - an attempt-counter collision across the CPU-lease window (the multi-hour
    queueing that iterate exists to measure)
  - `run_test_suite.py` at 518 lines against a cap of 300 — zero headroom, which
    forced a different design
Both are claims AGAINST THE CODE, which an external reviewer structurally cannot
check. The external pass then found two further highs on the revised spec.
Neither was redundant — consistent with the earlier measured result that the
internal cascade caught 21 items the external review missed (#438).

SCOPE — configurability is the point, not the default:
1. Declare a `plan_reviewer` ROLE alongside the existing reviewer roles, wired
   into the medium+ path before the external pass, and carrying the pass when
   external review is unavailable.
2. Every role takes a model from configuration. ANY model — the mechanism must
   not know or care which. `inherit` (take the session model) must be a legal
   value and should be what an unconfigured project gets.
3. SHIPWRIGHT MUST NOT PRESCRIBE A TIER. A shipped default that pins a role to
   an expensive model raises a consuming project's bill without their consent;
   pinning it to a cheap one silently lowers their review quality. Either
   direction takes away a choice that is theirs. We record OUR choice in OUR
   config, as one worked example.
4. Fix the invisibility instead: a project must be able to see which model each
   role actually used, and what it cost. That is the honest lever — the
   context-cost meter already carries the per-call model.
5. GUARD AGAINST SCOPE RATCHET (observed, not hypothetical): three review rounds
   on that one spec produced 12 acceptance criteria, one of them covering a
   configuration the spec itself calls unsupported. Every finding must be triaged
   fix / disclose / decline-with-reason, and declining must be legitimate and
   recorded.

Cost context for the worked example: measured internal reviewers ran $2-5.50 per
pass; a plan is a smaller input than a diff. Trivial/small complexity keeps the
Self-Review Checklist only and needs no role resolution at all.

title: Track the decision-drops folder instead of decoupling aggregation, and have Layer-1 context read the drops
detail:
AUTONOMOUS: yes.

SUPERSEDES an earlier framing of this card that proposed decoupling
`aggregate_decisions.py` from the release. That is the wrong fix: aggregation
lives in `/shipwright-changelog` Step 4 precisely because it is the ONE
serialized, lock-held point that assigns the sequential `ADR-NNN`. Moving it
would bring the numbering race back. Aggregation stays where it is.

THE ACTUAL PROBLEM. Measured on main 2026-08-07: 202 drops sit in
`.shipwright/agent_docs/decision-drops/`, and `decision_log.md` was last written
2026-07-20 (#415) — no release since. The folder is gitignored (`.gitignore:172`)
on the premise that drops are transient staging. That premise held while releases
were frequent. It no longer does: the folder now holds ten weeks of architectural
decisions that exist on exactly one machine, are absent from CI, absent from any
second checkout, and would be lost with the disk. Meanwhile the tracked record
every agent reads is ten weeks stale, and the next release will move
`decision_log.md` from ~333 to ~535 entries in a single commit.

SCOPE:
1. Stop gitignoring `.shipwright/agent_docs/decision-drops/`. There is no reason
   not to sync a durable record of decisions. Aggregation still consumes and
   deletes them at release exactly as today — tracked-then-deleted is a normal
   lifecycle, and git history keeps what was removed.
2. Apply the same change to the shipwright-webui repo, which has the same
   gitignore rule and the same exposure.
3. Layer-1 context loading then reads the drops as well as `decision_log.md` —
   today it reads neither the drops (they were invisible) nor, in practice, the
   full log. Without this step, tracking the folder fixes durability but not the
   ten-week blind spot in what agents actually see.
4. Check the drop-dir consumers still resolve against the MAIN repo root, not a
   worktree (`test_decision_drop_ssot.py` already guards this in both
   directions); tracking the folder changes what `git worktree remove` and
   `git add -A` will now sweep, so re-verify those two paths.

NOTE: this deliberately reverses the earlier "the gitignore is correct, do not
revert" decision from the launch-prep plan. The reason it is being reversed is
that its premise — drops are short-lived — is measurably false at the current
release cadence, and the alternative fix (aggregating more often) would cost the
serialized numbering. Operator decision, 2026-08-07.

Also: `trg-e21cc409` (drops lost on worktree cleanup) was marked
resolvable-on-merge 79 days ago and is still open — likely stale, GC candidate.

title: A truncated mandated context load is never reported, so the governance guarantee voids itself silently as a project grows
detail:
AUTONOMOUS: yes. Small — a check, not an architecture.

WHAT "MANDATED LOAD" MEANS: `references/context-loading.md` instructs an iterate
to read certain artifacts COMPLETELY at startup — Layer 1 includes
"`decision_log.md` — ALL architectural decisions (read completely)". That is a
governance promise: the agent is supposed to know every prior decision before
changing anything.

WHY IT SILENTLY STOPS BEING TRUE: `Read` returns at most 2,000 lines.
`decision_log.md` is 4,379 lines. So the agent is told to read the whole file,
receives roughly half, and NOTHING REPORTS THE SHORTFALL — it just proceeds,
usually falling back to greps. Measured across four projects 2026-08-07:
  leadwright        23 KB /   450 lines -> read in full   (1 of 1 sessions)
  shipwright       570 KB / 4,379 lines -> fragments      (15 of 194)
  shipwright-webui 641 KB                -> fragments      (6 of 85)
The guarantee holds while a project is small and evaporates exactly when the
project is mature enough to need it.

THIS IS NOT A COST FIX. The two big logs are ~0% of measured token cost; the
earlier claim that they drive it is falsified. This card is about correctness of
the product promise.

SCOPE: when a mandated load is truncated, say so — name the artifact, how much
arrived, how much exists, and that the instruction was not fulfilled. More
generally, any projection must DECLARE ITS COVERAGE so "I could not fit it all"
becomes a reported fact rather than a silent one. `event_context.py query`
already does this correctly and is the template.

The dangerous band is ~100-260 KB: still under the line cap, so still read in
full, already 6-13% of a session's context.

`supersedes` 4%, and `extraction.confidence: "low"` on 630 of 815. THERE IS
NOTHING TO RANK. Any relevance ordering built on this today is fiction.

CHECKED KEY BY KEY 2026-08-07 — three of five fall out of git exactly, two do
not, and an earlier version of this card wrongly promised all of them:
  - `commit`         -> git, trivially.
  - `changed_files`  -> git, trivially.
  - `area_ids`       -> YES, derivable. All 28 entries in
    `.shipwright/agent_docs/area_catalog.json` are `source: "deterministic"` and
    every one carries `path_patterns` (e.g. `CHANGELOG-unreleased.d/**`). Match
    a commit's changed files against those patterns and the area ids follow as a
    pure function of git. No LLM extraction.
  - `affected_frs`   -> NO. 0 of 28 areas populate their `requirements` field, so
    there is no area->requirement bridge to ride, and nothing else in git names
    an FR. This needs an `FR:` commit trailer GOING FORWARD; historical entries
    cannot be back-filled and must be DECLARED EMPTY rather than reported as
    zero, or a consumer will read "no FRs affected" as a finding.
  - `supersedes`     -> NO. Needs an explicit declaration, or derivation from the
    ADR link graph (the RFC-index pattern — see the ADR-index card).

SCOPE:
1. Backfill `commit`, `changed_files` and `area_ids` from git for all 815
   entries. Deterministic, re-runnable, no model involved.
2. Add `ADR:` / `Area:` / `FR:` commit trailers so the keys stay filled, and
   make the area value derived-and-verified against the catalogue rather than
   hand-typed.
3. Record per-entry which keys are DERIVED, which are DECLARED, and which are
   UNAVAILABLE — a per-row flag cannot report an absent row, so coverage belongs
   in the envelope, not only per entry.

This is the precondition for the ADR-index card: nothing can be ranked by
relevance until the keys exist.

title: Persist the iterate state that currently exists only in the conversation, so a compaction cannot lose work
detail:
AUTONOMOUS: yes.

OBSERVED 2026-08-07, two of two runs: both iterates compacted, one of them DURING
its external review. Compaction is routine now, not hypothetical —
`autoCompactWindow` is 400k (raised from 300k for exactly this reason) and a
median iterate runs 73k -> 508k of context.

WHAT IS AT RISK — the state that has no disk representation today:
  1. Interview answers. The `[interview]` step's questions and answers are never
     written anywhere; they exist only as conversation.
  2. The mini-plan at complexity `small`. At `small` there is no plan file — the
     plan is agreed in conversation and built from memory.
  3. Architecture-review reconciliation. What the review found and what was
     decided about it is conversational; only the outcome eventually shows up in
     a diff.
  4. Review findings between a reviewer returning and `record_review_pass.py`
     being called. This is the window the observed compaction landed in.
  5. The handoff decision itself. When to hand off to a fresh context is a
     heuristic, not a contract, so the receiving agent cannot know what the
     sending one had.
  6. Resume coverage: B1 checks only two markers, so a mid-phase resume cannot
     tell how far the phase actually got.

WHY IT CANNOT BE SOLVED AT COMPACTION TIME: `PreCompact` can only block or
observe — IT CANNOT SHAPE THE SUMMARY. There is no hook that protects a specific
piece of conversation. The state has to be on disk BEFORE the window opens.

SCOPE:
1. Persist (1) and (2) as they are produced.
2. Write review findings to disk as soon as each reviewer returns, before any
   further work — this alone makes a compaction during review harmless.
3. Then run the acceptance test: kill a run mid-phase and prove it resumes from
   artifacts alone, with no conversational memory.

PREREQUISITE FOR: phase-scoped contexts (each phase must be resumable from disk
before it can be moved into its own context), and any unattended iterate. It is
also why a finalization handoff is currently expensive — the fresh context has to
reload everything from scratch.

blocks no merges. This is Actions minutes and signal latency, not a gate.

functions and has already found two genuine Windows bugs that no gate marked

duration needs work.

title: opus-plan-reviewer is invoked by nothing, so the plan gate falls back to self-assessment
detail:
AUTONOMOUS: yes. Wiring only — model tiering is trg-88621183's job, not this card's.

Narrowed from an earlier version that also restated the model-config design.
trg-88621183 already owns that: it lists `opus-plan-reviewer` under the `review`
role, sets the precedence (flag > project config > unset), and its REJECTED
section already carries the consumer-freedom argument against pinning a tier.
This card is the separate defect underneath it: **a role in the registry that no
skill calls.** Tiering an agent that is never spawned changes nothing.

VERIFIED 2026-08-07 by a full grep over plugins/ (.md and .py, worktrees
excluded): `opus-plan-reviewer` is referenced by NO file except itself. Its own
frontmatter advertises "fallback when external LLM review is unavailable", but
`/shipwright-plan` Step 5 has three branches and none reach it:
  - external available  -> `external_review.py --mode plan`
  - no API key          -> interactive retry-or-skip -> Self-Review Fallback
  - user disabled       -> Self-Review Fallback
The Self-Review Fallback is a 5-item checklist ("2x denken") worked through by
THE SAME AGENT THAT WROTE THE PLAN. So when external review is unavailable, the
plan gate degrades to self-assessment.

THE ASYMMETRY: code review at medium+ has an internal cascade
(spec -> code -> doubt) PLUS a mandatory external pass. Plan review has external
only. Nothing designed that.

WHY AN INTERNAL ARM IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF THE EXTERNAL ONE — capability, not
opinion: the internal reviewer can read the repo; the external providers only see
the text they are sent. Measured in iterate-2026-08-07-test-phase-attribution,
where the internal plan review ran only because the operator ordered it, ran
FIRST, and found two BUILD-BLOCKING findings the external pass did not:
  - an attempt-counter collision across the CPU-lease window (the multi-hour
    queueing that iterate exists to measure)
  - `run_test_suite.py` at 518 lines against a cap of 300 (zero headroom), which
    forced a different design
Both are claims AGAINST THE CODE, which an external reviewer structurally cannot
check. The external pass then found two further highs on the revised spec.
Neither was redundant — consistent with the measured result that the internal
cascade caught 21 items external review missed (#438).

SCOPE:
1. Wire the plan-reviewer into `/shipwright-plan` Step 5 at medium+, before the
   external pass, and let it carry the pass on the two branches where external
   review is unavailable — replacing self-assessment there.
2. Resolve its model through trg-88621183's mechanism. Do NOT pin a tier here.

   calls unsupported. Every finding gets triaged fix / disclose /
   decline-with-reason, and declining must be legitimate and recorded.

Trivial/small keep the Self-Review Checklist only and need no reviewer at all.
Cost context: measured internal reviewers ran $2-5.50 per pass; a plan is a
smaller input than a diff.
